items.title: Humans predictively process high-level information during active natural vision
items.summary: Prediction is considered a fundamental principle of perception. However, evidence for predictive visual processing comes largely from paradigms that establish explicit predictive relationships, leaving unclear whether the brain spontaneously generates feature-level predictions during natural viewing. We analyzed magnetoencephalography data recorded concurrently with eye movements as participants freely explored thousands of natural scenes. Using linear deconvolution to disentangle overlapping neural responses, we demonstrate that high-level conceptual information derived from artificial neural networks is reflected in neural activity approximately 50-100 ms before fixation onset, whereas low-level perceptual information emerges only after fixation onset. Source analyses localized these predictive high-level signals to higher-order cortical regions.…

items.title: A dynamical mechanism for opposing cortical gradients in resting-state functional and stimulation-derived effective connectomes
items.summary: Resting-state functional connectivity (FC) and stimulation-derived effective connectivity (EC) offer complementary views of cortical interactions, yet how cortical dynamics shape their relationship within a shared anatomical network remains unclear. Using group-level resting-state fMRI and intracranial electrical stimulation data from large-scale human cohorts, we find that regional mean response to electrical stimulation is negatively correlated with its mean FC (r = -0.568), with the two measures exhibiting opposing trends along the cortical hi-erarchy. To account for this divergence, we develop a differentiable whole-cortex mean-field model with independently trainable regional parameters, fitted to EC and FC through two-stage EC-FC training using gradient-based optimization.…

items.title: A Reproducible, Leakage-Aware Machine Learning Pipeline for Antimicrobial Peptide Activity Prediction
items.summary: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are key alternatives to conventional antibiotics, but published machine learning models may overestimate predictive performance because of positive-class sequence redundancy and data leakage. We developed a leakage-aware pipeline using 13,469 peptides from DRAMP v5.0 and UniProt, clustered at 40% sequence identity with CD-HIT to enforce cluster-level splitting. A Random Forest trained on sequence and physicochemical features achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.939 and a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.671 on a cluster-disjoint test set (mean AUC-ROC 0.923 {+/-} 0.012 across 20 repeated cluster-disjoint splits, versus 0.945 {+/-} 0.004 under random splitting).…

items.title: DASTevolve: Evolving executable protein-design programs with large language models
items.summary: Protein engineering often requires improving one property while preserving others across multiple regions or molecular states. An aggregate score can reveal a poor design yet offer little guidance about which decision to revise. We introduce DASTevolve, which represents a design task as two linked abstract syntax trees. The functional tree specifies objectives and state relationships, and its links to the structural tree identify where edits are permitted for each objective. A large language model (LLM), as inspired by the recent works on coding agents, proposes program revisions from evaluation feedback, and a sequence optimizer searches within the compiled constraints.…

items.title: Recovering Missing Regulations by Multiplex Graph Aggregation of GRN Predictions (Technical Report)
items.summary: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) capture the complex gene interactions underlying biological systems. However, existing GRN inference models face technical challenges in recovering faithful GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing data in an unsupervised setting. GRN aggregation has been proposed to leverage the wisdom of different GRN models and improve overall performance, but aggregation methods either train on ground-truth edges, overlook the network nature of GRNs, or are computationally expensive. To bridge this gap, we propose MuxGRN, a novel GRN aggregation method that leverages multiplex link prediction to aggregate GRNs inferred from various state-of-the-art models and extract the information propagated within different layers of GRNs.…

items.title: TW-GMProt: Trust-Weighted Semi-Supervised Gated Modulation Protein Language Model for Antimicrobial Peptide Activity Prediction
items.summary: Antibiotic resistance poses a major global health threat, underscoring the need for faster approaches to antimicrobial discovery. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising therapeutic candidates, but experimental activity screening remains costly and time-consuming. We introduce TW-GMProt, a trust-weighted semi-supervised gated modulation protein language model for quantitative AMP activity prediction. It integrates pretrained protein language model representations with convolutional neural networks through a gated modulation strategy, complemented by biophysical priors. To address the scarcity of experimental data, the framework further employs trust-weighted semi-supervised learning to leverage a large collection of unlabeled antimicrobial peptides through pseudo-labeling.…

items.title: BioGCD: A Biology-Guided Multimodal Framework for Compound and Combination Discovery
items.summary: Phenotype-based transcriptomic screening provides a powerful approach for therapeutic discovery by capturing how compounds reshape cellular states. However, existing perturbation models lack biological constraints, limiting generalizability, mechanistic interpretability, and the ability to prioritize experimentally validated candidates. Here, we developed BioGCD, a biological knowledge-guided multimodal framework that integrates four gene-level prior graphs and a compound-aware pathway-level prior with cellular states, molecular structures and dosage information to learn biologically informed perturbation patterns. BioGCD outperformed existing models in predicting compound induced transcriptomic responses across diverse cellular contexts, achieving a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.912 between predicted and observed responses.…

items.title: Conditional Dirichlet Flow Matching for exploring the sequence space of protein families
items.summary: Protein folds have evolved to support a diverse range of functions, and repurposing an existing fold can offer a more effective route to engineering new functions than designing a scaffold de novo. Here, we introduce Syzygy, a generative model that learns the evolutionary sequence patterns of protein families to generate artificial homologues that diverge from natural sequences while preserving family-specific characteristics. Based on Dirichlet flow matching, Syzygy is trained on a single multiple sequence alignment and enables sequence generation conditioned on protein length, a discrete functional label, or both. The model is computationally efficient, with average training times of under 10 minutes on a single GPU and generation of 1,000 sequences in approximately 30 seconds.…

items.title: Enzymado: Are Protein Language Models Getting Better at Enzyme Tasks?
items.summary: Protein language model (PLM) embeddings are a common representation for enzyme engineering tasks. PLMs are pretrained using vast protein data, and while enzymes are proteins, they are distinguished by their catalytic nature, which is dependent on substrates and reaction mechanisms. Current PLM evaluations test isolated properties with incompatible data, splits, and metrics, leaving open how PLMs can better serve enzymes and what drives their performance. We present Enzymado, a framework for evaluating enzyme representations, with property datasets curated from public databases and experimental protein engineering studies, spanning kinetics, mutation effects, function, binding, solubility, and residue annotations. Enzymado standardizes data cleaning, evaluation splits, prediction heads, and metrics throughout the comparison of 14 PLMs.…

items.title: A data engine for AI-assisted labeling of high-density sperm microscopy videos
items.summary: Computer-aided semen analysis (CASA) systems are the standard tools for quantifying sperm motility, concentration, and morphology, but they rely on classical algorithms that struggle with overlapping cells, collisions, and the imaging artifacts that accumulate in long, high-density recordings. As a result, analyses are typically restricted to short videos of diluted samples. AI-based trackers could overcome these limitations, but they require large, accurately labeled training datasets, and manually labeling crowded sperm videos is prohibitively slow. Here we present a data engine for sperm tracking, where an AI model can be trained from low-density data to assist in labeling higher-density cases. We first obtain ground-truth trajectories from easy-to-label, low-density videos using a classical tracker (Trackpy) followed by human correction.…

items.title: Simultaneous Optimization of Codon Adaptation and Thermodynamic Stability in mRNA Therapeutics via Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Motivation. The efficacy of mRNA vaccines depends on translational efficiency and molecule stability, commonly captured by the codon adaptation index (CAI) and minimum free energy (MFE), respectively. These objectives are in tension, and codon degeneracy makes their simultaneous optimization in large RNA constructs encoding multiples peptides a combinatorial search problem intractable through brute-force computation. Methods. We present ReinforSeqPipe, a Deep Q-Network reinforcement learning pipeline coupling a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) sequence encoder with the bi-parametric MFECAI{lambda} objective as its reward function. Adapted from LinearDesign, MFECAI{lambda} is a weighted objective function of MFE- and CAI-centred subfunctions.…

items.title: Lung tissue organization shapes influenza spread and immune control
items.summary: Type I interferon (IFN) is a central defense against influenza A virus, yet its effectiveness depends on lung tissue organization, often simplified in mechanistic models. We investigated four IFN mechanisms--blocking infection, inducing a refractory state, suppressing virion production, and amplifying IFN production--using a homogeneous reaction-diffusion model and a spatial agent-based model reconstructed from murine lung histology. The latter represented approximately 233,000 detected cells in a single section or 4.1 million across a reconstructed volume. Models were calibrated against PR8 viral titers and IFN-{beta} measurements, with spatial models additionally constrained by day-2 lesion extent. In the homogeneous model, bulk kinetics could not distinguish IFN mechanisms, and tissue sparing arose from widespread refractory conversion rather than spatial containment.…

items.title: Understanding robustness and enabling remediation of neuroimaging-based deep neural networks for digital security: Semantic segmentation of brain tumors as illustrative study
items.summary: BackgroundApplications of deep learning models in neuroimaging have significantly advanced translational neuroscience, offering substantial benefits to human health. However, recent cybersecurity threats have undermined the reliability of digital neuroscience tools, posing challenges to the clinical neuroscience community. A critical issue is the automated semantic segmentation of malignant or premalignant brain tumors, essential for neurosurgery and radiotherapy planning. New methodsThis study investigates the robustness of customary deep learning models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and more recent Vision Transformers (ViTs) in semantic segmentation against adversarial attacks. We assess the performance of CNNs and ViTs under ideal nonhostile conditions and then under cybersecurity threats.…

items.title: A Deep Learning Model for Quantifying and Mapping Human Spiral Ganglion Neurons (SGNs): The SGN Base Model
items.summary: IntroductionSpiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) transmit auditory information and are a histological marker that have been quantified for decades to study various hearing loss pathologies in human temporal bone (hTB) specimens. Historically, quantification of SGNs has been labor-intensive and subject to manual bias and error. With the advent of digital microscopy, this study introduces and assesses the accuracy of a deep learning model for SGN quantification, providing an efficient approach that enables in-depth analysis of SGN distribution through three-dimensional frequency mapping. MethodsDigitized mid-modiolar slides from six hTBs from the Mass Eye and Ear Otopathology Laboratory Collection, representing a range of ages, post-mortem times, and diagnoses, were selected to train a computer vision model.…

items.title: Cross-Stream Self-Supervised Learning Inspired by Feature-Biased Visual Processing in the Brain
items.summary: Humans and other animals develop rich visual representations without explicit object-category labels. Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a computational framework for studying how such representations emerge from visual experience. Many contrastive SSL models, such as SimCLR, learn by being robust to augmented views of the same image, which may fail to preserve visual attributes such as color and orientation. Inspired by feature-specific visual processing streams in the brain, we propose BioCLR, an SSL framework that uses color- and orientation-biased networks to guide representation learning. We combine Bio-CLR with SimCLR into a BioCLR hybrid model, pretrain it on ImageNet-100, and evaluate it on this dataset and four transfer datasets.…

items.title: Nanoscale spatial-omics via contrastive embedding of single-molecule localisation data
items.summary: Omics approaches have transformed biology by characterising cells at the genomic, transcriptomic and proteomic levels. An additional layer of cellular information is provided by the nanoscale spatial organisation of molecules, which can be measured using super-resolution microscopy. We present a self-supervised contrastive learning framework that embeds single-molecule localisation microscopy (SMLM) point patterns into a learned representation of nanoscale organisation. Across simulated and experimental data, the representation distinguishes diverse spatial architectures, captures graded changes in organisation and supports unsupervised comparison of experimental conditions. The framework distinguishes proteins with different nanoscale distributions and captures variation associated with cell type and pharmacological perturbation.…

items.title: Predictive coding networks capture human neural representations missing in supervised DNNs
items.summary: Neuroscientific learning theories propose that the brain acquires knowledge by constructing internal world models. Supervised learning, the dominant approach in deep neural networks (DNN), relies on external category labels, making it difficult to reconcile with biological learning. There is an increasing trend towards more biologically valid approaches, such as predictive (minimize future surprise) or contrastive (minimize response to expected, maximize to unexpected inputs) objectives, but these approaches typically rely on pretrained DNN models that vary widely in architecture, size, and hyperparameters, making direct comparisons difficult. Here, we isolate the effect of learning by comparing small, identical networks trained with predictive, contrastive, and supervised learning objectives, as well as local (layer-restricted) vs. global (full backpropagation) learning.…

items.title: Accurate and Interpretable Prediction of Antidepressant Treatment Response from Receptor-informed Neuroimaging
items.summary: Conventional antidepressants show moderate efficacy in treating major depressive disorder. Psychedelic-assisted therapy holds promise, yet individual responses vary, underscoring the need for predictive tools to guide treatment selection. Here, we present graphTRIP (graph-based Treatment Response Interpretability and Prediction) -- a geometric deep learning architecture that enables three advances: 1) accurate prediction of post-treatment depression severity using only pretreatment clinical and neuroimaging data; 2) identification of interpretable biomarkers; and 3) causal analysis of treatment effects and underlying mechanisms. Trained on data from a clinical trial comparing psilocybin and escitalopram (NCT03429075), graphTRIP achieves strong predictive accuracy (r = 0.72, p < 0.01) and generalises across brain atlases.…

items.title: Sequential predictive learning is a unifying theory for hippocampal representation and replay
items.summary: The hippocampus represents an animal's position in the environment and generates "replay" proposed to support recall, planning, and memory formation. Recently, it's been found that artificial neural networks trained to predict sensory inputs develop spatially-tuned cells, however, whether predictive learning can account for the ability to produce replay, or the hippocampus' representation of non-spatial variables, is unknown. Here, we find that offline replay only emerged in recurrent neural networks that used head-direction information to predict multi-step observation sequences, which promoted the formation of a continuous attractor reflecting the geometry of the environment. These offline trajectories were able to autonomously replay recently experienced locations, generate novel paths, and could be directed by a virtual head direction signal.…

items.title: A signature of deep credit assignment in the human Orbitofrontal cortex
items.summary: Humans are remarkably efficient at learning from limited experience because they can generalize quickly. Doing so, however, requires first learning about the latent structures that govern outcomes. The dominant theoretical framework to understand this interactive cycle between learning task representations and generalisation is deep learning, which updates parameters throughout multi-layered neural networks using deep credit assignment. Yet, whether the brain uses a similar "deep" approach to learning is unclear. Here, we derive and test a prediction that uniquely characterizes deep credit assignment, namely, that a single learning experience should trigger immediate, structured representation changes that are non-local (i.e. generalize beyond the observed experience), and adapt as learning proceeds.…

items.title: Dopamine shifts striatal ramping dynamics
items.summary: Diseases that disrupt dopamine impair cognition; however, it is unknown how dopamine affects neuronal networks that instantiate cognitive processing. We studied this problem in the dorsomedial striatum during interval timing, an elementary cognitive task requiring working memory and attention to estimate an interval of several seconds. Interval timing requires medium spiny neurons (MSNs) that ramp up or down over temporal intervals. While these neurons receive prominent dopaminergic input from the substantia nigra, it is unknown how dopamine modulates MSN activity during interval timing. Here, we report four new findings. First, ramping activity of MSN ensembles predicts interval timing behavior.…

items.title: DualBranchEEG: A Dual-Branch CNN BiLSTM Network with Temporal Attention and Spectral Features for Three Class EEG Seizure Classification
items.summary: Automated seizure detection from electroencephalography (EEG) is a key step toward closed-loop brain-computer interface (BCI) systems and clinical decision support. We present DualBranchEEG, a dual-branch network that fuses (i) a temporal branch--a three-block 1-D convolutional encoder, a two-layer bidirectional LSTM and an additive attention layer--operating on the raw z-scored waveform, with (ii) a spectral branch--an MLP on log-power spectral density (PSD) features from Welch's method. We evaluate three-class classification (normal, interictal, ictal) on the Bonn University EEG dataset (500 single-channel recordings, 173.61 Hz) using a single stratified 70/15/15 split (seed 42). We position this work as a transparent reference implementation and exploratory comparison, not as evidence of superiority.…

items.title: Conditional feature importance with error control for machine-learning-based biomarker discovery in Alzheimer's disease
items.summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by complex biology captured by proteomics, transcriptomics, genetics, and brain imaging. These high-dimensional and correlated data make biomarker discovery challenging. To disentangle biomedical AD data, we propose Conditional Feature Importance (CFI), a theory-grounded framework quantifying the unique contribution of individual or grouped variables in any machine learning model while controlling false discoveries. Across ADNI, BioFINDER, and UK Biobank (nearly 48,000 participants), CFI uncovered a striking contrast between unique versus redundant biomarkers across protein and imaging signatures of AD diagnosis, onset, and progression. Age and neurofilament light chain (NfL) were important for all three outcomes, and A{beta}42 was common to diagnosis and progression.…
authors: for the Swedish BioFINDER study group,

items.title: Ongoing activity in anatomically recurrent cortex is predominantly feedforward
items.summary: The cerebral cortex is the major site of computation in the brain, and its recurrent wiring has motivated models in which repeated neuronal activation maintains information in stable attractor states. Large language models illustrate an alternative principle by transforming information layer by layer during each forward pass. A first step toward understanding what cortex and these models can teach us about each other is to establish whether feedforward dynamics can predominate in recurrent cortex. Here, we show that ongoing activity in the frontal cortex of awake mice is composed of parabolic neuronal avalanches in which activity progresses mainly through newly recruited neurons.…

items.title: A Spatiotemporal Code for Cognitive Flexibility in the Mid-Posterior Cerebellar Cortex
items.summary: Cognitive flexibility is the critical ability to adapt behavior in changing environments. Although traditionally associated with the prefrontal cortex, behavioral, lesion, and functional imaging evidence suggests the cerebellum contributes to cognitive flexibility. To test the role of the cerebellum at the circuit level, we paired widefield calcium imaging of single-cell Purkinje cells with a cognitive flexibility task and computational behavioral model. We find mid-posterior Purkinje cells encode all reinforcement learning parameters needed to produce flexible behavior, including specific representations for contingency degradation (CD) and enhancement (CE). Comparing somatic and dendritic encoding reveals a significant bias towards integrative multi-trial CD and CE representations in somas over long timescales, while dendrites encode more single-trial reward prediction errors.…

items.title: Network size regulates the balance between reuse and reconstruction of neural dynamics during reversal learning
items.summary: Neural system size is a fundamental quantitative property that may influence cognitive function. While larger neural systems have been associated with enhanced cognitive performance, how system size contributes to cognitive flexibility remains poorly understood. In particular, it is unclear whether size influences not only how efficiently a system learns but also how previously established neural dynamics are reorganized when learned associations must change. We addressed this question using recurrent neural networks trained on a reversal learning task. Despite reaching the same performance criterion, networks differed strikingly in how their internal dynamics changed across reversal.…

items.title: Modeling Speech-in-Noise Performance Using an Auditory-Nerve Manifold
items.summary: Speech-in-noise difficulties often exceed audiometric profile-based predictions, suggesting suprathreshold neural coding deficits limit understanding even when audibility is preserved. A major limitation of clinical speech tests is that reduced performance can reflect either hair-cell loss or cochlear neural degeneration (CND). We propose a computational framework estimating each factor relative contribution at a population level. We simulated auditory-nerve responses to a consonant-identification task for 94 adults (19-83 years; pure-tone average (PTA) 0-55 dB HL) under three conditions: audiometric loss alone, CND affecting low- and medium-spontaneous-rate (LS and MS) fibers, and CND affecting all fiber types.…

items.title: Single-molecule motion profiling reveals direct and indirect effects of PolyQ expansion on huntingtin dynamics and molecular engagement
items.summary: Huntingtons disease (HD) is caused by CAG expansion in HTT, but how PolyQ expansion alters huntingtin behaviour in human neurons remains unclear. We combined live single-molecule imaging and tracking with transformer-based motion profiling to resolve full-length HTT dynamics in pluripotent hESCs and their derived cortical- and MSN-like neurons. HTT occupied three behavioural states: bound, confined, and exploratory. PolyQ expansion progressively shifted molecules from bound and confined states toward the exploratory state. These effects emerged at shorter PolyQ lengths in MSN-like neurons, and only at 150Q included faster exploratory diffusion and impaired return to stable bound or confined states. Tag-swap experiments showed that mt- HTT imposed similar defects on co-expressed wild-type HTT (wt-HTT), revealing a dominant effect of the HD mutation on wt-HTT dynamics.…

items.title: Promise and Limits of Hierarchical Dynamical RNNs for Individualized Resting-State fMRI
items.summary: Modeling individual brain dynamics from resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) remains challenging due to substantial inter-subject variability, noise, and limited data length per subject. Here, we systematically evaluate whether hierarchical shallow piecewise-linear recurrent neural networks (shPLRNNs), recently introduced as interpretable dynamical system reconstruction models, can generate individualized rs-fMRI time series while preserving subject-specific functional connectivity structure. We applied the framework to 1,423 rs-fMRI samples from healthy participants of the Marburg-Muenster Affective Disorders Cohort Study (MACS). Simulated rs-fMRI data reproduced substantial empirical FC structure, with comparable reconstruction accuracy on the validation and held-out test sets.…

items.title: Predicting the synaptic partners of masked neurons across two female Drosophila connectomes with per-region graph models
items.summary: Whole-brain connectomes of adult Drosophila now exist for several individuals, so one can ask how accurately a neurons synaptic partners can be imputed in one animal by models trained on another. We trained a separate graph neural network for each of twelve brain regions on the FlyWire female brain and tested whether it could recover the connections of masked neurons in a second female brain reconstructed by a different pipeline (BANC). Every edge of a masked neuron was hidden, but the neuron kept features computed from its complete reconstruction (neuropil innervation, synapse-position features and total in-region synapse count) together with its cell type, transmitter and class labels. Each true partner was ranked against 100 non-partners drawn in proportion to their visible degree, and performance was measured by mean reciprocal rank (MRR).…

items.title: GinsengMind: An evidence-grounded AI research agent for integrative molecular research in Panax ginseng
items.summary: Panax ginseng C. A. Meyer is one of the most extensively studied medicinal plants, with substantial pharmaceutical and economic importance owing to its diverse bioactive constituents, particularly ginsenosides. Despite considerable advances in ginseng molecular research, the fragmentation of genomic, transcriptomic, protein structural, and biochemical information remains a major challenge for investigating gene function and specialized metabolism. Here, we developed GinsengMind (https://ginsengai.nrc.ac.cn), an evidence-grounded AI research agent that integrates species-specific molecular knowledge with large language model (LLM)-guided tool orchestration and structured retrieval-augmented generation. Built upon the telomere-to-telomere reference genome of P. ginseng, GinsengMind integrates 77,266 genes, 154,754 transcripts, and 77,266 protein records.…

items.title: Learning Protein Structure Representations through Joint-Embedding Prediction
items.summary: Motivation: Protein structure representations are often learned by reconstructing coordinates, yet reconstruction quality does not necessarily track performance on biological prediction tasks. We therefore investigate whether joint-embedding prediction can capture information useful for biological prediction while retaining recoverable backbone geometry. Results: We introduce PS-JEPA, a self-supervised model that learns protein structure representations by predicting masked residue embeddings from visible backbone context. The encoder combines geometric graph encoding with bidirectional Mamba and is pretrained without a coordinate-reconstruction objective.…

items.title: GRACE: Discrete Biological Sequence Optimization with Gradient-Resolved Adaptive Constrained Exploration
items.summary: Machine learning increasingly enables biological sequence redesign for therapeutic and biotechnological applications by optimizing sequences for desired properties. However, improving one property can compromise another: for example, increasing enzyme activity may reduce stability, while enhancing regulatory DNA activity may diminish cell-type specificity. We formulate sequence redesign as a constrained optimization problem guided by learned predictive models, where a reference sequence is mutated to improve a predicted target property while keeping predicted auxiliary properties within specified tolerances of their reference values. To solve this problem, we introduce GRACE (Gradient-Resolved Adaptive Constrained Exploration), a method that optimizes discrete biological sequences using gradients from property predictors via a straight-through estimator.…

items.title: scXOrGAN: A Generative Framework for Cross-Organ Single-Cell Transcriptomic Translation
items.summary: Gene expression profiles of organs provide important insights into their health and disease states. However, while some organs can be sampled only through invasive procedures, others, such as blood, are readily accessible. Existing methods for predicting gene expression in one organ from another typically work with bulk or averaged profiles, obscuring cell specific differences. Translation at single-cell resolution is more challenging, because individual cells in the source and target organs lack direct correspondence. Here, we present scXOrGAN, a generative model that translates single-cell transcriptomes between two organs of the same individual using data that are unpaired at the cell level. scXOrGAN combines two variational autoencoders that share a latent space with cycle consistency, adversarial training and distribution matching.…

items.title: Automated benchmarking with structured variant effect data
items.summary: Protein variant effect prediction (VEP) has a wide range of applications, from describing the role of mutations in human disease to improving enzymes for industrial applications. VEP is now predominantly powered by machine learning models and high-throughput experimentation. Progress in this field depends on fair and systematic model comparison, which is complicated by the heterogeneity of VEP tasks and the diversity of model implementations. ProteinGym is the most widely used VEP benchmark, but it does not have a standard representation for datasets or models. This makes it difficult for others to run their own benchmarks with it and for the benchmark to keep up with new datasets and models. We address these shortcomings with the ProteinGym framework (PGF), which standardizes dataset representations, model interfaces, and evaluation protocols.…

items.title: RBAi Scholar: Semantic and Hybrid biomedical literature Search for Researchers and AI assistants
items.summary: Motivation: A keyword search for mitochondrial dysfunction can miss a paper that says impaired mitochondrial function, so an empty result does not show that no such paper exists. Search by meaning addresses this mismatch, but it blurs exact strings such as gene symbols. Results: We present RBAi Scholar, which lets researchers and AI assistants search a growing corpus of biomedical abstracts by meaning (semantic search), by keyword, or by meaning among the papers that contain a required term (hybrid search). We tested it on a fixed version of 11.1 million records. For 500 questions worded unlike their target papers, semantic search placed the target in the top ten for 65.0%, against 18.6% for LitSense 2.0 and 0.8% for PubMed. OpenAlex semantic search, documented as using GTE-Large-EN embeddings, reached 27.8%.…

items.title: Adaptive Representations for Real-World Enzyme Optimization
items.summary: Protein fitness landscapes are highly rugged, giving rise to complex optimization landscapes. Bayesian optimization (BO) with Gaussian processes (GPs) is widely used in protein engineering for its sample efficiency and calibrated uncertainty estimates. Here, we study a joint fine-tuning framework of a protein language model (PLM) and a GP across enzyme fitness landscapes that span various distinct mutation regimes encountered in real-world engineering campaigns. Joint fine-tuning optimizes the PLM and GP parameters together in an uncertainty-calibrated manner, providing an adaptive representation that utilizes the information from previously acquired points in addition to the existing knowledge from pretraining.…

items.title: AUTOENCODIX: powering a hub for biological representation learning models
items.summary: Autoencoders are a foundational architecture for biological representation learning and empower methods for denoising, multi-modal integration, explainable embeddings, and synthetic data generation. But, new architectures are scattered across isolated repositories, which hampers benchmarking, the reuse of pretrained models, and the transfer to new data modalities. Here, we present the next generation of AUTOENCODIX, a Python package and model hub for biological representation learning. Its modular, standardized API unifies preprocessing, training, hyperparameter optimization, evaluation, generation, and explanation across a growing set of architectures, now including disentangled, masked, semi-supervised, and 2D/3D image autoencoders.…

items.title: Resplitting LIT-PCBA with MolSCISSOR: A Memory-Efficient, Quasi-Deterministic Framework for Reducing Structural and Physicochemical Biases
items.summary: Reliable training-test partitioning is essential for developing and evaluating virtual screening (VS) methods, particularly in the era of machine learning (ML). However, existing molecular dataset splitting approaches do not simultaneously address key challenges in rigorous VS evaluation: cross-partition structural bias, test-set inter-class physicochemical bias, high memory requirements, limited scalability, stochastic allocation, a lack of automated optimization and of flexible training-test similarity control. We introduce MolSCISSOR, a lightweight, memory-efficient, quasi-deterministic framework for stratified data partitioning that integrates clustering and training-test allocation through multi-objective optimization.…

items.title: Capturing human expertise for AI-assisted molecular structure annotation
items.summary: We developed a large language model-based tool that captures expert reasoning in bile acid structure elucidation, drawing on hand written notebooks, scientific literature, and recorded voice-to-text analytical sessions. It generates human-readable reports detailing evidence for and against candidate structures, tracing each inference to its source and identifying ambiguities. When applied to data, the tool proposes bile acid conjugates lacking reference spectra.

items.title: HapAdapter: A Transfer Learning Protocol for DNA Foundation Models Adapted to Diploid Personal Epigenomes
items.summary: The rapid rise of large language models (LLMs) has spurred the development of genomic language models (gLMs) that capitalize on the key features of natural language present in biological sequences. Moreover, DNA foundation models, a sub-class of gLMs, have demonstrated impressive accuracy in predicting a wide range of functional tracks from DNA sequence input. However, current DNA foundation models are exclusively trained on haploid reference genome sequences -- despite personal and graph genomes becoming the new standard for genomic analyses. This is principally because the cost to train gLMs on a personal diploid genome for a single individual is not currently practical.…

items.title: GeneArbiter improves plant genome annotations while preserving established gene models
items.summary: As plant genome resources expand, updating established annotations requires incorporating improved gene models without disrupting correct structures or stable identifiers. We developed GeneArbiter, an evidence guided framework that treats annotation updating as a correction preservation problem. GeneArbiter uses the current annotation as a backbone, integrates alternative models with RNA splice junction and homologous protein evidence, and applies constrained language model arbitration followed by deterministic release and identifier reconciliation. In rice MH63, GeneArbiter recovered 4,701 reference loci missed by the current annotation while losing 1,890 current exact loci, yielding a net gain of 2,811 exact matches and increasing the gene level exact hit rate from 70.77% to 77.77%.…

items.title: Confident but misplaced: a model-free ruler for post-translational modification placement by AI structure predictors
items.summary: AI structure predictors accept post-translationally modified (PTM) residues, but whether they place the added atoms where crystallography finds them, and whether their confidence reveals when they do not, is unknown. We first built a ruler from experiment alone: independent crystal structures of the same site reproduce the added atoms of oxidised cysteine and methionine to 0.32 [A], the closest pre-cutoff library rotamer lies at 0.41 [A] and a model-free guess at 4.17 [A]. We then predicted 176 hold-out PTM sites, released after every model's training cut-off, with RareFold, Boltz-2, Chai-1 and AlphaFold 3, using identical inputs and thresholds fixed before measurement.…

items.title: rnaModScan: context-aware deep learning-based filtering of nanopore m6A and inosine calls
items.summary: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) can detect multiple RNA modifications, but falsepositive background calls complicate transcriptome-wide analysis. We developed rnaModScan,a deep learning filter that integrates Dorado scores for all eight modification types with local sequence, repeat, and per-read alignment features to distinguish N6-methyladenosine (m6A) and inosine candidates from background calls. Using public RNA004 data, we evaluated site classification by grouped five-fold cross-validation and assessed transfer to HeLa cellular RNA using model weights fitted exclusively to HEK293T cellular RNA and unmodified in vitrotranscribed controls. For m6A sites outside the canonical DRACH motif, filtering removed 92.85% of the Dorado/modkit candidates while retaining 93.34% of their original matches to the GLORI reference map.…

items.title: L++: A Language for Programming Life
items.summary: Living systems run on a code written in DNA or RNA, but expressing that code as a model that scientists can write, run and read remains difficult. We present L++, a holistic programming language in which life can be described, simulated and, beyond that, designed; its nouns are biological, and people and AI systems can both write it. Molecules, reactions, compartments, cells, organs and populations are written directly and nest by containment, so one grammar spans a reaction and the population around it. Quantities carry units, objects take places in space, and values can be set in time. Named kinetic parameters select one family of rate laws, from mass action to cooperative enzyme kinetics, and a few operators write complexes, states and gene products in one line.…

items.title: FunDLM: A Foundation DNA Language Model for Fungi
items.summary: Background: Fungi are important pathogens and biotechnology resources, but lack a broadly applicable fungal DNA language model. Models trained on diverse fungal genomes can support functional interpretation of genomic variants and a broad range of genomic tasks. Results: We introduce FunDLM, a family of four DNA language models pre-trained on 426 fungal reference assemblies spanning 217 genera and 14.3 Gb of sequence. Without task-specific training, FunDLM-Medium-1024bp distinguished phenotype-associated missense variants of Saccharomyces cerevisiae from synonymous controls with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.875. It performed comparably to Evo 2, a generalist model with about 15 times more parameters, and better than Nucleotide Transformer v3. The model also recognized mutations that disrupt start codons or introduce premature stop codons in S.…

items.title: A Benchmark for Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Enzyme Kinetic Parameters of Metabolic Networks
items.summary: Large-scale kinetic models predict how metabolism responds to genetic and environmental perturbations, but building them at scale is limited by the scarcity of experimentally determined enzyme kinetic parameters. Generative machine learning has been proposed to address this bottleneck, yet prior work has each introduced a single, bespoke architecture, leaving open which generative paradigm suits this problem and why. We introduce a benchmark suite for generative modeling of high-dimensional enzyme kinetic parameter sets: labeled datasets of kinetically feasible Escherichia coli models paired with a mechanistically grounded evaluation harness that scores generated ensembles on dynamical stability and agreement with experimentally observed phenotypes, rather than statistical realism alone.…

items.title: EHRMENEIA: A Benchmark for Foundation Models on Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
items.summary: Electronic health record foundation models are evaluated using heterogeneous targets, vocabularies, and adaptation procedures, preventing systematic characterization across model families. We introduce EHRMENEIA (https://ehrmeneia.upc.edu/), a benchmark that provides a multidimensional evaluation framework for next-event prediction, multi-horizon event occurrence, trajectory fidelity and few-shot representation transfer. EHRMENEIA preserves each model's native vocabulary and temporal representation while mapping clinical outputs to shared evaluation objects. Applied to two released clinical checkpoints and two synthetic demonstrations, the framework exposed substantial differences not only in performance but in the clinical questions that could be evaluated from each model--dataset interface.…

items.title: Task-aligned foundation model representations enable single-cell cytokine response inference
items.summary: Inferring cellular responses from single-cell transcriptomes requires interpreting changes relative to an appropriate baseline while retaining cell-type context. Here we present CYTAP, which adapts frozen single-cell foundation model embeddings for cytokine-response inference by combining donor-adjusted receiver states with deviations from matched control centroids. CYTAP uses a shared classifier to assign relative single-cell response scores across 90 cytokines and supports unpaired analyses using counterfactual control references. Baseline-relative representations improved held-out-donor prediction with both State SE and scFoundation. Across independent perturbation datasets, CYTAP prioritized applied cytokines, including when receptor transcripts were sparsely detected, and ranked administered cytokines among the top ten in both in vivo datasets.…

items.title: GNEval: A Context-Specific Benchmark for Gene Network Inference with Single-Cell Foundation Models
items.summary: Gene network (GN) inference plays a critical role in understanding gene relationships and their roles in biological functions and diseases. Existing single-cell GN inference methods often rely on limited data from individual studies. Single-cell foundation models, pretrained on large and diverse datasets, provide a range of gene-gene association signals that offer a promising basis for GN inference. However, it remains unclear which GN properties these signals capture and how they compare with domain-specific methods. To address this gap, we introduce GNEval, a unified benchmark for evaluating pretrained model derived gene associations for network inference. We benchmark 21 gene representations and association scores from 11 models, including static gene embeddings (S), contextual embeddings (C), and gene-gene attention scores (A).…

items.title: CellTouch: Learning to separate touching nuclei in anisotropic 3D cell cultures
items.summary: 3D-oids, such as spheroids and organoids, are essential models in drug discovery and precision medicine, and quantitative analysis requires every nucleus to be segmented separately. Accurate 3D instance segmentation remains challenging, because nuclei are densely packed and touching, and volumes are sampled more coarsely along the Z-axis than laterally. Most existing methods were developed for near-isotropic data and tend to merge neighbouring nuclei. To address this challenge, we propose CellTouch, a deep learning method for anisotropic 3D nuclei instance segmentation that predicts flow fields and a contact channel, which separates touching nuclei directly from the network output. Ablations showed that the contact channel is the key design element, and CellTouch outperformed state-of-the-art methods on in-house data and widely used public datasets.…

items.title: Distance-stratified benchmarking of variant-effect predictors on β-lactamase deep mutational scanning data
items.summary: Mutations far from the active site of antibiotic-resistance enzymes can change resistance, but it is unclear what information predicts their effects. We asked how the performance of a protein language model (ESM2), a structure-based stability predictor (ThermoMPNN) and simple structural descriptors changes with distance from the catalytic residues, using deep mutational scanning data for the {beta}-lactamases TEM-1 (four assays) and VIM-2 (one assay). We measured Spearman correlation and AUROC within distance bins, with bootstrap intervals over positions. In TEM-1, ESM2 accuracy fell with distance (Stiffler assay: {rho} = 0.72 below 8 [A] and 0.42 beyond 20 [A]), while the stability score rose ({rho} = 0.41 to 0.70).…

items.title: VS-Suite: Automated Consensus Virtual Screening Platform for Improved Screening of Small Molecules
items.summary: Growing the recent advances in artificial intelligence and machine leaning (AI&ML) approaches accelerated small molecules screening against targeted proteins with limited computational resources and time. Finding accurate binding pose and affinity prediction is challenges task and traditional docking tools and lacks the reproducibility. Development of the Co-folding model is paradigm shift in drug discovery and development, allowing to predict protein ligand complexes without experimental crystal structures. Notably Boltz-2 predicts the complex structure along with binding affinity directly using protein FASTA sequence and ligand SMILES. Our previous studies confirmed that Boltz-2 is classify binder non-binders effectively. Autodock Vina and GNINA are widely used docking with knowledge and CNN based scoring functions allows to screen potential small molecules.…

items.title: RecurSieve: A Python Package to Detect Subtle Gene Expression Differences Across Single-Cell RNA-seq Comparisons Using Iterative Machine Learning
items.summary: Most existing methods for performing differential expression testing using single-cell RNA-seq data evaluate genes independently and primarily detect shifts in mean RNA levels. These methods may thus miss RNAs that distinguish experimental groups jointly or through changes in the shape of genes' expression distributions. To address this limitation, we developed RecurSieve, an iterative ensemble learning method that combines shared expression classification with unsupervised clustering to recursively identify gene sets with group-based expression differences. Because experimental labels apply to heterogeneous populations of single cells within each comparative group, RecurSieve allows dynamic label reassignment during iterative training to detect subtle, non-linear expression patterns.…

items.title: Extracting generator-specific information from irregular brain field potentials: a comparative study of feature-based and deep learning approaches.
items.summary: Brain field potentials (FPs) reflect the combined activity of multiple neural sources, challenging the accuracy of their temporal series and their spatial origin difficult to establish from waveform inspection alone. However, FP generators obtained by independent component analysis exhibit characteristic temporal patterns and unique spatial profiles that allow their identification, even during apparently irregular activity. Here, we compared feature-based machine learning (ML) and end-to-end deep learning (DL) approaches to assess how effectively this information can be extracted from short segments and whether learning directly from raw signals offers advantages over predefined signal descriptors. We analyzed irregular FP-generator activity from multiple hippocampal generators in a dataset pooled across experimenters, recording devices, and electrode types.…

items.title: Deep Learning-Guided Design of Candidate Synthetic Cis-Regulatory Elements for a TCF7+ Progenitor-Exhausted-like CD8+ T-Cell State
items.summary: Progenitor-exhausted CD8+ T cells (Tex-prog) are essential for sustaining T-cell-mediated immunity during chronic infection and cancer and therefore offer a promising immunotherapy target. Synthetic cis-regulatory elements (CREs) could enable selective transgene expression in Tex-prog cells, but whether they can distinguish this population from closely related CD8+ T-cell exhaustion states remains unclear. Here, we integrated publicly available paired single-cell ATAC-seq and single-cell RNA-seq datasets from mouse infection and tumor models and identified an ATAC-defined Tex-prog-like population (C1). We used the CREsted framework to fine-tune a pretrained Borzoi model to predict chromatin accessibility across C1 and ten comparator populations. We then used CREsted to design candidate synthetic CREs with predicted preferential accessibility in C1.…

items.title: Target-specifc machine-learning scoring functions boost structure-based virtual screening for PfDHODH
items.summary: Plasmodium falciparum dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (PfDHODH) is a validated antimalarial target for which no inhibitor has yet been approved, and no target-specific machine learning scoring functions (ML SFs) have been reported for it. Here, we developed PfDHODH-specific ML SFs for structure-based virtual screening from a small dataset of 73 experimentally confirmed actives and 86 inactives, supplemented with property-matched (PM) and property-unmatched (PU) decoys. We compared five algorithms, several protein-ligand interaction featurisation schemes and classification and regression formulations under two evaluation designs: a Butina clustering split and a UMAP-based split in which each cluster of actives was held out in turn.…

items.title: MoHuTS: Developability-Aware Antibody Humanization Using Multi-Objective Tree Search
items.summary: Antibody humanization aims to reduce the immunogenicity risk associated with non-human antibodies while preserving antigen binding and other properties important for therapeutic development. Identifying suitable framework substitutions often requires repeated rounds of variant construction and experimental testing, making humanization costly. Recently, machine-learning methods, including language models trained on antibody sequences, have been proposed to identify human-like framework substitutions. Although prior humanization methods have considered antigen binding and biophysical properties, it remains challenging to balance humanness across both chains with developability-related properties such as thermal stability and aggregation propensity while retaining favorable parental properties.…

items.title: Using deep learning to estimate the shifting mutational fitness landscape of SARS-CoV-2 spike along a phylogeny
items.summary: A longstanding challenge in evolutionary biology is to determine the fitness effects of mutations, and how they change during evolution. For SARS-CoV-2, millions of naturally evolved viral sequences are available. Bloom and Neher devised a method to estimate the effects of mutations from these sequences. The method counts how many times each mutation occurs on the branches of a phylogenetic tree and compares that count to the count expected under neutral mutation. However, the method assumes that the effect of a mutation at a site does not depend on the sequence at other sites. To estimate shifts in effects, it must divide the tree into clades chosen in advance and make a separate estimate for each clade. Here we train a deep-learning model on the entire SARS-CoV-2 tree.…

items.title: GlycaNER: An Automated Glycan Structure Term Detection and Normalization Tool in Biomedical Literature
items.summary: Glycans are complex carbohydrates covalently attached to biomolecules and play essential roles in protein folding, stability, intracellular trafficking, and molecular recognition. Glycan-related biological processes are vital to normal physiology, and their disruptions can contribute to various diseases. In the literature, glycans are described by their structures or recurring substructures, known as glycan structure terms (GSTs). We developed GlycaNER, a transformer-based entity recognition tool that detects GSTs and related glyco-terms in text, maps them to existing dictionary entries and suggests unmatched terms for expert curation. GlycaNER is developed with three objectives.…

items.title: Performance Characteristics of Reasoning Large Language Models for Evidence Extraction from Clinical Genomics Literature
items.summary: BACKGROUND Genetic variant curation requires literature-guided comparison of variant prevalence in affected individuals versus healthy controls. This evidence is categorized as the PS4 evidence code by the AMP/ACMG variant interpretation guidelines and its manual extraction is a major bottleneck in clinical variant curation. We evaluated whether reasoning-capable large language models (LLMs) can support guideline-constrained PS4 evidence extraction from literature. METHODS We benchmarked twelve reasoning-capable LLMs spanning providers, capability tiers, and releases on 281 publication-variant pairs against an expert-curated truth-set. Models performed variant detection (Task 1) and PS4-eligible proband counting under ACMG/AMP and gene-specific ClinGen Variant Curation Expert Panel guidance (Task 2). Six newer models also underwent variant-level PS4 strength assignment (Task 3).…

items.title: Cross-cohort reproducibility of AI-assisted nanopore methylation profiling establishes diagnostic equivalence to WHO-integrated diagnoses in adult CNS tumors
items.summary: Background: Array-based methylation profiling with the Heidelberg classifier supports WHO-CNS5 classification of CNS tumors, but its substantial hands-on time, cost, centralized infrastructure and dependence on externally-hosted software limit broad implementation. Nanopore methylation sequencing combined with AI-based classification is a viable alternative, yet performance evidence required for implementation in adult CNS tumor diagnostics is limited. We test the equivalence of nanopore methylation profiling using the Sturgeon-v2 classifier against a WHO-CNS5-compliant integrated reference diagnosis incorporating array-based classification. Methods: We compared Sturgeon-v2 classifications from nanopore sequencing of fresh-frozen tissue DNA with array-based reference diagnoses of matched FFPE tissue DNA, in two cohorts of 154 and 47 primary CNS tumors.…

items.title: Causal Emergence of Macroscopic Stochastic Dynamics from a Multi-modal Foundation Model of Human Sleep
items.summary: Sleep is an essential, self organizing physiological state conserved across species, yet its macroscopic coordination remains governed by unknown physical principles. For nearly sixty years, clinical medicine has classified sleep into heuristic, discrete 30 second epochs, an empirical convention that flattens continuous non-equilibrium dynamics and leaves deep subcortical neuromodulatory control fundamentally unobservable. Although emerging artificial intelligence foundation models can decode multimodal physiology with high accuracy, their high-dimensional representations remain uninterpretable black boxes, leaving the generative laws of sleep unformulated.…

items.title: How many large language models does title-abstract screening need? Theory, two replications and an evaluation at real prevalence
items.summary: Background and Objectives: Researchers increasingly combine large language models (LLMs) to screen titles and abstracts, assuming that more models make screening safer. We estimated how many models a screening ensemble needs, given correlated errors, and tested the answer on independent reviews and at real prevalence. Methods: We modelled correlated votes with a beta-binomial model and estimated, by bootstrap, the smallest ensemble capturing 95% of the net-benefit gain attainable over the best single model, accounting for human reading time and machine cost. Eleven LLMs from four developers voted blind on records from 13 SYNERGY reviews (derivation).…

items.title: MedDx, a training-free AI phenotyping model, identifies alcohol use disorder in cirrhosis with hepatologist-level agreement
items.summary: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is often under-documented in patients with cirrhosis, which delays treatment. Expert chart review of clinical notes can identify under-documented AUD, but is not scalable. We propose MedDx, an open-weight, training-free, and engine-agnostic language model, to phenotype AUD using clinical notes in patients with cirrhosis. We benchmarked MedDx on a 485-patient study cohort sampled from the 14,406-patient Indiana Cirrhosis Registry, using a chart-review-based reference as ground truth. MedDx agreed with the ground truth at three-class Cohen's {kappa} 0.92, against 0.67 for the AUD diagnosis code. It agreed with one hepatologist at 0.85 on all 485 charts and with a second at 0.82 on 186 charts, on which the two hepatologists agreed at 0.87.…

items.title: ViDAS: Timely and Granular Estimation of Respiratory Virus Distributions in SARI Surveillance in Brazil
items.summary: Effective monitoring of Severe Acute Respiratory Infections (SARI) is critical for public health but faces challenges such as reporting delays, incomplete information on negative test results, and data sparsity in specific regions and age groups. This study proposes a novel statistical framework to estimate the granular distribution of respiratory viruses among hospitalized SARI patients in Brazil. We employ Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT) to model viral proportions as conditional probabilities based on patient age, location, and time. A key methodological contribution is the development of SViDAS, a semi-parametric estimator that integrates viral probabilities over continuous lognormal age distributions, enabling estimation for arbitrary age intervals.…

items.title: Figuring out the crisis contact cycle: accumulating phenomena and investigating LLM functions to identify threats and opportunities to help people who remain in the background of a crisis conversation
items.summary: In a prolonged crisis dialogue with a large language model (LLM), a change of speaker or topic, or a pause, can leave part of the previously reported danger outside the focus of the response. A previous study of 14-turn dialogues described reactions to crisis messages; here, the subject is the subsequent history of specific people. The aim was to build a map of phenomena of person-level crisis contact from scenario circumstances, LLM responses, independent clinical judgments, and machine readings. The research design comprised 48 Ukrainian-language analytical dialogues with ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, built on 16 scenarios that unfolded over 37 turns in three rounds.…

items.title: Deformation prior-guided deep learning for post hoc motion deblurring in single-phase cardiac computed tomography
items.summary: Purpose: To develop and evaluate DeTangle, a deep learning-based method for cardiac computed tomography (CT) deblurring using internally estimated deformation-magnitude maps and single-phase reconstructed images. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study included 60 patients (median age, 61 years; 40 males) who underwent cardiac CT between January 2024 and October 2025. Patients comprised training, validation, and internal test sets (30, five, and 25 patients, respectively). DeTangle jointly optimizes deformation-map estimation and restoration using privileged deformation information during training but requires only target-phase reconstructed images at inference. Full reconstructions (250 ms) served as inputs and half reconstructions (66 ms) as references. The structural similarity index measure (SSIM) was assessed in 424 test phases.…

items.title: Reproducible variability: assessing human vs. AI discordance in attempting to reproduce the same observational study
items.summary: Objective: Previously, nine expert teams given a published study and identical code sets produced nine substantially different cohorts, prompting the conclusion that analytic code cannot be reliably generated from natural-language description. We tested whether an artificial intelligence (AI) agent, given that same description, reproduces a cohort definition more faithfully and consistently than those teams. Materials and Methods: Against a claims database of 35.9 million patients, we executed 27 independent reproductions of that published glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist cohort definition: the nine published human definitions re-implemented deterministically (Arm A); nine independent AI agent runs given the source paper as published (Arm B); and nine given a rewrite that removed its internal contradictions (Arm C). All arms received identical frozen code sets.…

items.title: efe-T/RecurrentGraphLM-fineweb-edu
Automated neuroimaging meta-analysis through LLM-guided selection improves recovery of published spatial patterns
items.summary: Systematic meta-analysis enables cumulative science, but expert-led, manual workflows do not scale with the growing literature. In neuroimaging, automated frameworks are widely used but typically sacrifice precision by using coarse article selection and pooling reported results, combining different tasks, populations or comparisons even when only a subset is relevant. Here we present AutoNIMA, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that screens articles using expert-defined eligibility criteria and parses heterogeneous tables to extract brain stereotactic coordinates and select relevant analyses within each article. AutoNIMA produced maps more closely matching expert-curated references than a search-only baseline representing existing automated methods in 26 of 27 meta-analyses. Analysis-level selection accounted for most of the improvement.…

items.title: Where single-cell foundation models help: a public-data benchmark of annotation, in silico perturbation and gene regulatory inference
items.summary: Single-cell foundation models (FMs) are proposed as general tools for cell-type annotation, in silico perturbation and gene-regulatory-network inference. We benchmarked five FMs (scGPT, Geneformer V1 and V2, Nicheformer, scFoundation), four newer FMs, CellOracle, supervised perturbation models and task-matched simple baselines on public data, from Perturb-seq screens of cell lines and primary T cells to a brain organoid screen, the developing mouse cortex and lung cancer biopsies, under an analysis plan fixed before the new results. FMs helped most when labels were transferred across species: Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy from human to mouse lung, above every baseline (at most 0.94), and fine-tuned Geneformer V2 reached macro-F1 0.88 from mouse to human, against at most 0.74.…

items.title: GeneScribe - a tool for fact extraction and gene summarization using Large Language Models (LLMs)
items.summary: <SPAN style="font-weight: 400;">The rapid growth of biological data presents major challenges for expert curation and integration of gene information into biological knowledgebases such as the Alliance of Genome Resources (Alliance), limiting data discovery, analysis and dissemination. The current automated approach to gene summary generation at the Alliance relies on curated data and a combination of rule-based and optimization algorithms. While effective, this method is limited by the timely availability of curated annotations, and prone to producing redundant or fragmented descriptions that may obscure the key biological roles of a gene. To address these limitations, we developed GeneScribe, a tool that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate and scale the generation of gene function summaries.…

items.title: Learning the Malignant Transformation of Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells Using Explainable AI
items.summary: Tumor evolution in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) drives drug resistance and disease progression, yet the cellular transitions underlying the malignant transformation of cells remain poorly understood. Comparing this progression of cancer cells across patients is challenging owing to substantial inter-patient cell heterogeneity. Here, based on single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data of 227 patients with LUAD including 422,727 tumor cells, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of tumor cell progression and developed Global Tumor Time (GTT), a continuous measure of tumor cell progression across patients.…

items.title: Auditable AI agents for verifiable end-to-end scientific analysis
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are evolving from research assistants into end-to-end executors, yet their capacity to generate conclusions at scale outpaces rigorous verification. Here we introduce an auditability-centred paradigm for scientific automation, wherein trust relies not on generative capability or self-evaluation, but on whether claims can be independently traced to primary evidence, reviewed and corrected. Moving beyond post-hoc checks, we embed verification throughout the research lifecycle via four principles: grounded knowledge, bounded execution, evidence-backed results and independent verification. We instantiate this paradigm in EvoTrace for viral evolutionary analysis.…

items.title: All-Atom Structure Tokenizer: AtomLM-9b for Biomolecular Structure Prediction
items.summary: We develop an All-atom Structure Tokenizer that compresses biomolecular geometry into discrete structural tokens and achieves high-accuracy all-atom reconstruction. A hierarchical geometric encoder and finite scalar quantization map chemical units to a shared vocabulary of 8,192 tokens, while a joint coordinate de-tokenizer reconstructs backbone, side-chain, nucleic-acid, and ligand heavy atoms. The tokenizer achieves all-atom lDDT scores of 0.832 and 0.835 on CASP14 and CASP15, respectively. Building on this tokenizer, we train AtomLM-9b, an autoregressive language model based on Qwen3.5-9B that predicts structural tokens from molecular identities and connectivity and decodes them into complete atomic structures.…

items.title: BYSTER: multimodal graph learning resolves bystander versus tumor-specific T cell states in the tumor immune microenvironment
items.summary: Bystander T cells infiltrate tumors without recognizing tumor antigens and constitute a substantial component of the tumor microenvironment. Whether they are passive residents or active participants in antitumor immunity, and how they influence immunotherapy response, remains poorly understood, largely because transcriptional states and T-cell receptor (TCR) sequences alone do not reliably resolve antigen specificity. Here, we developed BYSTER, a heterogeneous graph neural network that integrates transcriptional representations with paired TCR representations through cross-modal message passing at metacell and metaTCR resolution. Across three datasets with distinct definitions of tumor specificity, BYSTER achieved mean AUROCs of 0.729 to 0.920, outperforming unimodal and conventional multimodal baselines, and ablation analyses confirmed the contribution of cross-modal message passing.…

items.title: RIPPLE: learning nucleotide relations in an RNA foundation model
items.summary: RNA function depends on interactions between nucleotides that can be widely separated in sequence, yet capturing these relationships remains challenging for RNA language models. Existing approaches primarily learn nucleotide relationships implicitly from individual nucleotide reconstruction or rely on external structural information to model nucleotide interactions. Here we introduce RIPPLE, an RNA foundation model that learns to identify and represent sparse, predictively useful nucleotide relationships directly from sequence. Pretrained on 32.4 million RNA sequences, RIPPLE uses pairwise predictive utility to guide relational learning, transferring training-time supervision into a sequence-only model without requiring structural inputs at inference.…

items.title: Robust ORF Deconvolution from Multiple Ribo-seq Datasets with Group LASSO Penalty
items.summary: Ribo-seq has provided compelling evidence that there are many translated but unannotated ORFs. Despite a growing body of peptidomic support for cryptic ORFs, the computational discovery of weakly translated, short and mutually overlapping ORFs has remained a major bottleneck. Here we introduce PRICE 2, a method designed to resolve these challenging translation events by adapting concepts from isoform deconvolution. PRICE 2 employs a generative model combined with group LASSO regularized regression to jointly infer active ORFs across multiple sequencing runs. In a comprehensive benchmark, PRICE 2 outperformed thirteen state-of-the-art tools in detecting short and overlapping ORFs.…

items.title: Efficient 3D Cell Tracking by Integer Programming Guided by Self-Supervised Division Scores
items.summary: Recognizing divisions in cell tracking is difficult when cells are densely packed and divide frequently. A daughter can lie closer to a neighbor than to its mother, misleading distance-based linking. Visual cues can reduce such errors, but learning them often requires manual lineage annotations, which are particularly costly for 3D data. We propose an efficient self-supervised tracker trained without manual lineage annotations, using biological priors to extract reliable divisions from its distance-based tracks as labels. Networks trained on these labels predict division scores from mother-daughter images and the mother's temporal context to guide an integer linear program in resolving competing daughter assignments. Among the evaluated trackers, ours ranks first on one of three C. elegans datasets and second to a supervised tracker on the other two.…

items.title: Neural networks for dengue forecasting: a systematic review
items.summary: Background: Early dengue forecasts are an important tool for disease mitigation, and neural networks (NNs) are powerful predictive models that have contributed to many areas of public health. We reviewed NN applications in the dengue forecasting literature to inform model design for future studies. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched Web of Science/Knowledge, Scopus, PubMed, and Science Direct up to September 2025 for studies using NNs to forecast dengue in human populations, retrieving 628 records. After removing duplicates, four inclusion and two exclusion criteria were applied: articles had to be in English, implement NN or deep learning techniques, predict dengue fever incidence or risk, and clearly state data sources, processing steps, network parameters, and architectures.…

items.title: Language model-assisted label refinement for accurate sepsis detection from electronic health records
items.summary: Sepsis is a leading cause of hospital mortality, yet timely recognition is hampered by nonspecific presentations and label noise in code-based case definitions. We developed STRIDE, a machine-learning framework for sepsis detection across seven hospitals with a scalable approach to label quality. We used a large language model applied to discharge summaries to refine encounter-level labels, with 349 physician-adjudicated encounters informing prompt development and serving as a clinical reference for evaluation. We compared 8-, 24-, and 48-hour observation windows and benchmarked against SOFA, SIRS, and Epic. Among 352,415 eligible encounters, STRIDE-8 achieved ROC-AUCs of 0.949 in derivation testing and 0.871 in physician-adjudicated evaluation. Removing SIRS-related predictors reduced these values to 0.853 and 0.743.…

items.title: LifeLine.ai: A SigLIP-MedGemma Multimodal Framework with KTO Alignment for Open-Vocabulary 12-Lead ECG Report Generation
items.summary: Automated twelve-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation has historically relied on discriminative classifiers limited to closed-set diagnostic labels, signal reconstruction, or saliency heatmaps. While categorizing predefined arrhythmias well, these static classifiers cannot generate narrative clinical reports, incorporate patient history, or support interactive clinical question-answering (Q&A). We present LifeLine.ai, an end-toend multimodal Vision-ECG-Language framework for automated cardiac diagnosis and clinical reporting. After early attempts at waveform peak-tracking and coordinate mapping failed against complex morphological variations, we leveraged large-scale PhysioNet repositories (MIMIC-IV and PTB-XL).…

items.title: Estimating the prevalence of undiagnosed Long COVID using health insurance claims data
items.summary: Background: Long COVID (LC) is a complex, multisystemic condition whose prevalence is poorly understood due, in part, to underdiagnosis. Methods: We used the Colorado All Payer Claims Database (CO APCD), which covers approximately 70% of insured Coloradans, to train a machine learning eXtreme Gradient Boosting model to predict undiagnosed LC. The 243 candidate predictors included clinical symptoms, comorbid conditions, healthcare utilization, pharmaceutical prescriptions, and individual- and neighborhood-level socioeconomic conditions. Models were trained on a dataset of 38,064 adults (18+), including individuals with the LC diagnostic code (U09.9), and a set of comparators without the code, matched by age, sex and payer. The trained model was used to estimate the prevalence of undiagnosed LC within a larger CO APCD extract comprising 2.1 million adults.…

items.title: Scalable frameworks for local evaluation of AI-enabled imaging devices using PACS-integrated large language models
items.summary: Introduction: Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled imaging device performance may vary across institutions due to differences in disease prevalence, patient demographics, and acquisition protocols. Routine local evaluation, including pre-deployment baseline testing and post-deployment monitoring, remains limited by manual data curation. A large language model (LLM)-as-a-judge approach using existing radiology reports provides a method of performing local evaluation. Methods: We established PACS-integrated LLMs in HIPAA-compliant environments. We then developed two scalable frameworks to automate key processes of local evaluation: selection of a candidate series for device inference and generation of report-derived labels.…

items.title: Smartwatch-based loss-of-pulse detection for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: the BECA-S2 and BECA-S6 studies
items.summary: Objective. Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is often unwitnessed, which delays treatment and lowers the chance of survival. A smartwatch could act as a witness by detecting loss of pulse from wrist photoplethysmography (PPG) and subsequently alert emergency services. We aimed to develop and evaluate such a detection model. Approach. As smartwatch data of OHCA are extremely difficult to acquire, we used in-hospital proxy data to test sensitivity: wrist PPG and accelerometry recorded during baseline and induced loss-of-pulse periods in 31 patients during catheter ablation of ventricular arrhythmias and defibrillation threshold (DFT) testing during subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD) implantation (BECA-S2). In total, 33 loss-of-pulse events, annotated using accompanying electrocardiograms and, where available, arterial blood pressure, were included.…

items.title: AnyCam: Anything Can Represent Camera for Video Generation
items.summary: Camera-controlled video generation re-renders a video along a target camera trajectory, yet moving the camera around an object, the most natural way to change the viewpoint of an object-centric scene, remains difficult. Existing methods condition either on camera parameters, which are scale-ambiguous in monocular video, or on explicit geometry such as warped point clouds or depth, which breaks down under large viewpoint changes. We present AnyCam, a method that represents the camera with an anchor object in the scene: we reconstruct it in 3D and render it along the target trajectory, a camera signal that is scale-aware, view-complete and easy to specify relative to the object. A video diffusion model transfers the content and dynamics of the source video to the new viewpoint.…

items.title: Tracking Any Point with Agentic Visual Reasoning
items.summary: A general-purpose Vision-Language Model (VLM) has surpassed expert vision models in many domains such as object detection and video recognition. However, point correspondence is known to be challenging for VLMs since it goes beyond object-level recognition: it requires pixel-level localization of the same physical surface point across observations, even when appearance changes or the point disappears and later reappears. In this paper, we introduce AgenTAP, a VLM-based agent that directly predicts point coordinates and visibility and actively reasons over videos.
