In a ten-domain enterprise collection, a task's evidence is spread across a source document of median length 27 pages (mean 48.8, maximum 873); a third of tasks rest mainly on charts, drawings, and maps; and 70.9% require two or more reasoning hops. We post-train Kimi-K2.7, an open-weight foundation model, at its full context window on 1,465 expert-authored tasks with atomic rubrics from that collection, training rank-32 adapters with one round of privileged-context on-policy self-distillation followed by two rounds of rubric-reward reinforcement learning. We render each PDF as text for training and as extracted text plus selected page images at evaluation. The smoothed RL training reward rises from 0.37 in the first tenth of the run to 0.67 in the last.…

items.title: MotionServe: Efficient Multi-Robot Serving by Exploiting Robot Execution Slack
items.summary: As robotic arms undertake diverse manipulation tasks, a deployment may need to serve many task-specific vision-language-action (VLA) policies concurrently. Dedicating a GPU to each robot is costly, motivating shared-GPU inference. Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) allows compatible policies to share a frozen backbone with lightweight policy-specific adapters, reducing model-weight memory and enabling cross-policy batching. However, robot inference must keep pace with physical execution. With action chunking, robots continue executing buffered actions while awaiting new predictions, and the remaining buffered time provides each robot's execution slack for serving its next request. Once this slack is exhausted, the robot stalls until new actions arrive, interrupting task progress.…

items.title: The Growth Path Is the Missing Half of Neural Networks
items.summary: An artificial neuron computes and learns, but it does not live: the units of a network are fixed when it is designed, and every one of them is kept and paid for whether it is used or not. We give each neuron a second pathway. Beside its Task Path, the usual computation and gradient learning, a dual-pathway neuron has a Growth Path: a nutrient flows from the outputs back through the network, every layer receives the same fixed budget, and each unit is fed in proportion to how much the units above it use it. A well-fed unit divides and a starving unit dies. This allocation is not a separate analysis or pruning step: it runs throughout training and reads only activations and weights. The task is still learned from labels with the ordinary loss, and the training procedure gains no phase, no schedule and no target size.…

items.title: RadarOSV: Unified 3D Scene and Motion Perception from mmWave Radars
items.summary: Millimeter-wave radar offers weather-resilient sensing for 3D occupancy prediction. Existing radar occupancy methods mainly model geometry, with limited joint modeling of semantics and motion. Cascaded imaging radar provides fine spatial detail but has a limited unambiguous velocity range, whereas single-chip radar offers a wider range but coarser spatial resolution. We propose RadarOSV, to our knowledge the first radar-only framework that jointly predicts occupancy, dynamic object semantics, and ground-relative velocity from raw radar data in unified voxels, by exploiting complementary measurements from both radars. Its Polar-to-Cartesian Geometry (PCG) backbone maps polar imaging-radar features into Cartesian voxels through fixed and deformable sampling, guiding cross-radar fusion for geometry and attribute prediction.…

items.title: PushMimic: Learning Adaptive Humanoid Box Pushing via Dynamic Motion Augmentation and Reference Distillation
items.summary: Humanoid box pushing is challenging when the physical properties of the task, such as the box mass and the ramp inclination, are unknown before the push begins. This paper presents PushMimic, a framework that learns adaptive humanoid box pushing from a single level-ground kinematic reference motion. The learned policy adapts its pushing posture to these properties without observing them. PushMimic augments the reference motion into a dynamically feasible motion dataset over these properties with sampling-based trajectory optimization, and distills the dataset into one motion tracking policy in one stage of training. Simulation results over box masses from 5 to 15 kg and ramp inclinations up to 15 degrees show that PushMimic raises the success rate from 57.8% to 88.8% compared with a baseline that tracks the original reference motion. It also reduces the cost of push of the arms by 22%.…

items.title: HERO: Hierarchical Region-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Exploration
items.summary: Autonomous exploration is widely used to map unknown environments, yet maintaining both path efficiency and low online computation remains difficult as environment scale increases. Hierarchical planners reduce global search through coarse regional representations but often rely on handcrafted local viewpoint-selection rules. Graph-based reinforcement learning can improve local decisions, but its inference cost grows with the exploration graph and global direction is usually represented only implicitly. To address these limitations, we present HERO, a hierarchical framework that assigns distinct responsibilities to global planning and learned local decision-making, enabling each level to focus on the function it is best suited to perform.…

items.title: SalivaryHSI-Seg: A New Challenging Benchmark for Ex Vivo Salivary Gland Hyperspectral Tissue Segmentation
items.summary: Salivary gland tumors are common lesions in oral and maxillofacial practice, and accurate identification of tumor regions and surrounding salivary gland tissues is important for tissue assessment, pathological sampling, and clinical decision support. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) records continuous spectral responses together with spatial imaging information, providing a promising way to capture fine-grained tissue-discriminative information. Nevertheless, the development of salivary gland HSI tissue segmentation remains limited due to the lack of standardized benchmarks with pixel-level annotations and unified evaluation protocols. To address this issue, we introduce SalivaryHSI-Seg, a hyperspectral tissue segmentation benchmark for ex vivo salivary gland specimens, containing 119 HSI samples from 31 patients with multi-class pixel-level annotations.…

items.title: Stable but Hidden: Identifiability and Experimental Design under Missing Compositional Support
items.summary: AI-guided scientific discovery often uses inexpensive predictors to allocate scarce verification measurements. We study a structural failure when relevant components have been observed separately but never jointly: distinct admissible response functions can agree on all observed compositions while disagreeing on the missing combinations. Additional same-support data cannot resolve this ambiguity, and agreement among fitted models need not expose it. We characterize the unresolved directions as an invisible subspace $\mathcal{N}_T(\mathcal{F}) = \ker \mathcal{R}_T$, whose geometry determines oracle zero-shot ambiguity and minimax risk under a symmetric, bounded ambiguity class.…

items.title: Pixel as the Common Language: Unified Multimodal Embedding via Visual Rendering
items.summary: Multimodal embedding models map heterogeneous inputs into a shared representation space, yet text-only, image-only, and composed inputs are still presented in distinct formats and follow different routes through the model. This fragmentation prevents heterogeneous tasks from jointly optimizing the same end-to-end encoding process, limiting supervision transfer across input configurations. To address this issue, we propose unification before encoding and instantiate this paradigm in RenderEmbed. The framework uses Visual Substrate Rendering to convert heterogeneous inputs into a common visual substrate for encoding with a VLM. From the resulting visual tokens, Progressive Hierarchical Anchor Encoding produces compact retrieval representations by interleaving learnable anchors and fusing their states across layers, retaining broad context and fine-grained cues.…

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy Is Not Deployment Value: Decision-Aligned Reliability Evaluation for Foundation MLIPs in Materials Discovery
items.summary: In AI-guided materials discovery, machine-learning models increasingly decide which candidate materials should receive expensive first-principles or experimental evaluation. Standard reliability metrics such as uncertainty, calibration, novelty, and ranking accuracy evaluate properties of the predictions, but success on these metrics does not necessarily imply a better downstream screening decision. We study this mismatch for foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials (MACE-MP, CHGNet, Orb V3) used to rank candidate crystal structures before DFT verification. We evaluate three representative reliability interventions (novelty detection, sparse DFT calibration, and chemistry-level ranking audits) using a deployment objective that measures how much DFT can be avoided while maintaining a required recall of near-hull candidates.…

items.title: orcarouter/Inkling-2-Mini-abliterated-GGUF
items.summary: text-generation / gguf

items.title: How Latent Transition Geometry Matters for Planning in World Models
items.summary: World models support planning by predicting how the environment evolves under candidate actions. However, one-step predictive accuracy alone does not characterize multi-step planning utility, which depends on distinguishing candidate futures. This raises a natural question: How does latent transition geometry shape planning? We investigate this through an action-conditioned transition-field view, using curvature regularization as a controlled intervention. Across four continuous-control tasks, appropriately tuned regularization improves planning, while excessive regularization can be detrimental. By decomposing the transition field into affine and non-affine components, we find that regularization reduces action sensitivity mainly through the non-affine component.…

items.title: What Do Co-Folding Models Learn? Insights from Enhanced Transition Path Sampling
items.summary: Co-folding models are diffusion-based generative models that sample biomolecular complexes from distributions learned on a large corpus of experimental data. Although these models are powerful for structure prediction, it remains unclear whether the conformational ensembles they learn resemble physically meaningful statistical ensembles. To understand what these models learn, we introduce transition path sampling (TPS), which uses Markov chain Monte Carlo over denoising trajectories to sample the learned distribution. Because its Monte Carlo trajectories resemble biomolecular dynamics, TPS couples directly with enhanced-sampling techniques to recover the full conformational ensemble. Applied to Boltz-2, enhanced TPS reveals physical conformational changes biased toward crystal-like states near the training data, indicating both learned physics and memorization.…

items.title: EVD-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for EEG-to-Image Decoding
items.summary: EEG-to-image decoding recovers visual information from non-invasive brain recordings, providing a window into human perception. However, comparisons across systems are confounded by a variable that is rarely reported as such: which participants' data the system was allowed to use. The same Top-1 score on a 200-way gallery may come from a per-participant system, a pooled model over all participants, or a model that never saw the test participant---cases that differ by more than most architectural changes between the methods being compared. We present \bench, a benchmark on THINGS-EEG2 that standardizes the gallery and EEG input, matches training budgets across systems within each regime, and compares three participant-access regimes: within-subject, joint-subject, and strict leave-one-subject-out, with unlabeled target calibration reported separately.…

items.title: Beyond Binary Correctness: A Surrogate for Confidence Learning in Large Language and Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Confidence estimation for large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) aims to assess how likely a particular generated response is to be correct. We investigate how learning this assessment can benefit from the model's predictive reliability on the underlying query. Binary correctness supervision, however, assigns identical labels to occasional errors and frequent failures, as well as isolated successes and consistent success. These outcomes can arise from substantially different predictive behavior under stochastic decoding. We propose a confidence-learning framework that supplements realized response correctness with query-level predictive reliability. We estimate reliability through repeated generations under a fixed model and decoding configuration, then combine the empirical success rate with individual correctness to construct a graded confidence surrogate.…

items.title: Bi-Refine: Semantic Verification-Guided Progressive Refinement for Moment Retrieval
items.summary: Moment Retrieval (MR) aims to identify the temporal segment in an untrimmed video that corresponds to a natural language query. Existing approaches commonly refine temporal predictions within the localization pathway, without explicitly verifying candidate-level semantic consistency. Moreover, directly reusing semantic scores as feedback can cause over-correction when the verification signal is unreliable. To address these issues, we propose Bi-Refine, a semantic verification-guided progressive refinement framework that formulates MR as a closed-loop verification-and-refinement process. A Heuristic Localization Branch first generates candidate moments, while a Semantic Verification Branch evaluates their query consistency in a semantically enriched latent space.…

items.title: PsyDrift: Healthy-Reference Latent Diffusion for Anomaly Scoring in Autism Spectrum Disorder
items.summary: Individual heterogeneity and acquisition-site variability complicate neuroimaging-based characterization of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). We propose PsyDrift, combining ASD/healthy-control-supervised functional-connectivity representations with healthy-reference latent diffusion. An encoder produces 128-dimensional representations, and a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) learns exclusively from healthy training latents. Distance from a diffusion-denoised reconstruction provides a continuous deviation score. We evaluate 1,102 subjects from all 20 ABIDE-I sites using five-seed leave-one-site-out cross-validation. The classifier and DDPM achieve mean-site AUROCs of $0.798 \pm 0.003$ and $0.718 \pm 0.013$, respectively; uncertainties denote seed standard deviations.…

items.title: Domain advantage in two-dimensional quantum-device design with multi-modal agentic harness
items.summary: High-quality two-dimensional quantum devices are commonly fabricated from mechanically exfoliated crystals, whose irregular shapes and placement require a lithographic layout tailored to each specimen. Drawing these layouts remains largely manual. We introduce qlaybench, a benchmark that tests whether language-model agents can turn microscope images and experimental requirements into device layouts that fit the specimen. Agents with conventional tools often construct devices when material outlines are supplied, but struggle to identify those outlines from images. Modelled on the human workflow, qlaybot, a multimodal agentic harness, connects image interpretation to the tools used to align images, draw device features and inspect the resulting layout.…

items.title: SWAM: State-aware World Action Model for Multi-Agent 3D Environments
items.summary: Interactive world models generate virtual environments autoregressively from player actions and visual history. However, visual history alone cannot reliably capture the evolving states of independently acting non-player characters (NPCs) in real games, particularly when they are outside the camera view. Recent multi-agent world models address this challenge through joint multi-view generation or persistent shared state, but often rely on external observations, like maps or scene geometry, or predefined state transitions. We present SWAM, a State-aware World Action Model that separates agent-state evolution from autoregressive visual generation in interactive 3D environments. A lightweight state model propagates character dynamics from actions without consuming generated frames, combining motion priors with learned scene-dependent corrections.…

items.title: STUN-Bench: Truly Unseen Tools for Evaluating Shared Tool Experience
items.summary: A tool router retrieves a few candidate tools per request and lets a language model choose. Methods that share experience across organizations add past requests about each tool to what the router retrieves. StableToolBench calls some of its test groups tests on "unseen" tools, yet the ToolBench instruction pool, which retrievers and experience-sharing methods learn from, contains every test query and labels every gold tool of the two single-tool groups among them. We release STUN-Bench (StableToolBench, Truly UNseen), a split whose experience pool has no item that labels or names 172 held-out tools. Unseen here means absent from shared experience and retriever training data, not from pretraining.…

items.title: One UWB Radar, Many Views: Comparing and Fusing Signal Representations for Human Activity Recognition
items.summary: IEEE 802.15.4z-compliant impulse-radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB) transceivers are increasingly built into consumer devices, enabling contactless, privacy-preserving human activity recognition (HAR) in healthcare. Before activity classification, the signal is typically converted into range-time, range-Doppler, or time-Doppler maps, each exposing different spatial and motion cues. Existing comparisons often apply shared processing across representations, leaving it unclear whether their rankings hold after independent tuning. It is also unknown whether rankings and fusion gains generalize across environments and activities, and at what computational cost. Consequently, practitioners lack guidance on which representation and processing suit a given HAR deployment.…

items.title: MOVER: Planning Beyond Motion
items.summary: Residual world models forecast a driving scene through its temporal change, so feature components that stay constant over time vanish from the residual pathway. We ask whether evidence with weak temporal change, such as a waiting pedestrian or a stopped vehicle, can be used more effectively for planning, and introduce MOVER, a complementary event-routing mechanism. A training-time teacher measures how each spatially grounded event query responds when a past frame is removed from shared history and contrasts that sensitivity with the event's pooled temporal residual, prioritizing events that depend on history but receive weak residual evidence. A student predicts the resulting priorities from unperturbed history, so the teacher adds no inference cost.…

items.title: Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA) for Energy Market Settlements: A Machine and Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach
items.summary: The integration of segmented energy markets into Independent System Operators (ISOs) like CAISO and MISO has increased settlement complexity. Automated transaction processing creates challenges for evaluating accuracy, compliance, and financial integrity. Traditional rule-based manual auditing is inefficient, error-prone, and cannot handle the data volume from automated markets.This research proposes Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA), a machine and reinforcement learning framework for settlement auditing via anomaly prioritization. ANNA integrates statistical anomaly detection, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), clustering, and Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning to flag potentially anomalous transactions from historical market data.…

items.title: Nonmonotonic In-Plane Thermal Transport in Metal-Embedded Graphitic Carbon Nitride
items.summary: Embedding metal atoms within the intrinsic cavities of graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) modifies its local bonding and vibrational properties, yet its consequences for lattice thermal transport remain poorly understood. Here, we combine a machine-learned potential (MLP) with homogeneous nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) to investigate in-plane thermal transport in Cu-embedded g-C3N4 across the full range of cavity occupation. The thermal conductivity exhibits a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence on Cu occupation, decreasing at intermediate occupation and partially recovering as the cavities approach full occupation. Frequency-resolved analysis reveals that this behavior originates from the competition between two phonon contributions.…

items.title: Hierarchical randomized neural networks for efficiently and accurately finding multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
items.summary: Being able to find multiple solutions of a semilinear elliptic equation is a fundamental problem in scientific computing. In this paper, fully taking the advantages of randomized neural networks, we propose a new efficient and accurate method for identifying potentially as many solutions as possible. The new method is constructed from three aspects--initialization, optimization, a technique for acceleration and improving accuracy, two of which are innovative developments. Firstly, based on the basis functions of a randomized network and the sampling points, a characteristic matrix is introduced so that its singular value decomposition can be used to determine weakly variant search directions, followed by a newly developed algorithm to generate effective initial candidates. Then the good deflated Gauss-Newton method [see {\em A.…

items.title: Antiphony: A Dual-Process Agent for Deepfake Video Detection with Real-Video Calibration
items.summary: Reliable video deepfake detection requires generalization to unseen generators while limiting false alarms on authentic footage. Although existing detectors capture diverse visual cues, they may produce overconfident errors under generator shift, limiting the reliability of confidence-based fusion. Threshold calibration is further complicated by shifts in authentic capture domains and the lack of future-generator examples. To address these challenges, we present Antiphony, a framework that combines calibrated fusion of four visual experts with selective investigation. Authentic videos serve as a shared reference for score fusion and threshold calibration, enabling threshold updates without target deepfakes. For this expert-fusion stage, we establish finite-sample false-alarm control when the scoring procedure is fixed independently of calibration and authentic samples are exchangeable.…

items.title: inclusionAI/Ling-3.2-air
Performance of attention-based deep-learning models in Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor measurements
items.summary: A systematic performance evaluation of attention-based deep-learning models for wavefront reconstruction in Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor (SHWFS) systems is presented. While deep learning has been extensively applied to pyramid and focal-plane wavefront sensing, its application to standard SHWFS configurations remains relatively underexplored. A simulation dataset consisting of 3.5 million open-loop uncorrelated turbulent phase and image pairs modeled after the Subaru Telescope pupil was generated. The dataset spans four pupil-sampling cases (8$\times$8, 16$\times$16, 20$\times$20, and 32$\times$32 subapertures) under realistic conditions.…

items.title: Differential Proteomics to XAI Rules: A SHAP-FOL-ILP Modeling for Lung Adenocarcinoma
items.summary: Background: We developed an interpretable workflow linking paired differential proteomics, sparse logistic regression, SHAP attribution, and first-order logic (FOL) rule learning in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Methods: We analysed 213 CPTAC-LUAD tissue samples (111 tumour, 102 adjacent-normal) from 111 patients, including 102 matched pairs. Protein effect estimation and testing used the same complete pairs, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Sparse logistic regression used five-fold stratified patient-grouped nested cross-validation. Preprocessing and model selection were confined to training data, with feature selection repeated within inner folds. A separate five-fold patient-grouped evaluation tested SHAP-guided inductive logic programming (FOL/ILP) using training-derived evidence and discretisation. Results: Quality control retained 9,518 proteins.…

items.title: SHAKTI: Evidence-Grounded Conversational AI for Nutrition and Health
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) answer many diet and health questions but can state unsupported claims and cite sources that do not support them. We present SHAKTI (Smart Health Advisor for Knowledge-based Tailored Interventions), a conversational assistant that answers only from retrieved scholarly papers and exact food-composition data, and evaluate it with retrieval, generation, grounding, efficiency and contextawareness metrics. We indexed 484,368,086 OpenAlex works, searched exactly on a GPU for evaluation (10,065 NFCorpus, BioASQ, SciFact and PubMedQA questions) and through a compressed 230-million-abstract index in deployment. On 1,000 stratified questions, we compared single-shot, multi-hop, corrective and deep-research retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with Claude Sonnet.…

items.title: How Relations Impose Embedding-Space Structure
items.summary: Language models are known to encode simple relations, such as synonymy, in the geometry of their representations. It is unclear whether they also encode complex patterns of relationships such as those that drive analogy. We present a simple method, with no learned parameters, based on comparing the internal structural arrangements between disparate domains, to test this. Using our method we find over multiple models that representations are arranged consistently to encode complex relationship similarities. Models align distant representation clouds so that facets of meaning are easily comparable under simple mappings. Our work extends mechanistic accounts of representation space to the relative arrangement of representations that may be only weakly related to one another, showing that representation geometry is far richer than previously thought.…

items.title: Cqlib: A High-Performance Software Stack for Quantum Computing
items.summary: This paper presents Cqlib, a high-performance software stack for quantum computing built around a unified quantum circuit model. Its native Rust core provides efficient implementations of circuit processing, quantum-state and operator computation, compilation, and optimization, while Python and C interfaces support algorithm development and system integration. Cqlib covers quantum program construction, simulation, analysis, compilation, device adaptation, and result processing under consistent program semantics. Through OpenQASM and the Quantum Control Instruction Set (QCIS), Cqlib supports program representation and hardware-oriented execution. Cqlib further provides backend interfaces for device execution, with Cqlib-Tianyan serving as one implementation for QCIS-compatible quantum hardware.…

items.title: TeleMultiStream: An Integrated Robot Teleoperation System with Low-Latency Multi-Stream Video Feedback
items.summary: Training embodied-intelligence models requires large-scale, high-quality demonstration data. Robot teleoperation provides an important means of collecting these data. Low-latency teleoperation also helps human operators take control promptly and provide corrective demonstrations in DAgger-based interactive learning. This paper presents TeleMultiStream, a robot teleoperation system that combines multi-stream WebRTC video feedback with UDP pose downlink. The system supports heterogeneous video sources and uses buffer reuse, bounded queues, and native XR rendering to reduce processing and waiting. In wired-LAN ZED Mini tests, TeleMultiStream's software and high-performance hardware encoding modes achieved dominant-interval Glass-to-Glass latency medians of 60 and 66~ms, respectively. These medians were 26.8\% and 19.5\% lower than the 82-ms RobotVision-PC reference, respectively.…

items.title: Separating Genetic and Protein Evidence in Open Targets: An Auditable Re-ranking Study
items.summary: Biomedical target-ranking platforms combine genetics, literature, experimental evidence, tractability, and clinical precedent because each is useful for target discovery. A single integrated score, however, can be awkward to reuse for a narrower question such as which genes have direct evidence for disease risk or etiology. We examine this issue in Open Targets associations for Alzheimer disease (AD) and Parkinson disease (PD). Genetics-linked evidence and protein-oriented evidence are scored in separate channels and combined only at the end. In AD, the Open Targets overall top 20 contains 7 curated genetics-supported genes and 10 symptomatic pharmacology controls; the default late fusion contains 15 curated genes and no symptomatic controls. In PD, late fusion retains 13 curated genes and removes the 5 symptomatic controls present in the platform top 20.…

items.title: cfahlgren1/tesla-fsd-drive-5min
items.summary: Tesla FSD Drive Five continuous minutes · six cameras · per-frame telemetry Top: left pillar · front · right pillarBottom: left repeater · rear · right repeater Five continuous minutes of a Tesla Model Y (HW4) driving with FSD (Supervised) on suburban roads and a divided highway in daylight.…

items.title: Conartist: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Computer-Using Agents against Multi-Step Prompt Injection
items.summary: Harnesses secure Computer-Using Agents by enforcing security constraints and defending against prompt injection attacks. However, we find that two core security mechanisms of agent harnesses remain vulnerable. First, consistency checking prevents agents from deviating from legitimate user objectives, while attackers can bypass it by embedding malicious actions that appear logically consistent with legitimate task execution. Second, risk auditing proactively examines high-risk operations. Yet, the auditing process itself would introduce additional exploitable actions that violate security boundaries. To evaluate above defects we found, we propose Conartist, a cascaded adaptive prompt injection framework comprising two progressive stages.…

items.title: When Learned IDS Model Selection Collapses to a Static Choice: A Measurement Study at the Edge
items.summary: Runtime model selection trades detection quality against energy and latency. However, comparing a selector only with a more costly static detector conflates detector choice with the benefit of adaptation. We present a framework for analysis and physical measurement that combines a pairwise reward criterion, matched static controls, paired blocks, a fixed load-prevalence factorial design, and reporting of actions outside training support. On one Raspberry Pi 4B with four frozen TON-IoT detectors, tabular Q-learning and a deep Q-network (DQN) both select LightLR throughout. A retrospective audit using validation data only rules out preference reversals for MedRF versus LightLR and HeavyMLP versus LightLR. However, TinyDT has a higher reward than LightLR in seven of the 2,500 windows, so the audit does not establish global LightLR optimality.…

items.title: Structure-Exploiting Hierarchical Retrieval for Long Narrative Documents: A Precision-Oriented Alternative to Learned Abstraction Trees
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation over book-length documents must locate a small, coherent set of passages inside tens of thousands of tokens. Flat dense retrieval ignores document structure; RAPTOR instead builds a hierarchy by recursively clustering and summarizing with a language model. We study a complementary design that exploits the native structure of a document: a two-level retriever that (i) selects chapters with a hybrid BM25+dense match over chapter recaps, (ii) runs a chapter-filtered dense search, and (iii) expands top passages into contiguous, section-aware spans under a token budget, plus content-hash-gated delta ingestion to keep the index cheap to update. We evaluate on five public-domain books (113 chapter-localization queries) and on QuALITY and NovelQA (200K+ token novels).…

items.title: When Should We Trust Medical Image Models? Evaluating Confidence Reliability under Cross-Dataset Shift
items.summary: Deep learning models for chest X-ray analysis often achieve strong performance on benchmark datasets, but their reliability under cross-dataset deployment remains unclear. In clinical practice, models trained in one hospital system may be applied to data from another, where distributional and labeling differences can affect both prediction accuracy and model confidence. We conduct a controlled empirical study of model confidence under cross-dataset transfer. We train ResNet-50 and DenseNet-121 on CheXpert and evaluate them on MIMIC-CXR across five experimental settings, focusing on Pneumothorax and Pleural Effusion. We measure predictive performance using AUC and confidence reliability using Expected Calibration Error (ECE), Brier score, and average confidence on incorrect predictions, all reported with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.…

items.title: SAGE-Drive: Benefit-Aware Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving Planning
items.summary: Explicit reasoning enables autonomous vehicles (AVs) to interpret complex traffic interactions and support trajectory planning, but introduces additional computational demands. Determining when explicit reasoning can improve planning accuracy remains a key challenge, as its benefits vary across driving scenarios. To address this challenge, this study proposes Scene-Adaptive Gating of Explicit Reasoning for Driving (SAGE-Drive), a benefit-aware adaptive reasoning framework for autonomous driving planning. First, paired planning outcomes with and without explicit reasoning are analyzed to measure the reasoning benefit, i.e., the reduction in planning error achieved by explicit reasoning, which serves as the supervision label.…

items.title: LLM-Assisted Software Migration: from Module-Level Transformation to Repository-Level Integration
items.summary: Software migration adapts an existing implementation to a new language, version, API, framework, or platform while preserving its behavior. Large language models (LLMs) succeed on individual functions and modules, but this success does not readily carry over to entire repositories, particularly deployable applications. This survey reviews LLM-assisted migration from module-level transformation to repository-level integration, culminating in the delivery of complete applications. We analyze 96 sources---including 46 direct migration papers---across four perspectives: (1) supported software engineering activities, (2) model roles as editors or orchestrators, (3) orchestration workflows (agentless, single-agent, or multi-agent), and (4) enabling techniques including knowledge engineering, project context, environment feedback, and model adaptation.…

items.title: SAEPO: Sparse-Autoencoder-Guided Credit Assignment for Policy Optimization
items.summary: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has demonstrated strong performance in improving large language model (LLM) reasoning, yet its credit-assignment signal remains coarse. Outcome verifiers provide scalable supervision by judging whether a completed response is correct, but they do not directly indicate which intermediate reasoning tokens contribute to success or failure. As a result, policy optimization can be inefficient, especially when training base models directly from sparse outcome feedback. In this paper, we introduce SAEPO, a Sparse AutoEncoder-guided token-level credit assignment method for outcome-supervised Policy Optimization.…

items.title: GABIF: An Adaptive Guided Graph Denoising Framework for Antibody Conditional Inverse Folding
items.summary: Antibodies play a central role in the human immune system, and their design is critical for vaccine development, therapeutic intervention, and improving human longevity. However, the vast combinatorial search space of antibodies poses a fundamental challenge for de novo discovery. Recent advances in deep learning, particularly denoising diffusion models, have demonstrated strong potential in protein inverse folding. Nevertheless, existing approaches are largely constrained to learning from natural antibody repertoires, thereby generating sequences that closely resemble natural antibodies. Such similarity, however, does not necessarily translate into improved functional performance in downstream applications.…

items.title: Benchmarking VLM Medical Hallucination across 5 Modalities
items.summary: Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) within the medical domain remain a difficult and not well-understood problem, and it is still unclear where these models break down. Although several benchmarks targeting medical hallucination have been introduced, they often lack broad coverage across different medical imaging modalities. We introduce Multi-Med, a medical hallucination benchmark containing 1,000 image-question pairs spanning five distinct modalities. Using this benchmark, we perform an in-depth experimental study of 10 widely used VLMs across five modalities and four question categories. Our findings indicate that model performance differs substantially depending on the imaging modality and question type, and that the differences among the best-performing models are not statistically significant.

items.title: Beyond PINNs: Boundary-Enriched Holomorphic Networks for Laplace Problems
items.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations by penalizing their residual, but this formulation can be difficult to optimize for solutions with singular behaviour. We focus specifically on the two-dimensional Laplace equation, whose strong analytical structure allows the governing equation to be enforced directly in the neural representation. We compare a hybrid harmonic-neural model with a holomorphic neural network whose output is harmonic by construction and therefore requires only boundary training. We further enrich the holomorphic model with singular functions chosen according to the interior angle and boundary conditions at each junction of boundary segments. On six singular benchmarks, the enriched model is the most accurate of the neural models we compare.…

items.title: SpectralRoute: Adaptive Spectral Routing for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Hyperspectral Segmentation
items.summary: Open-vocabulary semantic segmentation enables the recognition of arbitrary categories through natural language descriptions and has recently been extended from natural images to remote sensing. However, existing approaches primarily focus on three-channel optical imagery or limited-band multispectral data, while pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) struggle to directly exploit the rich spectral information of hyperspectral imagery (HSI) without additional adaptation. More importantly, different land-cover categories rely on distinct spectral cues, which may be weakened by uniform fusion. To address these challenges, we propose SpectralRoute, a training-free framework for open-vocabulary hyperspectral segmentation.…

items.title: TidyFlow: Geometry-Aware Tabletop Arrangement Generation with Human-Aligned Tidiness Evaluation
items.summary: Generating tidy tabletop arrangements that align with human organizational preferences requires considering both functional relationships among objects and geometric constraints within limited tabletop space. We present TidyFlow, a tabletop arrangement generation framework that integrates conditional Flow Matching with topology-aware geometric refinement. We construct two tabletop arrangement datasets based on functional grouping and geometric constraints, namely General Tabletop Layouts (GTL) and Workstation Tabletop Layouts (WTL), and introduce a six-dimensional tidiness scoring function. Conditional Flow Matching is employed to learn a multimodal distribution of target arrangements conditioned on object attributes and tabletop geometry.…

items.title: Autonomous Multireference Quantum Chemistry with Artificial Intelligence Agents
items.summary: Accurately describing chemical reactions that involve strongly correlated electrons remains a major challenge in computational chemistry. Multireference electronic structure methods can address this challenge, but their application requires expert decisions that are di!cult to automate, particularly when the electronic structure changes as chemical bonds form and break. Here we introduce CASPER, an autonomously agentic workflow that performs multireference calculations along chemical reaction pathways. CASPER combines chemical knowledge, electronic structure calculations, and iterative assessment to identify chemically meaningful active spaces and maintain their consistency as bonds form and break. We demonstrate its capabilities on five transition-metal reactions, for which CASPER generates consistent multireference potential energy profiles with minimal human intervention.…

items.title: Segment Anything In-Context via Visual Demonstrations
items.summary: We present the Segment Anything Model via Visual Demonstrations (SAYD), a foundation model for in-context segmentation. Given visual demos comprising prompt images and their segmentation masks, SAYD segments coherent regions (e.g., objects or their parts) in a query image by establishing visual correspondences between the prompts and the query. SAYD generalizes to previously-unseen segmentation tasks, including those requiring tacit visual knowledge or involving concepts that are difficult to articulate unambiguously in language. We train SAYD on 12 public datasets originally curated for panoptic segmentation using our proposed techniques, including a lightweight mask decoder for prompt-agnostic mask generation and a learning mechanism for recognizing novel query classes absent in the prompts. These innovations enhance both computational efficiency and out-of-domain generalization.…

items.title: Second-Order Dynamics in Noisy RNNs Produce Exploration and Temporal Compression in Replay
items.summary: Biological neural networks (like the hippocampus) can internally generate "replay" resembling stimulus-driven activity. Recent computational models of replay use noisy recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained to path-integrate. Replay in these networks is described as Langevin sampling, but this theory alone fails to capture the environmental exploration and temporal compression observed in real biological replay. To close this gap, we re-examine spontaneous noisy RNN activity ("replay") as Langevin sampling, one timestep at a time, from a time-series distribution resembling lived experiences (unlike previous works which defined sampling as Monte Carlo inference over a static distribution).…

items.title: Particle Belief Representations for Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability
items.summary: Particle filters flexibly represent complex, multimodal beliefs but expose them as weighted, unordered sets incompatible with conventional fixed-dimensional policies. We study particle-belief encodings as inputs to reinforcement-learning policies while holding belief estimation and policy optimization fixed. We compare statistical summaries, cumulant-generating-function (CGF) features, and permutation-invariant set encoders. Trainable encoders are learned end-to-end or pretrained through belief reconstruction or task-specific prediction. Across eight tasks, pooling-based set encoders and gradient CGF features are reliable end-to-end, while the Set Transformer achieves the highest performance with appropriate pretraining.…

items.title: Towards Agentic Video Corpus Moment Retrieval
items.summary: Video corpus moment retrieval (VCMR) requires finding the video and time interval that match a text query in a corpus of videos. We present RELAY, a training-free framework for VCMR that shares memory across queries. RELAY processes a batch of queries in three stages: search with a query bank, ranking with video notes, and localization with video prompt caching. In the search stage, an embedding model scores each video by its best-matching frame. The query bank penalizes videos that score highly for many other queries in the batch. In the ranking stage, a vision-language model (VLM) writes notes on each candidate video's scenes, people, objects, and actions once. Then, a large language model (LLM) reranks the candidates from these notes. In the localization stage, a VLM predicts the time interval of the moment in the top-ranked video.…

items.title: Weight Averaging at Small Budgets Confounds Formula-Labeled Pretraining in Microstructure-Property Regression: A Pre-Specified Study with Post Hoc Rechecks
items.summary: Closed-form physics formulas can label synthetic microstructures at no cost, so supervised pretraining on those labels is an alternative to self-supervised pretraining when labels are scarce. One pre-specified protocol tests this on two public simulated benchmarks, two-phase conductivity and short-fiber stiffness: a ConvNeXt-Small is pretrained on 150,000 synthetic images by formula regression or masked reconstruction and fine-tuned on 100, 400, or 1,600 labels. Five fine-tuning seeds from one formula checkpoint have mean residual correlations of 0.994 (conductivity) and 0.999 (stiffness). On conductivity the formula network compresses its predictions (slope 0.64) and has four times the 400-label error of ImageNet initialization.…

items.title: ProMix: Efficient Data Mixture Optimization for Robotic Imitation via Proxy-Reference DRO
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel in open-world manipulation, yet their performance often saturates when training data are naively pooled across heterogeneous robots, tasks, and environments. Distributionally robust data mixture optimization, exemplified by Re-Mix, can recover much of this performance, but its weight search requires training full-scale policies twice on the entire corpus, placing it out of reach for most laboratories. We present ProMix, a compute-efficient instantiation of the proxy-reference DRO recipe for robotic imitation learning: a 15M-parameter proxy learns per-domain sampling weights by minimizing worst-case excess loss against a frozen reference model, and the learned weights transfer, without re-tuning, to VLA backbones up to 7B parameters.…

items.title: Arcadian: Open-Source Humanoid Ecosystem for Accessible and Customizable Research and Education
items.summary: Reproducing and modifying a meter-scale humanoid remains challenging for research and teaching groups with limited fabrication resources and engineering support. This paper presents Arcadian, an open-source humanoid ecosystem that offers accessible and customizable humanoid hardware and software with community support. Arcadian aims to strike a balance among cost-effectiveness, structural durability, and full customizability, lowering the barrier to entry for research and education. Specifically, this meter-scale humanoid adopts metal-embedded 3D printing to achieve a high strength-to-cost ratio, eliminating the need for computer numerical control (CNC) machining while retaining design flexibility.…

items.title: Semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Flash on H5N1 One Health questions
items.summary: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) has re-emerged as a One Health concern since 2024, and the public is increasingly consulting large-language-model (LLM) chatbots for health information during outbreaks. Before a chatbot's accuracy can be meaningfully assessed, its consistency must first be understood, so that any single response can be trusted as a fair representative of the model's behavior. We characterized the semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 (OpenAI) and Gemini 3 Flash (Google) on 15 H5N1 One Health questions sourced from social media discourse by adopting and extending a centroid-based evaluation framework. Each question was submitted 30 times and reformulated using five Chain-of-Thought (CoT) variants with 30 runs each, yielding 5,400 responses.…

items.title: World Models Are the Right Foundation for Simulating Mars Terraforming
items.summary: Terraforming Mars is a long-horizon, action-conditioned control problem that requires predicting atmospheric responses to interventions over centuries to identify effective policies. This position paper argues that physics-regularized recurrent state-space world models are the most promising foundation for this setting. Data-driven climate emulators lack action-conditioning, and physics-based general circulation models (GCMs) are too expensive for policy search. Among learned world models, recurrent state-space architectures with physics constraints are better suited than transformer-based alternatives: they provide native uncertainty quantification through their stochastic-deterministic decomposition, remain stable under sparse non-terrestrial training data, and enforce physical consistency at each rollout step.…

items.title: Landscape and Taxonomy of Prompt Engineering Patterns in Software Engineering
items.summary: Advancements in large language models (LLMs) have enhanced their ability to handle ambiguous user instructions. However, effective prompt patterns remain crucial for usability and comprehension. This article presents a taxonomy of prompt engineering patterns for software engineering. It is based on a systematic literature review that was conducted in early 2023, when LLMs still faced significant limitations in context length and inference capabilities. Our study explores techniques that enhance the usability and reliability of LLMs, emphasizing the ongoing importance of well-designed prompts in optimizing task performance. Our findings highlight the critical role of prompt patterns in maximizing LLM's potential, even as their capabilities continue to evolve.

items.title: GlobalHRBench: Does Changing the Question Language Change the Legal Answer?
items.summary: Language matters when deploying LLM agents across borders, especially in law, where the governing rules must hold across working languages. Does changing the language of a legal question change answer accuracy? We introduce GlobalHRBench, pairing 240 employment-law problems across eight jurisdictions and eight languages while fixing facts, applicable law and required conclusions. We evaluate nine models on all 1,920 prompts in independent, closed-book, single-answer trials, scoring legal correctness, completeness and answer-language compliance. GPT-6.1 Sol leads at 76.2% strict passes, with a 5.8% relative best-to-worst language decline, compared with 42.2% for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Kimi K3.1 Pro and Claude Sonnet 5.5 reverse order between English and Chinese.…

items.title: Circle-Pattern Linear Systems for the Twenty Trivalent Delaunay Types of a Genus-Two Surface: Rank, Feasibility and Polytope Dimension
items.summary: The hyperelliptic quotient of a closed genus-two Riemann surface is a hyperbolic sphere with six cone points of angle pi. Its Delaunay triangulation T is dual to a trivalent Voronoi graph G of one of twenty combinatorial types. For each type we study the angle system Ax = 1, x >= 0, where A is the vertex-edge incidence matrix of T and pi x_e is the angle subtended at a cone point by the Voronoi edge dual to e, equivalently the intersection angle of the two circumcircles adjacent across e. We prove that rank A = 6 for all twenty types, including the six whose triangulation has a loop, so the affine solution space always has the dimension of Teichmuller space. The polytope P = {Ax = 1, x >= 0} behaves differently. It is six-dimensional for exactly ten types, the ten Delaunay-realizable ones.…

items.title: MobileGrail: Learning Compact Guardrails for On-Device deployable Mobile GUI Agent Safety
items.summary: Runtime guardrails protect mobile GUI agents by assessing each proposed action before execution, but existing guardrails rely on cloud hosted large multimodal models, exposing every screen to a remote server, including private information such as payments, messages, and medical records. We propose MobileGrail, an on-device deployable model that addresses both. It maintains a recurrent task state that retains only the evidence subsequent safety decisions depend on, so that authorization and execution progress persist beyond the short context. To intervene early while keeping the safety boundary precise, it learns two labels, unsafe and block: unsafe marks the action that commits a violation, whereas block may be issued at any step of an intervention window, which spans from the first action that the user's authorization no longer explains to the committing action itself.…

items.title: The Temporal Residual: Fast and Effective Retrofitting of Latent Feedback into Pretrained Language Models
items.summary: A transformer language model computes a deep hidden state for every token but uses it only to sample that token. Existing latent-feedback designs, which feed hidden states back across tokens, are mostly built in during pretraining and gain little when added to a pretrained model. We introduce the temporal residual, a second residual stream that every sublayer reads and writes and that is carried from each token to the next. It adds 2,752 parameters to a 4.2B-parameter model and starts exactly at the pretrained network. Retrofitted onto Qwen3.5-4B-Base with 5B tokens of training, it beats a standard model trained on the same data by 7, 13 and 5 points on AIME 2024, AIME 2025 and AMC 2023, writes shorter solutions, and stays ahead at matched training compute.…

items.title: Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN): A Universal Primitive for Continuous-Time Spatiotemporal Learning
items.summary: Conventional artificial neurons separate spatial feature aggregation from continuous physical time, limiting their ability to model irregular observations. We introduce the Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neuron (DAWIN), a continuous-time primitive for replacing standard neural layers in MLPs, Transformers, and graph neural networks. DAWIN couples spatial projection with elapsed-time-dependent wave excitation and integrates it into a local complex state through closed-form damped evolution, avoiding numerical differential equation solvers. We show that DAWIN generalizes static sinusoidal and memoryless wave neurons on interval-augmented inputs, derive closed-form gradients, and establish bounded-input bounded-output stability for positive damping and sampling intervals bounded away from zero.…

items.title: Pretrained Tabular Features and the Measurement of Financial Proximity
items.summary: Spatial arbitrage pricing theory (S-APT) extends factor models to allow returns to spill over between connected firms, beyond what common risk factors explain. In recent years, tabular foundation models (TFMs) have matched or outperformed tuned gradient-boosted and bagged ensembles on small and medium-sized tabular benchmarks. Although their predictive performance is strong, these models reveal little about what they have learned, which limits their use in regulated financial applications that require explanation. Internal representations are widely used to probe what neural networks learn and to measure similarity.…
items.tldr: Using frozen internal representations of tabular foundation models as financial dissimilarity measures in a spatial asset-pricing model yields positive estimated gains over direct disclosure distance once broad SEC filing data are included.

items.title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) that continue improving after deployment (e.g., recursive self-improvement) offer a promising path toward general intelligence. Current test-time methods pursue this goal on unlabeled questions, primarily relying on self-consistency: they generate independent solutions and use majority voting to select an answer or construct training targets. This leaves earlier reasoning unused at inference and can reinforce an incorrect majority during training. Humans instead build on earlier attempts to preserve useful reasoning, correct mistakes and improve their problem-solving strategies.…
items.tldr: A label-free test-time framework, TT-RSI, improves large language models by repeatedly re-solving questions with prior solutions and distilling refinements into model weights, outperforming self-consistency methods under the same test-time scaling budget.

items.title: Speak When You See It: Proactive Task Assistants Should Wait for Evidence, Not the Clock
items.summary: Proactive assistants that guide people through physical tasks must decide, every few seconds, whether a step is complete and whether a mistake has occurred. We find that two benchmarks for this task largely reward knowing when rather than seeing what: a timer that never looks at the video, raising an alarm at 25 s and confirming each step at 30 s, reaches a mistake F1 of 0.373 on Ego-MC-Bench, above every published result (at most 0.27). We formalize this as the video-blind frontier, the best trade-off between completion accuracy and mistake F1 that policies reach from the elapsed time, the instruction and training statistics alone: every published per-step result on Ego-MC-Bench lies inside it, and so do all twelve zero-shot models we run on QICD.…

items.title: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design
items.summary: The physical world is open-ended, dynamic, and partially observable. While foundation models have advanced embodied intelligence, standalone models struggle with long-horizon execution, and simply integrating models with agents may lead to inconsistencies between planning and physical control. To support reliable and adaptive behaviors in the physical world, we introduce Innata-0, a native embodied world system. Innata-0 jointly designs an embodied world-action model and an agent to combine their complementary strengths. The model, Innata-0-WAM, adopts a tri-tower Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that integrates understanding, prediction, and action generation. The agent, Innata-0-Agent, coordinates long-horizon execution through memory, verification, and recovery.…
items.tldr: Innata-0 is a native embodied world system that co-designs a world-action model and an agent to enable reliable long-horizon physical behaviors through integrated understanding, prediction, action generation, memory, verification, and recovery.

items.title: RoomTokens: Masked Diffusion over Structured Tokens for Indoor Scene Synthesis
items.summary: Generating 3D indoor scenes requires a representation that captures object semantics, instance identity, height structure, and orientation while respecting room geometry. Methods that model scenes as sequences of object vectors learn spatial constraints implicitly, leaving collisions and boundary violations to losses or post-processing; semantic-map methods make occupancy explicit, but collapse instance and directional structure. We introduce RoomTokens, a sliced structured-token representation in which each token stores semantic class, instance-color identity, and facing field. This representation allows a scene to be generated as a discrete grid while preserving cues for instance grouping, orientation estimation, and 3D extent prediction.…

items.title: UUBench: Understanding the Unspoken toward Full-Duplex Multimodal Interaction
items.summary: Effective real-time, full-duplex multimodal interaction requires systems to understand not only what users say, but also the communicative needs conveyed through prosody, facial expressions, gestures, and context, and to generate audiovisual responses that appropriately address those needs. Existing evaluations offer limited insight into whether systems translate an understanding of such unspoken needs into effective responses. We introduce UUBench, a benchmark for assessing how well multimodal interactive systems Understand the Unspoken intent and address users' implicit communicative needs. The inherent subjectivity of implicit intent inference poses a key challenge for evaluation. To address this, we introduce Process-Oriented Scoring, which grounds the assessment of intent fulfillment in observable auditory and visual cues, such as prosody and gestures.…
items.tldr: UUBench assesses how well multimodal interactive systems understand and respond to users' implicit communicative needs through process- and outcome-oriented scoring grounded in observable audiovisual evidence.

items.title: LeadVLA: Learning Follower-Aware Route Execution for Robot Leading
items.summary: Robot leading requires executing a route while continuously adapting to a designated follower. Existing robot-leading systems often mediate follower understanding and physical route execution through explicit states, planners, or modular interfaces; directly learning this coupling through end-to-end trajectory prediction can instead entangle route execution with follower response. We introduce LeadVLA, a structured multimodal policy that preserves the route as an explicit Path reference while learning a Pace for route progress and a Residual for local follower- and scene-conditioned adaptation.…
items.tldr: LeadVLA is a structured multimodal policy that separates route execution into explicit path, pace, and residual components, trained and evaluated with generated closed-loop data and a benchmark, achieving the highest success among tested robot policies and transferring to unseen real environments…

items.title: Escriba-OCR: A 1B Vision-Language Model for Error-Preserving Transcription of Handwritten Portuguese Essays
items.summary: Feedback tools and research on learner writing need transcriptions of handwritten essays that keep exactly what the student wrote: misspellings, line breaks, struck-through words and insertions. Vision-language models (VLMs) read handwriting well, but they also tend to rewrite it into correct language. We measure this on BRESSAY, 1,000 handwritten Brazilian Portuguese essays, with a benchmark that adds error preservation, invented errors, edit-markup precision and recall and line structure to the character error rate (CER) and uses paired bootstrap confidence intervals. We restrict the study to open-weight models that schools can run on their own hardware.…

items.title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
items.summary: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overhead. We present Motion Mamba 2.0, a Mamba-based root-body diffusion architecture that integrates local attention, resumable recurrent states, and persistent content memory (PCM) for long-horizon controllable motion generation. PCM transforms compressed motion history from Mamba recurrent states, together with state changes and text-conditioned features, into dynamically updated content slots accessible to local attention.…

items.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
items.summary: Animating arbitrary 3D assets from instructions requires both structural inference and motion control, yet existing motion benchmarks mostly cover conventional human or animal skeletons with simple instructions. We introduce DivDynBench, which evaluates rigging and motion generation across six morphology categories, with instructions requiring multi-phase part coordination and explicit timing, angle, repetition, and trajectory constraints. With large language models, we systematically compare three common paradigms: specialized motion generation, video generation followed by motion recovery, and direct agent-driven generation. We analyze their control capabilities, cross-morphology adaptability, and generation costs.…
items.tldr: A new benchmark evaluates rigging and motion generation across six 3D morphology categories, compares specialized, video-based, and agent-driven paradigms, and proposes an agentic framework that writes compact parametric skeleton and motion programs executed deterministically for reliable control.

items.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based Experience Reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed interactions, while Recursive Harness Self-Improvement refines operational guidance across successive attempts.…
items.tldr: A dual-agent framework with hierarchical memory and recursive self-improvement enables robotic manipulation agents to convert execution evidence into reusable guidance without updating model parameters.

items.title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?
items.summary: Robot policies must adapt to the speed of moving objects, yet existing benchmarks rarely measure this ability across diverse tasks and speeds. We introduce SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks spanning 16 skill categories, each evaluated at 13 belt speeds (0.10-0.40 m/s). Objects are transported through physical contact with a visibly moving belt. Each task has a static counterpart, and each evaluation episode uses the same randomized scene at all 13 speeds. We fine-tune eight vision-language-action and world-action models on demonstrations spanning the full speed range, comparing observations from the current frame alone with those including two past frames.…
items.tldr: A simulation benchmark shows that robot manipulation policies often fail at non-average conveyor speeds, while past frames or speed inputs improve models when speed is linearly decodable.

items.title: Decoding Cortical Precursors of Evoked and Spontaneous Pupil Dilation
items.summary: Pupil dilation reflects arousal and occurs both in response to sensory events and spontaneously. However, whether these two forms of dilation are preceded by distinct cortical dynamics remains unclear. Here, we combined pupillometry, wide-field Ca2+; imaging in mice, and explainable machine learning to estimate cortical activity patterns that predict pupil dilation. Evoked dilation was examined during somatosensory, visual pattern, and visual context stimulations, and spontaneous dilation was analyzed using a public resting state dataset. Independent components of cortical activity were used as inputs to recurrent neural network (RNN) decoders. When sessions with pre-existing dilation were excluded, the decoders predicted evoked dilation above that of the shuffled-label controls.…

items.title: NeuroMetaBench: Expert-curated benchmark for evaluating automated neuroimaging meta-analysis
items.summary: Automated neuroimaging meta-analysis is widely used to generate hypotheses and interpret findings, reducing the time and effort required for manual literature searches and evidence curation. However, how closely these methods recover effortful expert-curated syntheses has not been established. We present NeuroMetaBench, an openly available benchmark linking expert curation records across stages of systematic review, from author-stated eligibility criteria and research-article inclusion decisions to individual analysis selections and meta-analysis-specific reference maps. The resource includes bibliographic records for 1,611 research-article inclusions across 17 quantitative review articles and candidate search pools for three.…

items.title: Computational model for Rumination as Self-Supervised Learning in a World Model
items.summary: Rumination is a cognitive process characterized by repetitive negative thoughts that persist even in the absence of external threats. Although excessive rumination is associated with stress-related mental disorders, the computational mechanisms underlying its persistence and its impact on threat perception remain unclear. Here, we propose a computational framework in which rumination emerges from recursive learning within a world model. Inspired by the social defeat stress (SDS) paradigm in mice, our model assumes that direct experiences of social defeat first establish beliefs about the threat posed by an aggressor. These beliefs subsequently generate internally simulated experiences, which are repeatedly used to update the beliefs themselves.…

items.title: Machine Learning-based Transcriptomic Data Analysis of Long COVID Patients: Generating Hypotheses for Molecular Signatures
items.summary: Introduction: Long COVID (LC) remains a global public-health challenge, affecting an estimated 10-30% of COVID-19-survivors. Machine learning (ML) can help identify molecular features associated with LC. Human ion channels (HICs), that regulate immune-cell signaling and cellular homeostasis, may contribute to LC-associated processes and offer insights into relevant pathways and potential drug-repurposing candidates. Methodology: RNA-seq data from COVID-19-recovered and LC patients across six datasets were integrated, preprocessed, and corrected for batch effects. Supervised ML models were evaluated using leave-one-batch-out validation, with SHAP identifying features across validation folds. Functional enrichment, host-host and host-viral protein-protein interaction analyses were performed, followed by drug interaction analysis of potential HICs within the resulting interactome.…

items.title: Machine learning prediction of antimicrobial resistance in respiratory metagenomes
items.summary: Background: Targeted therapy for patients with suspected respiratory infections traditionally requires bacterial culture followed by phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), a process that can take up to 5 days. In acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), delays in identifying the causative pathogen and its resistance profile may be especially harmful because patients are critically ill and often receive broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics. The growing burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) further complicates clinical decision-making by reducing effective treatment options and increasing the risk of inadequate initial therapy. Culture-free, AI-driven computational metagenomic strategies have the potential to drastically shorten this window, enabling more rapid targeted therapy prescription.…

items.title: A2Holo: Dual-Stream Flow Matching of 3D Structure and a Protein Language Model for Conformational Transition Prediction
items.summary: Modelling a ligand-bound holo conformation from a ligand-free apo conformation is essential in structure-based drug discovery. We present A2Holo, which casts apo-to-holo prediction as flow matching between two experimental structures rather than generation from noise. It transplants the dual-stream joint attention of in-context image generation to residue-aligned protein language model embeddings and structure. Without ligand conditioning or stochastic sampling, A2Holo's single deterministic trajectory reaches a median C RMSD of 0.809 [A] on the D3PM benchmark, the lowest among existing methods. Its TM-score exceeds even the best of 10 samples from every stochastic baseline on at least 144 of 150 pairs. Beyond performance, we directly measure the transplanted multimodal mechanism itself.…

items.title: Dependence-Aware Conformal Prediction for 3D Uncertainty Quantification in Molecular Docking
items.summary: Molecular docking plays a critical role in drug discovery by predicting three-dimensional (3D) binding poses of small molecules within proteins. However, docking predictions can contain substantial positional errors, making reliable uncertainty quantification essential. Conformal prediction (CP) provides a principled framework for uncertainty quantification, yet constructing compact 3D prediction regions with reliable joint coverage remains challenging due to heterogeneous atomic errors, dependence among spatial coordinates, and distribution shifts. We develop a dependence-aware CP framework for molecular docking that leverages a shared graph neural network (GNN) to estimate adaptive, asymmetric uncertainty intervals using local atomic and global molecular information.…

items.title: The IGVF Catalog Knowledge Graph
items.summary: The Impact of Genomic Variation on Function (IGVF) consortium is systematically characterizing how genomic variation influences regulatory elements, gene expression, and human phenotypes through thousands of experimental mapping and perturbation datasets alongside predictive models. To synthesize these diverse results into quantitative relationships and situate them within established biological knowledge, we developed the IGVF Catalog, a large-scale knowledge graph. Implemented in ArangoDB using schema-validated JSON records. Version 1.3 encompasses nearly 3 billion nodes across 14 entity types (including variants, coding variants, genomic elements, genes, transcripts, proteins, pathways, and ontology graphs for biosamples and phenotypes) connected by more than 8.6 billion edges across 31 relationship types.…

items.title: How predictable is an individual's DNA methylation?
items.summary: DNA methylation is largely shared among individuals of the same cell type, yet at specific genomic sites it differs substantially between individuals. Methods that predict methylation are usually evaluated by their accuracy over all sites. Because methylation at most sites is shared, this accuracy cannot show whether a method predicts an individual's methylation where individuals differ. We present individual-level methylation prediction at sites where individuals differ as a new challenge. Given the reference genome sequence, the methylation of other individuals of the same cell type, and measurements at some sites of a target individual, but not the individual's genotype, the task is to predict the target individual's methylation class (unmethylated, intermediate, or methylated) at the remaining sites.…

items.title: Deciphering state bridges via a single-cell large language model
items.summary: Large-scale single-cell transcriptomic data provide a new avenue for precision medicine by uncovering cellular heterogeneity. However, systematic comparison of remodeling patterns across various biological states remains unavailable. Here, we first developed a computational framework based on a foundation model of single cell biology, Universal Cell Embedding (UCE), to harmonize annotations comprising 36 cell types. Based on an integrated dataset of single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with 8,789 human samples comprising more than 59 million cells or nuclei across 614 biological states, we then embedded each state with a 36-dimensional vector in a unified space of cell-composition change and further deciphered states bridges by analyzing the relationships among the 614 state vectors. As a result, 22,161 significant bridges (P < 0.05) between the 614 states were revealed.…

items.title: Genomic foundation models and complementary variant-scoring strategies in LGMD-associated genes: architecture, adaptation, and sequence context
items.summary: Genomic foundation models learn representations from DNA sequence, although their usefulness for variant classification depends on the architecture and downstream evaluation procedure. We compared six genomic foundation models using 6,960 ClinVar single-nucleotide variants from ten limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD)-associated genes, with 4,866 variants assigned to training and 2,094 to held-out testing. The analyses included frozen alternate-minus-reference embeddings at 101, 201 and 501 bp, supervised adaptation at 101 bp, and gene-held-out downstream classifier training. GPN-Star V100 and AlphaGenome Atlas AVI were evaluated separately using their native scores. At 101 bp, frozen Evo2 achieved the highest discrimination among the six foundation models (MCC 0.644; AUROC 0.879; AUPRC 0.818).…

items.title: deeprok: highly accurate prokaryotic gene prediction through deep learning and overlap-aware decoding
items.summary: Prokaryotic gene prediction is often considered solved, yet widely used tools still disagree on many genes, chiefly short genes and translation starts. We present deeprok, an ab initio prokaryotic gene prediction method that combines a base-level neural network with an overlap-aware decoder, and refines start-site predictions with a self-trained neural ranker. On four curated genomes distant from its training data, deeprok made 10-18% fewer exact-match errors than Prodigal and GeneMarkS-2, and on 2,925 experimentally verified starts it made 21-41% fewer start errors. Furthermore, deeprok's base-level architecture reveals lineage-specific translation initiation signals. These results show that per-base deep learning combined with overlap-aware decoding can improve prokaryotic gene prediction, especially for resolving translation starts.

items.title: Integrating CRISPRi perturbation responses and transcription-factor binding priors for regulatory network inference in triple-negative breast cancer
items.summary: Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) represents an aggressive breast cancer subtype that lacks actionable cell-surface receptors, restricting frontline systemic management to cytotoxic chemotherapy. While recent functional epigenomics shows that TNBC progression is governed by non-coding regulatory remodeling at distal super-enhancers, conventional Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) inference methods rely on observational transcriptomic co-expression, which suffers from technical dropouts and confounding correlations that inflate false discoveries (>30%).…

items.title: Vir2vec: A Genome-Wide Viral Embedding
items.summary: Genomic language models (gLMs) enable the extraction of meaningful numerical representations from DNA sequences, yet existing approaches primarily focus on human genomes or limited viral datasets, and systematic evaluations of viral representations remain scarce.
