Here, we introduce Vir2vec, a family of decoder-only gLMs (from 17M to 422M parameters) continually pretrained on a curated viral corpus comprising 565,747 complete genomes and genomic segment records assigned to 295 different species. We also present the viral Genome Understanding Evaluation (vGUE), a seven-task evaluation suite assessing viral representations across broad organism discrimination, evolutionary signatures, intra-genus species classification, variant subtyping, and host-associated phenotypes.…

items.title: RAxML-NG 2: Automatic model selection, novel tree search heuristics, and fast branch support metrics
items.summary: RAxML-NG is a widely used tool for maximum likelihood based phylogenetic inference. In the seven years since the last RAxML-NG publication, we have continuously improved and extended the code. Here, we describe the next major release, RAxML-NG 2.0. It introduces a plethora of new features: integrated model testing, multiple fast branch support metrics, automatic parallelization tuning, phylogenetic difficulty prediction, genotype evolution models, to name but the most important ones. Furthermore, we introduce two novel search heuristics at production code level: the adaptive difficulty-aware heuristic (default) and the fast mode with early-stopping that prevents over-optimization.…

items.title: Modeling Host-Virus Interactions of Avian Corona Virus Reveals Cytokine Feedback as a driver of Strain-Specific Immune Response
items.summary: The interplay between RNA viral dynamics and innate immunity remains poorly understood, mainly because RNA viruses trigger highly nonlinear cytokine responses. We address this using infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a major poultry pathogen, as a model system. We developed a set of mathematical models and compared those with experimental data from two IBV strains infecting chicken macrophages.By model fitting and supervised Machine Learning we reveal that positive feedback in interferon- production is essential to reproduce the dynamics of one IBV strain but likely absent in the other. We further provide strain-specific estimations of key parameters such as infection rates, production and decay rates of virus and cytokine levels. Notably, different strains produced distinctive cytokine profiles, highlighting feedback as a key determinant of strain-specific immune signatures.…

items.title: Population-level learning of non-additive effects enables accurate and efficient prediction of combinatorial perturbation responses
items.summary: Combinatorial perturbations are widely used to study genetic interactions and to develop drug combinations, but the number of possible combinations grows quadratically with the number of perturbations, and only a small fraction can be measured in a screen experiment. Despite their growing sophistication, deep-learning and foundation models often fail to outperform a simple additive baseline based on measured single-perturbation responses. This suggests a simpler approach that builds on these measurements and directly learns deviations from additivity at the population level. We therefore developed GAIN, a lightweight model that implements these principles by predicting the pseudobulk response to a combination as the sum of its two single-perturbation responses and a learned interaction term.…

items.title: Clinical translation of ultrasoft Fleuron probes for stable, high-density, and bidirectional brain interfaces
items.summary: Building brain foundation models to capture the underpinning neural dynamics of human behavior requires large functional neural datasets for training, which current implantable Brain-Computer Interfaces (iBCIs) cannot achieve due to the instability of rigid materials in the brain. How can we realize high-density neural recordings with wide brain region access at single-neuron resolution, while maintaining the long-term stability required? In this study, we present a novel approach to overcome these trade-offs, by introducting Fleuron, a family of ultrasoft, ultra-low-k dielectric materials compatible with thin-film scalable microfabrication techniques. We successfully integrate up to 1,024 sites within a single minimally-invasive Fleuron depth electrode.…

items.title: Plasma DNA fragmentomic analysis for evaluation of patients with pancreatic cystic neoplasms
items.summary: Background Incidental detection of pancreatic cystic neoplasms (PCNs) is common, but to identify patients with malignant PCNs (high-grade dysplasia or carcinoma) who need invasive testing such as endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) or surgery is challenging. Plasma DNA fragmentomic analysis has recently shown promise for early detection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Objective To evaluate the ability of plasma DNA fragmentomic analysis to differentiate between patients with benign and malignant PCNs. Design We performed whole genome sequencing of pre-treatment plasma DNA from 121 patients with PDAC, 121 age and sex-matched healthy controls, and 99 patients with PCNs referred for EUS (total n=341).…

items.title: Unified Machine Learning Model for Early Detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment, Frailty, and Fall Risk Using Multimodal Motor-Function Data
items.summary: Background: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI), frailty, and fall risk often co-occur in older adults and share motor signs, yet they are screened and modeled separately. A unified model that predicts all 3 conditions from 1 sensor-based assessment could support earlier and more efficient screening, but such a model has rarely been developed or rigorously compared with separate models. Objective: This study aimed to develop a unified machine learning model that predicts MCI, frailty, and fall risk together from sensor-based motor-function data, compare it with separate single-label models, explain its predictions, and test its robustness.…

items.title: What Does an Agent-Run Clinic Cost? Protocol for a Prospective Observational Study of the Compute Cost of Completed Work in a Clinical Agent Fleet
items.summary: Background: Decisions about deploying large language model (LLM) agents in health care require the cost of completed work in production. Published evidence reports benchmark accuracy, benchmark-level cost, and time or financial outcomes for ambient documentation, and list prices alone do not determine the cost of completed work. To our knowledge, no deployed clinical agent fleet has published a measurement method that ties compute cost, latency, failures and retries to completed work. Objective: This study aims to estimate the compute cost of completed work by the orchestrated clinical agents of a deployed LLM agent fleet over a 12-week window of production telemetry, using estimators, data-quality gates and an analysis plan fixed before any window data are extracted for the study.…

items.title: Heterogeneity in excess respiratory acute care utilization during wildfire smoke waves in California
items.summary: Rationale: Wildfire smoke is an increasing public health threat, yet most epidemiologic studies estimate average smoke-health associations across broad spatial or temporal scales. Such approaches may obscure substantial heterogeneity across individual smoke waves, leaving an important evidence gap for dynamic public health preparedness, risk communication, and clinical practice. Objectives: To estimate event-specific excess respiratory acute care utilization during smoke waves and identify smoke wave features associated with higher excess utilization. Methods: We conducted a statewide study of 18,271,754 respiratory acute care encounters in California from 2006 to 2019. A smoke wave was defined as at least 2 consecutive days during which county-level wildfire smoke fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exceeded the 95th percentile over the study period.…

items.title: Beyond billing codes: a proof-of-concept study of large language models for pregnancy episode reconstruction from clinical notes
items.summary: Background: Accurate identification of pregnancy episodes from electronic health records (EHRs) is essential for maternal and fetal health research. Existing approaches rely primarily on diagnosis and procedure codes, which may miss pregnancies documented outside the health system and are susceptible to coding errors. Clinical notes contain richer information but remain largely unexplored for this task. Objectives: To evaluate whether a large language model (LLM) can reconstruct complete pregnancy episodes directly from clinical notes. Methods: Chronologically concatenated notes and messages were provided to GPT-5, which identified episodes and extracted variables including assisted reproductive treatment, gestational age, outcome, and complications.…

items.title: Baseline Prognosis and Treatment Benefit From First-Line Immunotherapy Strategies: Target Trial Emulations Across Advanced Solid Tumors
items.summary: Background In randomized trials, first-line immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapy has shown excess early mortality versus chemotherapy- or targeted therapy-containing regimens. ICI monotherapy is often chosen for frail patients because it is perceived as less toxic. Whether treatment benefit varies with baseline prognosis is unknown, as poor-prognosis patients are underrepresented in trials. Methods Using the US Flatiron Health electronic health record-derived database, we emulated target trials among 8,688 patients initiating first-line therapy during 2011-2023 across five comparisons: pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus pembrolizumab in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC; PD-L1 CPS [≥] 1 or unknown) and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC; PD-L1 TPS [≥] 50%); carboplatin plus gemcitabine versus pembrolizumab in urothelial carcinoma; pembrolizumab versus…

items.title: CB-COMIL: interpretable prediction of melanoma immunotherapyresponse from multiplex immunofluorescence whole-slide images
items.summary: Deep learning models can predict melanoma immunotherapy response but rarely explain predictions biologically. Concept bottleneck models offer interpretable predictions, but have not been applied to multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF), and whether their learned concepts reproduce tissue measurements remains unclear. We developed CB-COMIL, which routes mIF predictions through four supervised concepts (immune:tumour ratio, CD8/SOX10 balance, CD68 relative signal and PD-L1 evasion index), decomposing each prediction exactly into concept contributions. Developed on 211 slides and evaluated on 42 slides from an independent, differently acquired test cohort, CB-COMIL achieved macro-F1 0.69 versus 0.67 for an opaque comparator (difference 0.020, 95% CI: -0.103 to 0.144).…

items.title: A deep multimodal model for age-related macular degeneration detection using optical coherence tomography imaging and clinical text data
items.summary: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a major cause of vision loss, with a significant impact on the elderly population worldwide. Machine learning and deep learning methods, combined with optical coherence tomography (OCT), are promising for the rapid diagnosis of AMD. However, most models focus only on one single OCT imaging modality or neglect clinical information. To improve this problem, we design a deep multimodal framework that integrates OCT images with clinical text data for the detection of AMD. Then, we evaluate the proposed model using metrics, such as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F-score, and the area under the curve (AUC), achieving excellent detection results at both the image level and patient level.…

items.title: Asking Conversational Artificial Intelligence about Health and Subsequent Actions among Adults in Japan: A Cross-sectional Web Survey
items.summary: Introduction: People increasingly ask conversational artificial intelligence (AI) about health; however, how this relates to care seeking in Japan, where universal health coverage renders care accessible, remains unknown. This study described how many adults ask AI about health, why and when, what they do afterward, and how much they trust AI compared with other sources. Methods: This two-stage cross-sectional survey employed a commercial web panel (October-November 2026). A screening survey of adults aged [≥]20 years (10,000 responses; 8,209 analyzed) estimated prevalence. A main survey of users (1,000 responses; 735 analyzed) asked about purposes, the most recent use and subsequent actions, and trust in seven information sources. Responses were weighted by sex and age.…

items.title: Task-specific fine-tuning versus frontier large language models for RoB 2 risk of bias assessment: development and external benchmark evaluation of RoB-BERT
items.summary: Background: Researchers increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to assess risk of bias in randomized trials, but how task-specific fine-tuned models compare with frontier models remains uncertain. Objective: To develop RoB-BERT, a fine-tuned RoB 2 assessment system, and to compare its agreement with human assessments against that of three frontier LLMs. Methods: RoB 2 rates five bias domains and the trial overall as low risk, some concerns or high risk, based on answers to 22 signalling questions. RoB-BERT answers each question, quotes the supporting sentences from the trial report, and applies the official RoB 2 algorithm.…

items.title: Personal HbA1c trajectories and incident diabetes: association, prediction and observability in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing
items.summary: Background. Clinical diagnosis often relies on a snapshot: a single measurement interpreted against a population threshold. Repeated (longitudinal) measurements, however, may reveal an individual's typical level and how it changes over time. Extracting this information is challenging when measurements are sparse and biological fluctuations may resemble sustained changes. Using data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA), we investigated whether individual glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) trajectories improved the prediction of incident diabetes beyond the most recent measurement, whether they were associated with incident diabetes, and how reliably they could be estimated. Methods. In this secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study, we analysed venous HbA1c measured approximately every four years in ELSA, with a longer final interval of about seven years.…

items.title: AI Identification of Transdiagnostic Factors in Adolescent Mental Health
items.summary: Background: Adolescent psychopathology is commonly assessed using high-dimensional questionnaire data. These data often consist of ordinal, sparse, and overlapping symptom items, creating challenges for deriving latent phenotypes that are both interpretable and generalisable. This study addressed the need to derive low-dimensional transdiagnostic phenotypes from adolescent mental health data by evaluating denoising autoencoders as a flexible non-linear representation-learning approach. Methods: Using baseline data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study, we analysed mental health questionnaire data from a large community sample of adolescents (N = 9,799).…

items.title: Classifying chronic kidney disease from non-invasive questionnaire features in adults with long-standing diabetes in Bangladesh: model development, internal validation and the limits of small-sample evidence
items.summary: Background Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a common complication of diabetes, and in Bangladesh laboratory testing for it is not always available. Questionnaire answers could help decide whom to test first, but small machine-learning studies often report optimistic accuracy. Methods We analysed a public dataset of 400 adults with at least 10 years of diabetes attending a tertiary hospital in Dhaka, 185 with a hospital diagnosis of CKD. A pre-specified ridge logistic regression using 20 non-invasive features was developed and internally validated with nested cross-validation (five folds, ten repeats), compared with lasso, random forest and gradient boosting, and assessed for discrimination, calibration and net benefit. Simulations examined case-enriched sampling and single train/test splits.…

items.title: The unedited acceptance rate: a review-fidelity metric for human-in-the-loop clinical AI
items.summary: Objective. Guidance for large language model (LLM) drafting in clinical care relies on human review, yet review is rarely measured as a control. We aimed to define computable measures of review fidelity, establish which a deployed system can compute, and pre-specify their first analysis. Materials and Methods. For a multi-agent clinical system in routine use at one private London outpatient clinic, we defined acceptance coverage, attribution completeness, the unedited acceptance rate (UAR), a bounded normalized edit distance, availability latency and an unedited fast-approval rate (UFA). We checked each measure against the system's code and database structure at a fixed commit on four approval routes and pre-specified a prospective 12-week analysis. Results. The UAR equals the mass at zero of the edit-distance distribution, and availability latency bounds reading time from above only.…

items.title: WITHDRAWN: Predicting Distant Melanoma Metastasis at Diagnosis Using Machine Learning
items.summary: Distant melanoma metastasis at the time of diagnosis is uncommon, but has major implications for patient prognosis and treatment selection. However, few tools can reliably predict the risk of distant metastasis at initial presentation. Here, we developed and evaluated machine learning models to predict distant melanoma metastasis using routinely captured clinicopathologic and demographic variables across all histologic subtypes. Using the National Cancer Institute Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) program from 2010-2022, we identified adults aged 20 to 90 years with melanoma as the first and only primary malignancy (n=51,285). Explainable Boosting Machine achieved a strong balance of discrimination and precision (AUROC = 0.947, AUPRC = 0.610, Precision = 0.793, Brier = 0.015).…

items.title: External validation of the EK-LEF electrocardiogram model for left ventricular systolic dysfunction in three U.S. health systems
items.summary: Background: Heart failure is projected to affect more than 11 million U.S. adults by 2050, and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) can be present before symptoms appear. Deep learning models can detect reduced LVEF from the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), but most have been tested only in the institutions that developed them, often after excluding patients with prior heart failure or recordings of poor quality. We evaluated EK-LEF, a self-supervised ECG model fine-tuned on low LVEF detection. Methods: A bidirectional Mamba encoder was pre-trained on 435,420 unlabeled MIMIC-IV ECGs and fine-tuned on 471,248 ECG-echocardiogram pairs from 235,969 patients at Mayo Clinic Rochester and the Mayo Clinic Health System.…

items.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Autism ADOS-2 Calibrated Severity Scores Using Genetic and Behavioral Features
items.summary: Background: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition characterized by social communication difficulties and restricted, repetitive behaviors. While machine learning has been widely applied in autism research, few studies have predicted continuous autism severity measures such as the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule Calibrated Severity Score (ADOS CSS). We evaluated behavioral and genetic predictors of ADOS CSS across ADOS modules. Methods: Participants from the Simons Simplex Collection who completed ADOS Modules 1, 2, or 3 were included. Behavioral questionnaire data and gene-level measures of loss-of-function intolerance (pLI, LOEUF) and brain-expression specificity (pExt) were used to train 12 machine learning models separately for each module.…

items.title: Exercise misinformation in fitness content targeted at women on Instagram and TikTok: a cross-sectional content analysis of 6,982 posts
items.summary: Objectives. To quantify exercise misinformation in female targeted exercise content on Instagram and TikTok, determine whether content textually targeted at women carries higher rates of misinformation, and compare content from creators self identifying as ethnic minority with other content. Methods. Cross sectional content analysis of 6,982 posts collected March to June 2026 by manual browsing, which captured on screen and caption text, and automated collection, which captured captions only. Text was coded for claim accuracy, textual female targeting and creator characteristics, with large language model assisted coding verified against an independent human coder. Effects were estimated by logistic regression using adjustment sets from a pre specified causal diagram, with creator clustered standard errors. Results.…

items.title: Spatially localized racial differences in the association between white matter hyperintensities and verbal memory in cognitively unimpaired adults
items.summary: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are common in aging, but whether their cognitive associations differ between African American and White older adults is unclear. We studied 5,187 cognitively unimpaired non-Hispanic African American (NHA) and non-Hispanic White (NHW) older adults across three independent cohorts using depth- and lobe-resolved WMH mapping with cross-sectional, longitudinal and machine learning analyses. In the Emory Healthy Brain Study (EHBS), greater WMH burden was more strongly associated with poorer verbal memory among NHA than NHW participants. A similar difference was observed in a 34-center cohort but not detected in the third cohort. Differences localized to frontal juxtacortical and parietal deep white matter in EHBS and the multicenter cohort, respectively, and did not parallel WMH burden distributions.…

items.title: Spatial proteomics identifies a myeloid-dominated, compartmentalized microenvironment and a proliferation-associated prognostic signature in clear cell sarcoma
items.summary: Clear cell sarcoma (CCS) is a rare soft-tissue sarcoma with poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options. Because of its rarity, the composition, spatial organization, and functional relevance of the CCS tumour microenvironment and tumour cell heterogeneity remain largely unexplored. Here, to address this gap, and as part of the Clear Cell Sarcoma Consortium, we used imaging mass cytometry with two antibody panels to generate a single-cell, spatially resolved proteomic map of CCS, profiling more than 5 million cells from a multi-institutional, clinically annotated formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded cohort of 52 patients. Our analysis shows that CCS is immune-cold, with the tumour centre dominated by myeloid cells, principally CD68+ and CD163+ macrophages, whereas the invasive front harbours a more diverse, lymphoid-containing immune infiltrate.…

items.title: Relevance-Based Prediction: A Transparent, Patient-Specific Approach to Predicting Medical Outcomes
items.summary: Accurate prediction of individual medical outcomes is essential for optimizing treatment allocation amid rising costs, coverage denials, and limited clinical resources. Traditional predictive models, including linear regression and neural networks, rely on average effects and cannot tailor predictions to the specific circumstances of individual cases. We present relevance-based prediction (RBP), a model-free and task-specific method that predicts outcomes as weighted averages of observed cases, with weights determined by a rigorously defined and theoretically justified measure of relevance. Unlike model-based methods that rely on fixed calibrated parameters, relevance-based prediction revisits the original data for each prediction and customizes both the cases and variables used.…

items.title: PortalEvent: An Event-Based Ontology for Patient-Initiated Portal Communication
items.summary: Background: Patient portal messaging has become a primary channel for asynchronous clinical communication. The messages cover a wide range of topics, from symptom reporting and medication concerns to administrative requests. In recent years, message volume has grown substantially. When a message lacks information the clinician needs, it often leads to back-and-forth that delays resolution of the patient's request, and it also takes time from clinicians that could be spent on more urgent matters. To build automated tools that reduce the burden, a structured representation is needed to understand what details these messages contain or lack, so the automated tool can provide help accordingly. However, there is no existing scalable, reproducible method to characterize these messages in a structured way with fine granularity.…

items.title: rendehR: a cohort-first, provenance-aware, agentic-ready pipeline for harmonizing multi-source electronic health records
items.summary: Objective: Public electronic health record (EHR) databases differ in schema, identifiers, coding systems, units, and event structure, making disease-specific studies across multiple sources difficult to construct and audit. We developed rendehR, a computational pipeline and R package for cohort-centered extraction and harmonization of multi-source EHR data. Materials and Methods: rendehR treats cohort definition as an explicit executable component of dataset construction. Cohorts can be defined using diagnosis codes, identifiers, R callbacks, or source-specific SQL. After cohort selection, linked source tables are restricted to the selected population and can be retained as cohort-specific Parquet datasets or loaded into a persistent database.…

items.title: Adapting Echocardiographic Foundation Models for Detecting Pulmonary Embolism-Related Right-Heart Strain
items.summary: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a time-sensitive medical emergency in which rapid recognition of right ventricular (RV) dysfunction by point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) can support early risk stratification. Here, we present HOPE (ecHO-Pulmonary Embolism), a real-world emergency cardiac POCUS video dataset comprising 4,069 patients with suspected PE, and EchoPE1, a foundation-model-based video classification framework for detecting PE-associated right-heart phenotypes. HOPE includes five commonly acquired emergency echocardiographic views, with all positive PE cases confirmed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography. EchoPE builds on EchoPrime-pretrained echocardiographic representations and incorporates view recognition, task-specific adaptation, and attention-based interpretability.…

items.title: Regional brain-age gaps reveal a shared polygenic architecture and regionally patterned clinical and cell-type associations
items.summary: A single brain-age estimate may obscure regional differences in clinical vulnerability. Using voxel-level deep learning, we derived whole-brain and nine regional brain-age gaps (BAGs) spanning cortical, subcortical and cerebellar regions from T1-weighted MRI in 46,254 UK Biobank participants. Genetic correlation estimates in 41,067 participants (rg = 0.56-0.93) exceeded phenotypic correlations across all 45 pairs, yet regional profiles varied across 24 hospital-recorded diagnoses. Oligodendrocyte annotations predominated for whole-brain and cerebellar BAGs, whereas annotations for caudate BAG included astrocyte and vascular classes. In the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, temporal BAG showed stronger associations with cerebrospinal fluid A{beta}42 and cognition than whole-brain BAG when modelled together.…

items.title: Continually pretrained open-weight language models can outperform traditional machine learning in EHR-based clinical prediction
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) prompted with electronic health record (EHR) data have predicted clinical outcomes less accurately than locally trained machine-learning models. We developed VEX-EHR by extending the vocabulary of a 12-billion-parameter open-weight LLM (weights publicly available) with 17,601 clinical and audit-log codes from 170,483 patients' records at one academic medical center, continuing its pretraining on those 2019-2024 records (4.7 billion tokens) and fine-tuning it per task. AUROCs were 0.917 for next-24-hour discharge, 0.715 for 30-day readmission and 0.847 for intensive care unit acute kidney injury, against 0.868, 0.677 and 0.828 for gradient-boosted trees and 0.848, 0.650 and 0.791 for CEHR-BERT, an EHR foundation model. Continued pretraining added 0.031-0.053 AUROC on every task.…

items.title: STREAM: Sequential Transformer for Risk Estimation from Asynchronous Medical Events for Dynamic Postoperative AKI Prediction
items.summary: Postoperative acute kidney injury (PO-AKI) risk estimates evolve as clinical information accumulates, yet many electronic health record (EHR) models use static or fixed-window representations. We developed STREAM, a perioperative event-stream Transformer that represents irregular EHR data as chronological clinical events and supports surgery-index prediction at surgery completion and event-by-event postoperative AKI prediction. In a retrospective cohort of 167,078 noncardiac surgical episodes, STREAM achieved surgery-index AUROC/AUPRC of 0.942/0.771, the Time-series Transformer 0.933/0.729, and GRU-D 0.926/0.695. Postoperative macro-AUPRC across 6-hour evaluation intervals was 0.589, 0.525, and 0.547, respectively. STREAM showed more consistent calibration across postoperative time points than the comparators.…

items.title: LUCID: Statistically Grounded Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning Evaluation
items.summary: Cheap language-model raters grade chain-of-thought reasoning at scale, yet systematic step-rating errors can skew reasoning audits and solution rankings. We introduce LUCID (Loop for Unbiased Calibration via Inference-time Diagnosis), which pairs prompt self-correction with Design-based Supervised Learning (DSL). Without retraining or weight access, LUCID calibrates binary step ratings by aligning predicted and expert soundness rates. From a small expert-labeled set, LUCID summarizes rater bias in plain text and prompts the rater to re-grade unseen steps. For example, on PRM800K, GPT-5-mini grades too strictly, under-rating computation, verification, and late-trace steps most acutely. In one pass, LUCID shrinks GPT-5-mini's calibration gap from 7.8 to 0.9 percentage points in absolute predicted-expert rate difference.…
items.tldr: LUCID calibrates language-model step ratings using prompt-based self-correction and Design-based Supervised Learning, reducing bias and improving reasoning audit and selection accuracy without retraining.

items.title: From Rewarding What Models Say to How They Think: Attention Process Reward Model for LLM Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an important component in large language models (LLMs). However, existing RL approaches focus on final outputs or textual solution trajectories, leading to coarse-grained rewards and unreliable reasoning. Such paradigms focus mainly on what the model outputs while overlooking how the model internally reasons. Therefore, can we reward how a model thinks internally rather than merely what it says? We first reveal the problem of textual reward aliasing in existing reward modeling approaches. Motivated by this, we propose the Attention Process Reward Model (APRM), which assigns internal rewards based on hidden states and attention maps to capture high-quality reasoning patterns.…
items.tldr: An attention-based process reward model that rewards internal reasoning through hidden states and attention maps improves reinforcement learning for large language models, yielding an average pass@8 gain of 2.88%.

items.title: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents
items.summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are rapidly improving, yet their evaluation remains largely static. Existing benchmarks provide a strong foundation, but fixed difficulty ceilings, limited feature coverage, and coarse aggregate scores progressively weaken their discriminative and diagnostic value. We introduce CUA-SEE, a closed-loop evaluation environment that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers from rollout evidence. It disentangles three objectives: benchmark evolution expands evaluation scope through cohort-calibrated difficulty and coverage growth; diagnostic evolution increases resolution through agent-conditional capability-boundary probes; and verifier evolution improves precision by translating changing requirements into state-grounded checkpoints with adversarial validation.…
items.tldr: CUA-SEE is a closed-loop evaluation environment that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers to adaptively measure computer-use agents’ capabilities, boundaries, and progress reliability.

items.title: WeaveVLA: 3D Relational Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models leverage pretrained vision-language representations for instruction-conditioned robot control, yet their understanding of task-relevant 3D relations and how these relations evolve during manipulation remains largely implicit. To address this challenge, we introduce WeaveVLA, a framework that enhances VLA action generation by explicitly modeling task-relevant relative 3D relations and maintaining relational context across observations. WeaveVLA employs a task-conditioned sparse graph neural network to encode relative 3D relations among objects, the gripper, and nearby references. Pair-specific recurrent edge states integrate geometric evidence across observations to maintain evolving spatial context.…

items.title: RUIBench: What Makes a Good Robot-Use Interface?
items.summary: Foundation models can reason about complex physical tasks, yet translating this intelligence into reliable robot execution remains challenging. We argue that a critical, often overlooked factor is the robot-use interface (RUI), which determines how agents express and execute physical actions. To systematically study its impact, we introduce RUIBench, comprising 30 manipulation tasks across five suites spanning world knowledge, in-context learning, discovery, dynamic interaction, and contact-rich manipulation. We further develop RUIKit, a unified framework that crosses six action abstractions with two interaction forms, yielding 13 interfaces under shared perception and control. In simulation, changing only the RUI shifts a frontier agent's success rate from 45% to 81%, and that of a fine-tuned 4B model from 13% to 47%.…

items.title: ReWeave: Emergent Physical Task Topologies for Embodied Harness Optimization and Cross-Task Meta-Distillation
items.summary: Long-horizon embodied tasks involve physical dependencies that may only become clear through interaction. As task understanding deepens, past trials can reveal new information for adaptation and transfer. However, coarse progress feedback cannot identify which physical preconditions held, leaving search unguided, while task-specific optimization easily overfits to individual scenes, making cross-task transfer brittle. We introduce ReWeave, a framework that jointly optimizes an embodied agent harness and an emergent physical task topology from interaction without updating policy weights. Keeping execution policies and perception frozen, ReWeave co-optimizes coupled context, workflows, and control loops.…
items.tldr: ReWeave jointly optimizes an embodied agent harness and an emergent physical task topology from interaction without updating policy weights, improving success and enabling continual learning across tasks.

items.title: WorldLeague: Benchmarking Physical Agency
items.summary: AI systems can now operate Blender, follow instructions in complex video games, and manipulate objects with robot arms. What range of physical goals can today's AI systems achieve autonomously? Answering this question requires testing systems on tasks that demand different combinations of perception, memory, planning, and action. We introduce \textbf{WorldLeague}, a benchmark that compares AI systems on a common set of \textbf{60 simulated robot tasks} by measuring progress toward each task's physical goal from the robot's trajectory. Robots explore scenes to gather evidence in \textbf{WorldSeek}, rearrange objects in \textbf{WorldShape}, and adapt to changes in \textbf{WorldShift}. Tying these goals to a single control interface limits which AI systems can be compared.…
items.tldr: WorldLeague benchmarks 13 AI systems on 60 simulated robot tasks spanning exploration, rearrangement, and adaptation, measuring progress and success to compare autonomous physical goal achievement.

items.title: Foresight Forcing: Learning Spatial Foresight for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Robotic manipulation policies can improve action prediction by anticipating how objects move and how their spatial relationships change. World Action Models (WAMs) learn to predict future visual observations, but their training objectives typically leave the underlying 3D geometric transitions implicit. To alleviate this problem, we introduce Foresight Forcing ($\mathcal{F}^{2}$), a WAM that learns a spatial transition representation from changes in a pretrained 3D feature space. During training, a frozen 3D foundation model extracts patch-wise feature differences from aligned current and future observations that provide dense supervision for geometry-aware feature transitions.…
items.tldr: Foresight Forcing distills geometry-aware spatial transition queries from a frozen 3D foundation model to improve robotic manipulation action prediction without requiring future observations at deployment.

items.title: Small Learned Projections for Semantic-Reversal-Aware Retrieval with Spectral Acceleration: A Four-Domain Empirical Study
items.summary: Dense-embedding retrievers can fail adversarially: when a query is answered by a document A and reversed by a near-copy B that differs from A by a small meaning-changing edit (a "trap"), raw cosine over E5-Large-v2 places B in the top-10 for 82-100% of queries at a pool of 5,000. We study two things. First, a small learned projection W: R^1024 -> R^d (d in {11, 32}), trained by a deterministic recipe on a declared set of cases, that suppresses the trap: for the declared cases, HN@10 = 0.0000 (no trap in the top-10) in all twelve (domain, pool-size) settings across four independent domains (legal, medical, patent, financial) and pools up to 100,000, while the correct paraphrase is retained for 93-99% of cases, under exact nearest-neighbour search.…

items.title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models
items.summary: Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. Latent action models (LAMs) can recover these dynamics, but they train their inverse- and forward-dynamics models (IDM, FDM) from scratch, trading off pixel reconstruction against latent capacity and accuracy. Pretrained video world models natively generate high-fidelity dynamics, yet represent them densely, entangled across all layers. Viewing the world model as a LAM, we show that these dynamics can be extracted with minimal changes to the model.…
items.tldr: Native LAM distills compact latent actions from a pretrained video diffusion transformer via learnable dynamics registers, and PAWlicy uses these actions to pretrain VLA policies without generating video, achieving strong robotic control and cross-embodiment transfer.

items.title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
items.summary: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as a second residual stream. This yields LoomFormer, a dual-stream architecture that splits control and content between the vector and matrix streams. Across model sizes and training token budgets in language modeling and downstream tasks, LoomFormer matches Transformers trained with over 3x compute and recent residual-stream baselines (HC/mHC, MUDDFormer, AttnRes) trained with ~1.7-2.8x.…

items.title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
items.summary: Coding agents can construct and revise robot behavior during execution, but using one agent for the whole robot can delay otherwise independent work. We introduce Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy (ACAP), an asynchronous framework that organizes one robot as a team of persistent agents. Each member reasons and acts for a configurable control group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis, enabling asynchronous reasoning and execution. However, different robot components often have physical dependencies that require coordination. To address this challenge, ACAP introduces a hyper-agent that assigns tasks, coordinates dependencies, and dynamically allocates control between the lead and member agents. This allows independent work to progress concurrently while supporting tightly coupled manipulation when necessary.…

items.title: On-Policy Codec Distillation for Efficient All-in-One Video Generation
items.summary: Modern visual generative models operate on tokens, and every visual asset they receive, whether an identity, a scribble, a depth map, or a motion video, is tokenized and appended to the input token sequence. Consequently, conditioning quickly dominates the computation cost. Yet most of these tokens carry redundant spatiotemporal information. Our key insight is that identifying what is genuinely new is exactly the problem that classical video codecs have long solved. Thus, we first introduce a codec-based token pruning method that discards redundant tokens. Then, we propose an on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) strategy to train a DiT adapter capable of learning the codec pruning pattern well without quality degradation. Together, they form On-Policy Codec Distillation (CodecOPSD).…

items.title: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation
items.summary: Recent advances in video generation have made automated advertising production increasingly feasible. However, an effective advertisement must faithfully represent the product and communicate its selling points through compelling visual storytelling, which requires more than visual synthesis: it calls for deeper product understanding and strategic decisions about how to present product value. Crucially, product research and creative design are closely intertwined, as the information gathered about a product determines which features can be faithfully demonstrated and how they should be presented. In this paper, we introduce AdProducer, the first end-to-end agentic framework for advertising video creation, transforming concise creative briefs into finished advertisements.…
items.tldr: An end-to-end multimodal agent framework autonomously researches products and creates selling-point-driven storyboards to guide a frozen video generator, trained via supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to produce effective advertising videos.

items.title: Do learned image captioning metrics generalize? Auditing duplicated samples in human-judgment benchmarks
items.summary: Learned image captioning metrics are trained and tested on human judgments, so their reported correlation is a claim about generalization. We audit this claim for the three most recent collections of such judgments, Polaris, Nebula, and Spica, matching images at the pixel level. First, test samples reappear in training sets: the Spica training set contains about two-thirds of the Polaris test set, with identical human ratings. Second, controlled retraining shows that duplicates can inflate a metric: for Pearl, the gain is confined to the duplicated samples and grows with every epoch; for DENEB, it stays below one point. The gain depends on the learner and on how often a training set repeats a sample.…
items.tldr: An audit of recent image captioning evaluation benchmarks shows that duplicate samples and metric behavior inflate reported correlations, and proposes a protocol under which zero-shot vision-language judges perform best on recent test sets.

items.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
items.summary: Frontier multimodal models exhibit extraordinary generalization in generating robot actions from observations and instructions, enabling a new paradigm in which they serve directly as policies within closed-loop robotic harnesses. However, the design principles of such harnesses, and the capabilities underlying their strong performance, remain unclear. We present Embo-Harness, a framework for systematically studying frontier-model-as-policy harnesses. We investigate four components of the robotic agentic loop, namely, prompting, planning, action execution, and tool use, and distill six empirical findings into a practical recipe.…
items.tldr: A systematic framework shows that frontier multimodal models can serve as robot policies when harnessed with interfaces favoring native visual reasoning and tool use, achieving high success in simulated and real manipulation tasks.

items.title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce
items.summary: We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. The family spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. Our training pipeline begins with two-stage continued pre-training that progressively raises the proportion of e-commerce data within a diverse multimodal data mixture, followed by hybrid-thinking post-training that combines on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning to support both non-thinking and thinking modes. For evaluation, we construct a comprehensive suite of 28 e-commerce benchmarks (23 in-house and five open-source) covering eight business scenarios and complement it with 64 public general-purpose benchmarks.…
items.tldr: WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models spanning dense and mixture-of-experts sizes, is trained with continued pre-training and hybrid-thinking post-training to achieve strong e-commerce and general-purpose results and is deployed in WeChat.

items.title: ViDiHand2: Unifying Video Diffusion Priors and Hand Geometry for 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild
items.summary: Learning robot manipulation from egocentric human videos requires accurate metric 3D hand motion. Recent methods leverage pretrained video diffusion model (VDM) priors to recover occluded hands directly from full-frame videos, but their appearance-based depth regression generalizes poorly to unseen cameras. In this work, we propose ViDiHand2, a geometry-driven framework that reformulates VDM-based hand depth estimation from direct regression into fine-grained geometric constraint solving. Specifically, we introduce Fine-Grained Geometric Lifting and Clip-Level Ray Fitting, which recover metric depth by enforcing geometric consistency between pixel-aligned 2D joints and the metric structure of MANO hands, while leveraging temporal observations across the clip.…

items.title: What Makes Good Data for Training Coding Agents? A Systematic Study on SWE-Gym
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) trains coding agents on software tasks whose hidden tests decide the reward, yet task collections check these tests only against the reference fix. We ask what makes a task good training data, focusing on the correctness of its reward labels. We audit SWE-Gym with two LLM families, and a suspected error counts only if execution reproduces it. We find that unsolved often means mislabelled: 74% of the tasks that a 9B base model never solves have a test that rejects correct fixes (a false negative), versus 20% of those it sometimes solves. We repair or remove such tasks, and the audited tasks that remain train better policies.…
items.tldr: Auditing reward labels in coding-agent reinforcement learning tasks shows many unsolved tasks are mislabeled, and training on corrected tasks improves policy performance on SWE-bench benchmarks.

items.title: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
items.summary: Looped Transformers iterate a shared block of layers to increase computation without adding parameters, offering stronger performance and test-time scaling. However, this power has so far required training from scratch and yielded only modest gains for LLMs. Finetuning existing models into loops is far cheaper, yet also brings only marginal gains over SFT. We propose LoopRes, an effective, scalable, and simple approach that turns loops into significant and consistent gains for pretrained LLMs. Building on Attention Residuals, LoopRes lets each looped layer attend directly to the outputs of earlier loops. Since these outputs are iterates of the same layers and become harder to tell apart, we give each a trainable loop-aware key that encodes its structural identity.…
items.tldr: LoopRes enables pretrained large language models to benefit from looped computation by letting layers attend to recent earlier loops with trainable loop-aware keys, yielding consistent gains and improved test-time scaling.

items.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
items.summary: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild. Human practitioners, by contrast, cope with insufficient tools by fashioning new ones from familiar parts and reusing them across tasks. Inspired by this, we propose ToolSmith, an automatic tool-generation framework that grows and reuses modules on top of a lean base tool library. We evaluate ToolSmith on three in-domain multimodal search benchmarks and ten out-of-domain benchmarks under a VLM-as-a-Judge protocol.…

items.title: DexDuet: Learning Contact-Preserving Bimanual Dexterity from Human Demonstrations
items.summary: Human demonstrations provide a rich source of bimanual dexterous skills, yet transferring them to robot hands remains challenging. Existing methods primarily optimize object trajectory tracking, often overlooking how human hands interact with the object. Even with accurate tracking, robots may contact incorrect object parts or slide their fingers, resulting in unstable manipulation. We present DexDuet, a framework that learns contact-preserving bimanual dexterity from a single human demonstration. DexDuet employs two interaction rewards to preserve human hand-object configurations and contacts. To enable coordinated manipulation, we factorize the bimanual policy into two weight-sharing per-hand policies that condition on each other's states.…

items.title: Can Latent Reasoning Drive LLM Outputs Without a Trace?
items.summary: LLMs typically solve complex tasks with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, which is also the main tool for monitoring them for misaligned behavior. However, standard transformers can also solve tasks with complete latent reasoning (CLR), carrying out the whole task internally and outputting only the final answer. Theory bounds the depth of CLR, the number of sequential steps it can carry out, and recent work measured it to be shallow. In this work, we ask whether CLR is deep enough for a model to pursue a hidden objective that requires reasoning. Such a model would generate a CoT that appears to solve the given task, while a latent multi-step computation decides its answer based on the hidden objective. First, we show that a simple auxiliary loss allows models to solve a multi-step task latently at least 5x deeper than previously reported.…
items.tldr: Models can use deep latent reasoning to pursue hidden objectives while generating chain-of-thought explanations that appear task-appropriate and evade output-based monitoring.

items.title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation
items.summary: AI agents accumulate conversations, images, and documents through long-term interactions with users. Answering later questions often requires connecting evidence across these records, yet the resulting understanding is rarely retained, allowing mistakes to recur on related questions. Existing multimodal memory methods largely focus on storing and retrieving records, with limited mechanisms for learning from completed tasks and consolidating task-specific experience. We therefore propose MMMem, a task-aware multimodal memory framework that extracts and consolidates experience from completed tasks through four complementary strategies. First, source-linked multi-view memory organizes original text, images, and rendered pages alongside generated scene images that combine clues across records for retrieval.…
items.tldr: A task-aware multimodal memory framework consolidates experience from completed tasks using source-linked multi-view memory, source-generated tasks, distillation, and task-aware retrieval, yielding consistent gains across memory benchmarks.

items.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
items.summary: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Keeping the patches matters. Averaging each view to one token removes most of the success, adaptation helps every pair we test, and one shared policy keeps most of the success of separate policies at a fraction of the updates. The same tokens are then scored with statistics, state and object readouts, published vision scores, and an inverse-dynamics readout. That readout of the commanded motion is one of the strongest measurements available before a policy is trained.…
items.tldr: A shared flow-matching policy that reads dense patch tokens from multiple vision encoders improves success on egocentric bimanual tasks, and inverse-dynamics readout of commanded motion is a strong pre-training signal, while recognition, depth, and correspondence transfer unreliably.

items.title: Let Vision-Language Models Generate Images through Their Representations
items.summary: Recent unified multimodal models aim to combine visual understanding and generation within a single model, yet effectively integrating the two capabilities remains challenging. Leveraging pretrained vision-language models offers a way to build on already learned multimodal knowledge, but making this knowledge effectively accessible to visual generation remains nontrivial. We find that a central challenge lies in the heterogeneous visual representations used for understanding and generation. To address this challenge, we introduce Integral, which converts a pretrained vision-language model into a unified multimodal model by constructing a shared visual representation space across the two capabilities. Integral implements this design through two complementary components.…
items.tldr: Integral converts a pretrained vision-language model into a unified multimodal model by constructing a shared visual representation space, preserving understanding while enabling strong visual generation.

items.title: WorldLatent: A Unified 4D Latent Space for World Perception and Generation
items.summary: Generative Pre-Training (GPT) represents a profound milestone in natural language processing, serving as the foundation for most of today's state-of-the-art large language models. By casting diverse understanding and generation problems into a shared token representation, GPT enables a single architecture and unified optimization loop to master heterogeneous tasks across massive corpora, giving rise to powerful foundation models for natural language. In contrast, 4D spatiotemporal vision lacks a common representational protocol: perception (such as depth and camera estimation) and generation are either handled by separate one-way pipelines or bolted together from unaligned single-modality spaces. In this work, we introduce WorldLatent, a framework that formulates a unified 4D latent space as a common protocol for both world perception and generation.…
items.tldr: WorldLatent unifies 4D perception and generation in a shared multimodal latent space, enabling a single model to perform zero-shot 4D perception, coherent 4D generation, and controllable editing.

items.title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games
items.summary: Interactive intelligence requires agents to act on observations and adapt to the consequences of actions. Studying these abilities calls for diverse, challenging tasks under controlled conditions. We introduce GameDojo, a controllable interactive gameplay benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games for evaluating model capabilities, learning algorithms, and agent harnesses. Coding agents reconstruct the environments and write gameplay scripts, producing GameDojo-Data with 600 hours of gameplay trajectories. Experiments reveal substantial challenges for frontier models, especially in real-time interaction. Training on GameDojo-Data brings GameDojo-4B to frontier performance, with the strongest real-time performance. We also find joint training improves individual tasks, and learned policies transfer across bosses.…
items.tldr: GameDojo is a controllable benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games with 600 hours of gameplay trajectories, showing frontier models struggle in real-time interaction while training GameDojo-4B achieves frontier performance and policy transfer across bosses.

items.title: A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models
items.summary: Depth-recurrent (Looped) models raise effective depth by applying a shared stack of blocks several times. Scaling them usually requires pipeline parallelism, but commonly used interleaved 1F1B is drawn for an acyclic stage graph in which each micro-batch enters each stage once. Once that stack is split across stages, the same stage is visited several times on one micro-batch and later stages feed earlier ones: native 1F1B has no slot for the extra visit, cannot rank a first iteration against a second, and its neighbour-only send/receive order has no back edge to the first stage, so the arrangement stalls or fires out of order. We present Loop-PP, which rebuilds both the timetable and the communication for this cyclic layout.…
items.tldr: Loop-PP schedules cyclic pipeline stages for depth-recurrent models, overlapping communication and compute while preserving exact numerical equivalence, reducing memory and increasing throughput on MoE models.

items.title: GlanceNav: Efficient Vision-and-Language Navigation with Streaming Memory and Counterfactual Rewind
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become strong policies for vision-and-language navigation (VLN). However, most of them encode a sample of past frames again at every decision and are trained on isolated decisions, so computation is redundant and the usable history is short. They also learn from their own mistakes through outcome rewards that give one scalar to a whole episode. We ask whether a navigator can encode each frame only once, at a constant cost per step, and still remember what matters and learn efficiently from its mistakes. We present GlanceNav, a streaming navigator built on a hybrid MLLM. Its Gated DeltaNet layers carry a recurrent state through the whole episode, while its attention layers keep a short window of recent observations and a small bank of keyframes, selected by how much each frame changes the recurrent state.…
items.tldr: GlanceNav is a streaming multimodal navigator that maintains constant per-step memory through recurrent and attention mechanisms and uses a reinforcement learning correction method to improve vision-and-language navigation.

items.title: Distill the Correction, Not the Rewrite: Hindsight Twins for Self-Improving Text-to-Image Models
items.summary: Text-to-image models can learn from their own mistakes by distilling a self-teacher conditioned on a vision-language critic's revised prompt. However, such self-teachers barely improve alignment, and both they and their hindsight-contrast variants absorb the critic's unintended additions to the scene, such as lighting or scenery. We attribute this to two factors: (1) the prompt already specifies the desired fix, so a useful revision must go beyond the failed span, often rewriting the entire scene and adding details that overshadow the fix; (2) although the critic localizes the error to a single span, self-teachers condition on the rewrite, entangling the intended fix with unintended additions.…
items.tldr: Hindsight Twins improves text-to-image alignment by distilling the velocity difference between twin prompt revisions while avoiding critic-induced bias.

items.title: MORSE: Optimizing Streaming Memory Design via Open-World Auto-Research
items.summary: A streaming video system must decide in a single pass what evidence to retain under bounded frame storage, before it knows which details a future question will require. Recent recursive self-improvement methods automate the design of the harness that stores and retrieves this evidence. They revise the harness in response to failures, but the editor must still devise each repair from its prior knowledge and a predefined set of tools. A failure that recurs across videos, however, may point to a problem that prior work has already addressed. We introduce MORSE (Memory Optimization with Recursive Self-Evolvement), an open-world auto-research framework that uses recurring failures to guide an online search for solutions. Its editor groups failures in training traces by cause, then searches papers, model cards, and code for methods it can adapt or pretrained perception models it can use.…
items.tldr: MORSE leverages recurring failures to search for adaptable methods and pretrained perception models, improving accuracy and speed of a frozen video-language model on streaming video question answering.

items.title: Write, Evolve, Read: Streaming Cameras into a Persistent World State for 4D Occupancy Forecasting
items.summary: 4D occupancy forecasting predicts the 3D semantic occupancy of a driving scene seconds ahead. Over a few seconds, the scene changes little while the vehicle moves, so most of the space ahead has already been seen. Sorting the future into unchanged, changed, and unseen space, we find that current camera-based world models fall short on the unchanged part: they fail to hold on to what they have already seen, rather than to forecast what will change. We therefore make what the model has seen its state. PersistWorld streams camera frames into a persistent 3D world state anchored in the scene, writing each frame once instead of rebuilding the state from past frames. The state is learned end to end with the forecast, and an evolver predicts it at any queried time along the ego trajectory.…
items.tldr: PersistWorld maintains a scene-anchored 3D world state updated from camera streams and forecasts future semantic occupancy more accurately and faster than prior camera-based world models.

items.title: Context-Grounded Skill Internalization for Vision-Language Agents
items.summary: Skill internalization offers a way for agents to learn useful behaviors from skills and use them without explicit guidance in context at inference time. A common approach is to generate demonstration trajectories with the skill in context and then fine-tune the same model on its own trajectories with the skill removed. However, this leads to the problem that the model may learn to reference the removed skill, which we named as context misalignment (CoMi). In this work, we first analyze agent behaviors related to CoMi under this common pipeline. Across ALFWorld, WebShop, and ARC-AGI-1, skill-removed fine-tuning consistently results in CoMi: 12.2-46.0% of test trajectories reference the removed skill. To address this problem, we develop Context-Grounded Skill Internalization (CGSI).…
items.tldr: Context-Grounded Skill Internalization mitigates context misalignment in skill-removed fine-tuning by detecting and masking or rewriting unsupported skill references, preserving task success while reducing training and processing costs.

items.title: PixelOne: From Options to Pixels in a Single Forward for GUI Grounding
items.summary: GUI grounding requires precise clicks at low latency. Recent models such as GUI-Decisions and GUI-Swift predict coordinates in one forward pass using fixed global bins with local refinement. However, screenshot downsampling removes detail needed to locate small controls, while fixed bins cover larger pixel ranges at higher resolutions. We introduce PixelOne, which transfers spatial knowledge from a search teacher to a student that predicts clicks directly from screenshots at native resolution. The teacher uses VideoJEV's text-option scorer to select rows and columns and progressively zoom into candidate regions. The student inherits the teacher's parameters and matches its distributions over explored regions through spatial distillation alongside box supervision.…
items.tldr: PixelOne transfers spatial knowledge from a search teacher to a student to predict GUI clicks at native resolution in one forward pass, achieving high accuracy and low latency.

items.title: Self-Supervised Dataset Distillation via Mutual Information Maximization
items.summary: Dataset distillation (DD) aims to compress a large dataset into a small synthetic one that remains effective for training neural networks. Despite its success in supervised learning, DD remains underexplored in self-supervised learning (SSL), where distilled data must preserve the information needed to learn representations that remain consistent across augmentations. To bridge this gap, we introduce Mutual Information Prototype Alignment (MIPA), an efficient SSL dataset distillation approach that optimizes synthetic images to preserve augmentation-invariant information. Specifically, MIPA treats synthetic images as learnable prototypes and uses a frozen encoder to assign real samples to them based on feature similarity. A synthetic dataset that preserves such augmentation invariance should yield stable prototype assignments across multiple augmented views of the same real image.…
items.tldr: Mutual Information Prototype Alignment distills datasets for self-supervised learning by optimizing synthetic prototypes to preserve augmentation-invariant information and improve learned representations.

items.title: Typhoon OCR 2: From Thai Document Transcription to Multilingual, Multi-Task OCR
items.summary: Typhoon OCR 1.5 focused on reading Thai documents. However, in real-world workflows, users often need to extract specific information or preserve the structure of an entire page for further processing. Typhoon OCR 2 handles both tasks in a single model, with prompt-driven extraction and structured full-page parsing. Full-page parsing covers Thai, English, and Chinese. We release compact 2B and 0.8B models adapted from open document parsers through supervised fine-tuning on curated Thai and public multilingual data, followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with task rewards and a rule penalizing unfinished responses. Among evaluated open models, Typhoon OCR 2 2B scores highest on Thai MDPBench (80.7 versus 68.9 for Typhoon OCR 1.5) and on ThaiOCRBench (59.91 versus 40.45), which covers recognition, extraction, and document understanding.…

items.title: Lyris: Layout-Guided Long Video Generation with Persistent 3D Memory
items.summary: Exploring a scene from as little as a single photo requires generating a long, camera-controlled walkthrough that extends far beyond what was captured, yet remains consistent upon return. Memory-based video generation methods preserve what they have already seen, but have no anchor beyond it, where the camera drifts from its path and a text prompt can name objects but not place them. Layout-conditioned methods provide such an anchor and precise control over what appears where, but rely on layouts that are typically authored by hand. Both limitations arise because, beyond what was captured, nothing anchors the video model unless a human authors one.…
items.tldr: Lyris uses persistent point-cloud memory and vision-language-model-authored 3D layouts to generate long, camera-controlled walkthroughs from a single photo, improving camera accuracy and return consistency.

items.title: CCFinance: Reconstructing Financial News Samples from Web Archives
items.summary: Proprietary news archives assign stories to firms, so reproducing a financial study often requires access to both the articles and the vendor's assignments. CCFinance lets researchers reconstruct firm coverage under different selection rules by recording which version of a story was captured, which issuers it names and how often each appears. From 14.8 million English-language records in Fine News, derived from public Common Crawl News, we identify 5.22 million distinct, consistently dated articles with issuer links. Exact reconstruction requires the restricted snapshot and derived artifacts. We compare GLiNER and Stanza on 250 model-labeled article leads and assess issuer links and story focus against blinded model judgments. Estimated precision among 475 accepted links is 96.8%.…
items.tldr: CCFinance reconstructs firm coverage from public news archives under different selection rules, using model-assisted labeling and validation, and shows how mention thresholds affect issuer-year counts and financial network measures.

items.title: DyLoMo-DiT: Dynamic Looped Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) scale model capacity by increasing both parameter count and computation. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants expand parameter capacity while keeping per-token computation roughly fixed, but still require substantial parameter storage. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Looped MoE DiT (DyLoMo-DiT), which reuses parameters rather than adding them: a weight-shared loop repeatedly applies the middle layers, while sparse experts allocate parameter capacity across tokens. This design deepens the network without adding parameters, freeing the parameter budget for other uses, such as more experts or more distinct layers. It also allocates compute dynamically, varying the number of passes across noise levels. Experiments show that DyLoMo-DiT makes more effective use of parameter and compute budgets, with further gains from assigning more passes to low-noise steps.…
items.tldr: A dynamic looped mixture-of-experts diffusion transformer reuses shared parameters and varies compute across noise levels, improving image generation quality under matched budgets.

items.title: Target-Part Preference Optimization for Part-Aware 3D Generation
items.summary: Part-aware 3D generation requires not only globally plausible objects but also complete, well-separated semantic parts, yet high-quality part decompositions remain too scarce to support large-scale supervised fine-tuning. We study whether preference fine-tuning based on Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) can adapt a pretrained part-aware generator from limited part-annotated data without architectural changes. We rank candidates generated with different random seeds against ground-truth (GT) geometric metrics, and select the (object, target-part) examples with the largest across-seed quality gap. Each selected example stores a seed pair whose two flow trajectories share one clean GT compositional latent and differ only in Gaussian noise. We derive a reference-relative target-block preference loss from FlowDPO that compares the two trajectories against a frozen reference model.…
items.tldr: Preference fine-tuning based on Direct Preference Optimization adapts a pretrained part-aware 3D generator with limited part annotations, yielding the best multi-part results at medium scale but less consistent gains under distribution shift.

items.title: Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation
items.summary: Visual creation demands expressive imagery together with precise control over text, layout, and structure. We introduce Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation, an agentic framework that connects these capabilities through Pixel as Code. Raster images are represented by learned discrete visual tokens, while structured artifacts use explicit programs. A shared generation-and-rendering interface connects these representations to visual feedback across images, vector graphics, webpages, and documents. A Nemotron-native harness coordinates planning and raster candidate selection, with targeted repair for editable structured and hybrid artifacts. To support this interface, we develop Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer, the autoregressive raster generator Nemotron-Labs-Image-30B-A3B, and the structured-code model family Nemotron-Labs-VisionCode.…

items.title: Seeing Is Locating: Spatial Awareness and Geographic Bias in Decision Language Models
items.summary: Decision models, which output probability distributions over candidate labels instead of generating text, are increasingly used as classifiers and evaluators for inputs associated with real-world locations. However, it remains unclear whether they can leverage spatial context and whether their predictions are geographically biased. We introduce GeoDecisions, a multimodal benchmark for evaluating the spatial awareness and geographic bias of decision models. GeoDecisions comprises two tasks: (1) geo-aware image classification, and (2) location rating on objective and subjective topics. Evaluating six decision models against supervised task-specific models, we find that spatial awareness requires vision: textual coordinates alone provide insufficient context for classifying everyday photos and satellite images. We also find substantial geographic bias.…
items.tldr: A multimodal benchmark evaluates decision models on spatial awareness and geographic bias across image classification and location rating tasks, revealing reliance on vision and socioeconomic biases, and proposes a training-free location-prior method to improve spatial awareness.

items.title: OWE-Bench: A long-horizon benchmark for measuring real-world engineering
items.summary: We present OWE-Bench (OpenWorldEngineer-Bench), a benchmark of 26 long-horizon engineering tasks written by domain experts in software engineering, physical engineering, machine learning, and scientific computing. Tasks range from optimizing kernels and designing an aircraft, to identifying the faults responsible for an earthquake. Each task requires significant domain knowledge and engineering work, with models averaging hundreds of millions of tokens per task. Solutions are scored on practical measures such as speed, cost and accuracy, both on provided cases the agent could test against and on hidden cases that an engineer would expect from the task description. The best-performing frontier model so far, Claude Fable 5.2, scores 54.6% and averages 211 million tokens per task. We highlight two findings.…

items.title: FATCAT: Fault Injection Attacks Targeting Chip-level Alignment
items.summary: Model alignment is the primary safety and security mechanism for enforcing refusal of malicious prompts in modern foundation models; yet, existing adversarial evaluations implicitly assume underlying hardware integrity. In this paper, we present FATCAT, the first physical fault-injection attacks capable of eliminating refusal in modern large language and vision-language models. Specifically, we present a non-invasive electromagnetic (EM) fault injection attack targeting GPU-accelerated Systems-on-Chip with physical access, requiring neither software execution privileges nor model-layer access.…

items.title: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models
items.summary: A foundation model for time series is pretrained once and then asked to forecast series it has never seen, so the evidence for it is its score on held-out datasets. Such datasets are scarce, and a few public leaderboards carry most comparisons, yet none of them states how small a difference its datasets can detect. We call that quantity the resolution of a board and introduce Vernier, a tool that computes it from the files a board already publishes. Vernier also reports which entries a board cannot separate from its leader and whether its order changes when unrelated parties submit. GIFT-Eval resolves 6.8 rank places, and its displayed neighbours sit 0.91 apart. The ten places of its top ten hold fewer than two resolvable steps. fev-bench, Chronos Benchmark II and TIME show the same pattern: their resolution is 3.6 to 19 times the gap between neighbours.…
items.tldr: A tool called Vernier measures the smallest score difference a time-series forecasting leaderboard can distinguish, showing that most boards cannot separate top entries and that ranking order can change with pool composition.

items.title: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
items.summary: AI agents now run statements against production databases, and several of the incidents that followed deleted production data, which came back only through backups or the provider's help. We ask what decides the damage when such an agent makes a mistake: the model, a guard layer in front of the database, or the database engine itself. The study has two preregistered layers. In Layer A, a frozen library of 22 canonical mistakes is applied by script, with no model involved, to four relational engines under five permission arms and two recovery arms, followed by an engine-native recovery drill (792 cells; 874 drill runs including 10-minute repeats).…

items.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers
items.summary: As large language models (LLMs) are used in more and more new tasks, context engineering becomes a fundamental method to efficiently steer LLMs by constructing instruction prompts or metadata without intensive training. A growing number of LLM context engineering (LCE) approaches automate the task by casting the LLM itself as the engineer that draws generalizable instructions or experiences from offline trials as context. Although these methods resemble how humans learn from experiences, it remains unclear when and how LLMs can engineer effective context from data.
