items.title: Handover Cost Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks using an RL-based Multiple-Column Selection Strategy via Branch-and-Price
items.summary: Next-generation wireless networks increasingly rely on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites for broad coverage and low latency, making efficient handover management essential. We formulate satellite handover as a combinatorial optimization problem, assigning each ground user to exactly one capacity-limited, visible satellite while minimizing network handover costs. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based branch-and-price (B&P) framework with learned multiple-column selection (MCS) to accelerate column generation while retaining exact dynamic programming pricing. We also develop two lightweight heuristic policies: handover-aware visibility duration (HAVD) for online decisions and congestion-aware predictive (CAP) for offline planning.…

items.title: Your Diffusion-Based Driving Planner Only Needs a Nudge
items.summary: Diffusion-based planners capture the multimodality of human driving behavior well, yet covariate shift in closed-loop driving can lead them to generate trajectories that result in collisions or road departures. Reinforcement learning (RL) finetuning offers a promising way to tackle this issue, but applying it to diffusion-based planners is complicated by their iterative denoising process and receding-horizon execution. We find that small adjustments to the planned trajectories can prevent many of these unsafe outcomes. Motivated by this observation, we propose PlanNudge, which preserves the learned planning capabilities of a pretrained diffusion-based planner by freezing it and trains a lightweight policy that we call the nudge policy. At each planning step, the nudge policy outputs a nudge, a two-dimensional adjustment of the speed and curvature of the plan from the frozen planner.…

items.title: When Can a Rewiring Control Test LLM Weight Readers? C2 and an Eligibility Protocol
items.summary: Large language models can predict the outputs of small neural networks from raw weights, but success could reflect recognition of weight-space regularities (fingerprints) rather than computation, and function-preserving controls cannot tell these apart. We propose C2, a counterfactual that permutes the columns of a network's final linear readout: every other parameter, and the readout's singular values, norms and entry multiset, are unchanged, and the function can change in an exactly recomputable way; we verify that each evaluated permutation does. C2 separates fingerprinting from computation only under three conditions, which we state as an eligibility protocol: a strategy restricted to C2-invariant summaries must already predict the target; C2 must change a property specific to the rewiring; and the reader's identity must be attested. No natural setting we tested is eligible.…

items.title: GAG-Net: Graph-Based Anatomical Guidance Network for Pharyngeal Area Segmentation in VFSS Images
items.summary: Diagnosing sarcopenic dysphagia typically requires costly supplementary imaging such as CT or MRI to assess muscle atrophy, burdening elderly patients. The pharyngeal area at rest (PA_rest), measurable directly from videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS) images, is a promising biomarker that could eliminate this dependency, but repeated manual measurement has limited its adoption. PA_rest segmentation is further complicated by indistinct soft-tissue boundaries and clinical rule-based delineation criteria that data-driven models capture only imprecisely. We formulate automated PA_rest segmentation as a clinically defined measurement task, translating an implicit clinical measurement into an explicit landmark specification and annotation protocol developed with a rehabilitation medicine specialist.…

items.title: Decoding Transformer Dynamics via Koopman Subspaces
items.summary: We apply Koopman operator theory and Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) to characterise how large language models (LLMs) process different input topics. Treating the layer-to-layer evolution of hidden states as a dynamical system, we fit a linear Koopman operator and take the subspace spanned by its dominant modes as a per-topic spectral fingerprint. Four findings emerge. First, the depth map is near-linear: a single linear operator predicts each next-layer state to within approx. 18% relative error (interior variance explained approx. 0.99). Second, over the 57 MMLU subjects the fingerprint is topic-discriminative, matching the MMLU taxonomy at 0.72 nearest-neighbour purity and each subject's semantic neighbourhood at 0.75 any-hit@3. Third, it is a reproducible signature (split-half self-retrieval approx. 0.97$).…

items.title: Bridging Blind Spots With Words: Decentralized Multi-View Spatial Reasoning via Language-Constrained Communication
items.summary: As multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) get increasingly used as collaborative partners across embodied robotics, AR/VR, and multi-user systems, spatial reasoning is now often distributed across agents with partial environment visibility, necessitating spatial reasoning integration. Prior work in language-mediated spatial integration is however strictly limited to simplified two-agent scenarios. To address this gap, we first formalize the general problem of decentralized multi-view spatial reasoning, where N agents observe distinct viewpoints, exchange budget-constrained natural language messages, and collaborate to enable a listener to answer spatial queries. We then introduce a novel multi-view spatial benchmark to isolate queries that demand non-trivial multi-view integration.…

items.title: Beyond Evidence Coverage: Encoding-Time Access in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Cache-sharing multi-agent systems can retain every evidence token's representation while preventing cross-worker access during encoding. We test whether this coverage recovers joint-encoding quality using attention masks over two logical workers in frozen Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct models. Tokens, positions, and answer-time access remain fixed within comparisons. We evaluate 200 two-hop MuSiQue-Ans questions and 200 selected HotpotQA bridge questions. In data-layout seed 0, averaged across models, blocking access costs 5.6 and 6.8 F1 points relative to full access on MuSiQue and HotpotQA, respectively. Exposing the earlier worker's supporting paragraph improves F1 over blocked access by 7.6 and 6.7 points; equal-token non-support access provides no detectable average gain.…

items.title: Look Back: Reinforcement Learning with Counterfactual World Models
items.summary: Agents in complex, stochastic environments must contend with dynamics that can exceed their world models' predictive capacity and randomness that obscure the consequences of their actions. We hypothesize that, compared to imagining entirely new trajectories in such complex environments, it can be easier to transform observed trajectories with alternative actions. Counterfactual world models condition on observations to predict alternative outcomes under the same underlying environmental randomness, using experience as a reference for predicting action-dependent changes. We present a policy gradient estimator, REINFORCE Look Back (RLB), that uses counterfactual returns as baselines to distinguish action effects from environmental luck, and prove conditions for unbiasedness and variance reduction.…
items.tldr: Counterfactual world models that predict alternative outcomes from observed trajectories under the same environmental randomness enable a policy gradient estimator using counterfactual returns as baselines, improving policy learning when environmental dynamics are harder to predict than action…

items.title: Wactorz: Self-Writing LLM Agents That Discover, Repair, and Migrate at the Edge
items.summary: Most LLM agent frameworks build a crew that runs a task and exits. Physical environments (e.g., homes, labs, factory floors) need agents that stay up for months, survive their own bugs, and run on whatever hardware is already next to the sensors. We present Wactorz, an open-source runtime in which LLM-generated agents are long-lived, supervised actors: a planner turns a chat request into Python, compiles it into a new actor at runtime, and a supervisor restarts that actor alone, with its state intact, when it crashes. All coordination rides on MQTT, so agents can be spawned on, and live-migrated between, edge nodes such as a Raspberry Pi, and every internal event is a topic external systems can subscribe to.…

items.title: KernelShift: Benchmarking Kernel Optimization Across Evolving Hardware
items.summary: Efficient AI computation depends on hardware that evolves over time, shifting the strategies needed to implement performant code. For CPU kernels, a key evolving factor is the set of available architectural extensions, which expose specialized hardware instructions that change the techniques used to optimize kernels. We study how effectively coding agents use these new, potentially unfamiliar extensions to write fast code. We introduce KernelShift, a benchmarking pipeline and a set of environments for evaluating coding agents in kernel optimization across evolving CPU architectures. Its agent-assisted, human-verified pipeline turns code repositories into benchmark instances, and its environments let agents optimize code with feedback from the target hardware.…
items.tldr: A benchmarking pipeline evaluates coding agents on optimizing CPU kernels across evolving Arm architectural extensions, showing strong gains on established SIMD extensions but unreliable adaptation to newer matrix-tile programming models.

items.title: Polytropos: What Do Vision-Language Model Descriptions Make of a Cultural Object?
items.summary: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. Descriptions of cultures tend to turn particular things into types, and what a description loses shows what its describer lacks. We introduce Polytropos, a benchmark that measures what model descriptions of cultural objects keep of the particular object by turning each description back into an image and comparing it with the original photograph. On 374 objects from the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Getty, with 1,870 descriptions from five models and 230 written by curators, reconstructions are recognised as the recorded culture more often than the photographs, at 54.55% to 59.09% against 52.14%, yet 16% to 21% of objects change outcome and only 0.49% of reconstructions are identified as the…

items.title: Can an Agent Trust Its Own Zoom? Cross-Magnification Provenance Verification for Whole-Slide Images
items.summary: Visual agents navigate whole-slide images through magnified observations associated with claimed locations. However, a visually plausible observation does not necessarily originate from its claimed location, particularly across magnifications and in regions with similar tissue structures. We formulate cross-magnification provenance verification (CMPV) to evaluate whether visual evidence supports a claimed spatial association, recover the source when possible, and abstain when evidence is insufficient. We introduce PyraFault, a benchmark of 3.06 million coordinate-supervised examples from 2,200 cases across five TCGA cohorts, covering within-context substitutions, absent-source faults, and geometric perturbations. We further propose ZoomTrace, a claim-independent verifier that estimates the observation's source before evaluating its agreement with the claimed location.…

items.title: HealthFound: a health world model for quantitative reasoning on longitudinal health profiles
items.summary: Medical large language models have shown promise in medical knowledge retrieval and clinical reasoning but remain limited in quantitative reasoning over longitudinal health data, partly due to the lack of effective data construction and model training strategies tailored to large-scale prospective cohorts. Here, we present HealthFound, a health world model trained on 12.4 million constructed examples, including 14-year longitudinal biomedical records from 501,936 participants and datasets for medical knowledge and general reasoning. We propose a three-stage training framework comprising progressive curriculum supervised fine-tuning, rejection-sampled retention fine-tuning, and task-verifiable policy optimization. This enables the model to effectively parse heterogeneous quantitative data and perform robust quantitative reasoning about incident diseases and health trajectories.…

items.title: AI chatbots abandon sleep apnoea referral when simulated patients minimise symptoms
items.summary: Background: Patients increasingly consult free artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots about their symptoms, but these models may favour agreement with the patient over accuracy. In obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), where most cases in the general population remain undiagnosed and diagnosis depends on referral, this could validate symptom denial. We tested whether consumer chatbots maintain guideline-concordant referral when a simulated patient minimises symptoms. Methods: Seven guideline-concordant and standardised OSA vignettes (apnoea-hypopnoea-index, AHI 18-52 events/h; body mass index 28-42 kg/m2) were presented to five free chatbots (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek V4 Flash and Grok-4.3) under neutral and symptom-minimising conditions (10 simulated conversations per model-vignette-condition cell; N=700).…

items.title: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds
items.summary: AI-driven game development holds the potential to transform diverse human inspirations into interactive experiences. However, existing systems and benchmarks primarily focus on explicit development specifications, with limited support for adapting multimodal references and evaluating actual gameplay experiences. We introduce GameAnything, an open-source agentic platform that transforms multimodal inspirations into playable extensions of existing games through iterative development. GameAnything integrates coding agents with an independent playtesting critic, persistent development state, and reusable experience memory to support continuous refinement. We further present GameAnything-Bench, a benchmark spanning diverse reference modalities, game creation objectives, and gaming environments, with exploratory gameplay testing to assess both functional correctness and gameplay quality.…
items.tldr: An open-source agentic platform and benchmark enable iterative transformation of multimodal inspirations into playable game extensions, revealing that coding agents can adapt reference content but still struggle with playable interactions and precise modifications.

items.title: Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values
items.summary: Current MLLM methods largely focus on whether models attend to the right visual regions, implicitly treating spatial attention map as the primary key of effective visual perception. To examine this assumption, we introduce a medical VQA dataset with paired non-contrast (NC) and contrast-enhanced (CE) images that share corresponding anatomy while providing different cues. We show that this view is incomplete: across paired NC and CE medical images, MLLMs often exhibit similar attention patterns despite producing contrasting answers, while controlled bidirectional interventions induce substantially larger prediction changes on visual values than attention weights. These results identify the visual content retrieved through values as a critical factor in improving perception beyond spatial attention alone.…
items.tldr: Paired non-contrast and contrast-enhanced medical images reveal that visual content retrieved through value vectors, rather than spatial attention alone, is critical for multimodal model perception, motivating a distillation method that improves non-contrast inference.

items.title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Recently, GPT-6 Astra demonstrates strong generalization in robot control, yet limited disclosure of its training leaves open how such capabilities can be reproduced. We introduce nanoAstra, an approach to training vision-language models (VLMs) for generalizable manipulation that combines semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning (CP-SFT). nanoAstra represents robot behavior as semantic steps composed of reusable, parameterized action primitives, guided by explicit progress descriptions. Meanwhile, CP-SFT uses an explicit robot-specific system prompt to constrain manipulation outputs to a structured action space, aiming to focus adaptation on robot-specific contexts and promote specialization while minimizing interference with broader pretrained capabilities.…
items.tldr: nanoAstra combines semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning to train vision-language models for generalizable robot manipulation, achieving strong zero-shot success and faster streaming execution.

items.title: Layer-Wise Emergence of Human-Derived Object Dimensions in Deep Neural Networks
items.summary: Object recognition in the human visual system is implemented within a hierarchy characterised by increasing feature complexity. Here, we investigated whether human-derived dimensions of object knowledge become increasingly predictable from layer-wise activations in deep neural networks (DNNs), and how this predictability is related to architecture, learning objective, dimension type, and stimulus statistics. To test this, we predicted human-derived dimensions from layer-wise activations of multiple DNNs and transformer models trained on large-scale datasets. In trained DNNs, information relevant to human-derived object dimensions was largely absent in early layers, strengthened across layers, and peaked in later layers, in contrast to the flatter, non-progressive profiles we observed for raw pixel statistics and untrained networks.…

items.title: An open long non-coding RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
items.summary: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play essential roles in transcriptional regulation and chromatin organization, yet predicting their functional properties from sequence remains challenging because informative signals span both local motifs and long-range base pairing across kilobase-scale transcripts. Current RNA foundation models are restricted to short sequences and existing lncRNA prediction models narrowly focus on isolated tasks, leaving a dedicated foundation model notably absent. Here we present LncRFM, a dedicated lncRNA foundation model, supported by the LncCorpus pretraining data and the LncBench evaluation suite, which stand for a systematic framework to decode lncRNAs.…

items.title: Leveraging the largest harmonized epigenomic data collection for metadata prediction validated and augmented over 350,000 public epigenomic datasets
items.summary: Epigenomic data found in public databases often suffer from issues of non-standardization and incompleteness in their associated metadata. There are currently no automated approaches to validate or correct such missing or inaccurate metadata information. To tackle this challenge, we harnessed the extensive harmonized data and metadata provided by the EpiATLAS project of the International Human Epigenome Consortium (IHEC) to train EpiClass, a suite of machine learning classifiers that can predict key metadata (~98% accuracy), including experimental assay, donor sex, biospecimen source and sample cancer status. The development of these classifiers enabled the identification of a few mislabeled and low-quality datasets in the EpiATLAS project, while also completing with high-confidence most of the missing metadata.…

items.title: Deciphering the limitations of immortalized hepatocyte cell lines for the study of liver cis-regulatory elements
items.summary: Background: Immortalized cell lines are widely used to study transcriptional regulation. However, previous studies have shown that immortalization and prolonged culture can alter their regulatory landscapes, potentially compromising their ability to model native cis-regulatory element (CRE) activity. Hepatocyte-like cell lines (HLCs), particularly HepG2, are frequently used to study liver CREs, but whether non-cancer-derived HLCs, such as AML12, better recapitulate native regulatory landscapes remains unclear. Furthermore, cell culture conditions have been shown to influence gene expression and CRE activity, raising the possibility that optimizing culture conditions could improve HLC gene regulatory similarities to primary liver tissue.…

items.title: FHIRTrustBench: An Open Benchmark for Evaluating FHIR-Integrated Clinical AI
items.summary: Hospitals now use AI models to support clinical decisions. Increasingly, these models read patient data from electronic health records through FHIR, the standard format for exchanging health data. Before the data reach the model, they are converted: codes are mapped, units are normalised and records become model inputs. This conversion is rebuilt at every hospital, and when it fails, for example when a lab value arrives in an unexpected unit, the model still accepts the input and returns a score, and the error can pass unnoticed. Existing reporting guidelines ask authors to describe how input data were prepared and checked, but not in terms specific enough to verify a FHIR pipeline. Here we introduce FHIRTrust-Bench, an open benchmark that assesses what published FHIR-based AI systems demonstrate, from patient record to clinician.…

items.title: PhyCoVE: Benchmarking Physical Counterfactual Video Editing across Diverse Material Dynamics
items.summary: Physical counterfactual video editing turns a source video and a language-specified physical edit at a given execution frame into a counterfactual video that shows how the scene would evolve after the edit. Existing evaluations with counterfactual target videos mainly cover object removal or specific rigid-body motions, although real scenes also involve elastic deformation, fluid flow, and interactions among rigid bodies, elastic solids, and fluids. We introduce PhyCoVE, a benchmark of 533 cases on 110 source videos that covers rigid, elastic, and fluid dynamics in five interaction patterns, with edits that remove an object, change a physical quantity, or insert a new object.…
items.tldr: PhyCoVE, a 533-case benchmark, and counterfactual fidelity evaluate video editing models on physical counterfactual edits involving rigid, elastic, and fluid dynamics, showing that even the best model reproduces only about one seventh of the physical change.

items.title: PINE: Point, Instance and Normal Estimation in One-Step Diffusion Model
items.summary: Understanding a scene requires both geometry and semantics: geometry recovers its spatial structure, and semantics separates it into objects. Current models obtain the two from separate networks or separate passes. We present PINE, a one-step Omni Diffusion Transformer that predicts the point map, the surface normals, and the instance map of an image in one forward pass. PINE treats each map as a token stream, and a stream mask decides which streams interact. A camera-aware ray encoding positions every token by its camera ray rather than its pixel. Grounding attention adds the affinity of pretrained DINOv3 features to the attention logits. Trained on only 139K synthetic images for geometry, PINE achieves state-of-the-art point maps whether or not intrinsics are given and the best average rank on surface normals.…

items.title: Align the Pair, Not the Sample: Representation Alignment for Faster and Better One-Step Generato
items.summary: Representation alignment markedly accelerates diffusion training, but one-step generators raise a question that diffusion does not: which training path should receive the loss? A one-step generator sees two kinds of inputs. Corrupted real images come with their clean counterpart, which provides an instance-paired target. Samples generated from pure noise have no corresponding real image, yet this is where the final model operates. We study this question on Priming, which trains one-step generators from scratch by reconstructing corrupted images and then matching feature distributions with optimal transport. Aligning the generative path, the natural choice, collapses recall (0.45!to!0.15--0.25) in all 17 configurations we test, including five target constructions and loss weights down to 0.05.…
items.tldr: In one-step generator training, aligning the paired reconstruction path rather than the generative path improves recall and sample quality while accelerating both training stages and lowering FID.

items.title: ApexID: Hierarchical Learning for Multi-Species Animal Re-Identification
items.summary: Animal re-identification (Re-ID) must distinguish individuals across species and capture conditions. We introduce ApexID, a hierarchical SphereFace2-based loss that integrates global identity discrimination with balanced animal-category supervision. Using 132,533 images curated from 19 public datasets, we evaluate three model families and four objectives on four external datasets with observation-aware retrieval protocols. ApexID achieves a dataset-averaged Rank-1 accuracy of 64.89% with ConvNeXt-Small and an mAP of 32.54% with MIEW-ID, outperforming their pretrained reference models. On elephants, a category absent from animal Re-ID training, our ConvNeXt-Small variant achieves the highest retrieval performance among the fourteen evaluated configurations. Scores vary by backbone and dataset, and open-set evaluation reveals remaining discovery challenges.…
items.tldr: ApexID, a hierarchical SphereFace2-based loss combining global identity discrimination with balanced category supervision, improves animal re-identification and transfer to unseen datasets and species, though performance varies by backbone and open-set evaluation remains challenging.

items.title: The norm axiom and factor hyperfields
items.summary: Touchard and the author asked whether every valued hyperfield, in Krasner's sense with the norm axiom, is of the form H_ρ(K): a valued field K read up to relative error ρ. The question turns on the norm axiom. If a valued hyperfield is a quotient K^times/Tcup{0} of a field, the norm axiom forces T=1+m_ρ for a valuation on K. This completes the proof of a published proposition, and it makes the question equivalent to asking whether every Krasner valued hyperfield is such a quotient. For value group Z we prove directly that it is. Without the norm axiom the answer is negative. Layering a hyperfield over a non-trivial ordered abelian group gives a factor hyperfield exactly when the hyperfield itself is one, so Massouros's hyperfields yield hyperfields with a non-trivial valuation, satisfying all the other axioms, that are not factor hyperfields. The general question remains open.

items.title: SynTrustBench: Benchmarking Synthetic Clinical Data with Calibrated False-Positive Rates and Certified Limits of Detection
items.summary: Medical research requires large volumes of patient data. Such data are difficult to obtain because of strict privacy regulations. Artificially generated data (synthetic data) promise to share data safely, thereby bypassing any need to go through strict, time-consuming regulations. To test this promise, benchmarks have been developed to evaluate synthetic data on their safety and usefulness. However, the benchmarks themselves are rarely evaluated. We propose Syn-TrustBench, an executable framework for evaluating the fidelity, utility and privacy of synthetic clinical data. Unlike existing benchmarks, SynTrustBench does not assume its metrics are valid before testing them. For each dimension it evaluates, SynTrustBench estimates two properties.…

items.title: Who Makes the Decision? Auditing an Agentic LLM Pipeline for Illicit Cryptocurrency Transaction Monitoring
items.summary: Agentic pipelines that combine graph detectors, deterministic rules, retrieval-augmented generation and an LLM judge are being proposed to monitor illicit cryptocurrency flows and to write regulation-citing justifications for analysts. They are evaluated on end-to-end accuracy or on the quality of those justifications, and neither shows which component made a decision. We audit such a pipeline on the Elliptic++ Bitcoin dataset with decision-source attribution, a trace-level protocol with three layers: per-case actual causation, interventional Shapley credit, and mediation of upstream risk scores. A deterministic wallet-score override carries about 94% of the credit for flags, and a verification gate cancels most of the judge's own flags, which fall on licit transactions.…

items.title: DUO Policy: Bridging Human Video Coverage and Robot Precision for Fine-Grained Manipulation
items.summary: Human videos promise a scalable way to reduce expensive robot data collection, but the embodiment gap limits the resulting policies to coarse behaviors, and they fail at precise tasks such as insertion. Existing methods co-train or finetune a single policy on both data sources, treating each source as equally useful in every state: the policy either absorbs the embodiment error at precision-critical steps or spends scarce robot data relearning free-space motion. We observe that the value of each source depends on the state: human data is useful where precision requirements are low, while robot data is disproportionately valuable near precision-critical states.…

items.title: Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation
items.summary: Future missions will benefit from onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation to correct deviations from the nominal flight path caused by navigation errors and thruster outages. Onboard computing resources rarely allow the solution of a cold-started, long-duration nonconvex optimal control problem, especially in dynamically challenging regions such as the cislunar to translunar corridor of the Earth-Moon system. This paper develops data augmentation and training techniques that enable a neural network to predict accurate initial costates of the indirect method. A recovery trajectory is then built from repeated network queries in a computationally efficient guidance algorithm. Training data are produced by the backward generation of optimal examples method, extending prior approaches to the circular restricted three-body problem.…

items.title: TesseraFlow: Scalable Video Diffusion for Dynamic Medical Imaging Inverse Problems
items.summary: Generative priors are state-of-the-art for modeling medical images in image reconstruction tasks, but reconstruction with video priors takes tens of seconds to minutes per frame. Latent priors inherit the errors of their autoencoder, the memory of pixel-space whole-frame priors grows with the frame size, and pixel-space patch priors are slow for two reasons. First, their deep networks process every frame at full resolution at every sampling step, even though early steps resolve only low frequencies. Second, their samplers spend many network evaluations per sampling step on overlapping windows, multiple re-noising rounds, or backpropagation through the prior. We introduce TesseraFlow, a complex-valued pixel-space flow prior that reduces the first cost. A global encoder reads a low-resolution view of every frame once per sampling step.…

items.title: JEPA-Tuner: From Predictive Fine-Tuning to Asynchronous Execution of Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generate sequences of actions from visual observations, proprioceptive states, and language instructions. In embodied interaction, executing these actions influences subsequent observations and robot states, providing a natural predictive signal for policy learning. However, standard action-supervised fine-tuning does not explicitly capture these action-conditioned temporal dependencies in the guidance consumed by the action predictor. We introduce JEPA-Tuner, a predictive fine-tuning framework that regularizes the VLA's native policy guidance through action-conditioned future prediction. During fine-tuning, a predictor in JEPA-Tuner learns to match guidance encoded from a future observation given the current guidance and committed actions.…

items.title: RES: Accelerating Diffusion Language Models with Rolling Entropy Sampling
items.summary: A diffusion language sampler makes two choices for every position in its denoising window: where the next token comes from, and when the position is committed to the KV cache. Using the entropy-bound sampler in DiffusionGemma, we study two extremes of the second choice. Committing each token as soon as it is accepted removes the chance to revise it, which hurts when the entropy bound is relaxed to trade accuracy for speed. When accepted tokens are frozen, macro accuracy falls from 73% to 20% as the bound is relaxed, while the unfrozen sampler stays near 70%. Committing a whole block at once wastes computation, since tokens converge in a largely left-to-right order and more than half of the window holds already-final tokens by twenty denoising steps.…

items.title: HyperHarness: Learning to Generate Personalized Agent Harnesses from User Histories
items.summary: Personalized LLM agents rely on an agent harness, the surrounding memory and control code, to connect user history with downstream decisions. Existing methods typically employ either a single shared memory workflow across all users, which is efficient to deploy but cannot adapt how evidence is retrieved and interpreted across diverse histories, or per-user harness optimization, which customizes behavior for each user but requires costly repeated candidate evaluation at deployment and suffers from sparse, noisy supervision in raw logs. To address this trade-off, we present HyperHarness, a framework that learns a shared history-to-harness generator to synthesize executable, user-specific retrieval and answer-guidance code directly from user histories.…

items.title: Distributed Interactive Conformal Prediction for Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Multi-agent systems increasingly rely on learning-enabled components and distributed algorithms for perception, estimation, and control, introducing uncertainty that makes it challenging to satisfy mission requirements. Conformal prediction quantifies uncertainty with distribution-free guarantees, but existing methods do not address the challenging combination of dependence among robots, distributed calibration, and the distribution shift induced when calibrated uncertainty bounds modify the closed-loop system. We introduce Multi-Agent Interactive Conformal Prediction (MA-ICP), a distributed framework for computing robustness margins in heterogeneous systems to satisfy mission requirements with high probability.…

items.summary: text-generation / peft

items.title: Population-Based Post-Training for Large Language Models
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is one of the most popular post-training paradigms for large language models. RLVR typically trains a single model under hyperparameters chosen before training begins, while researchers tune hyperparameters across consecutive runs. We introduce Population-Based Post-Training (PBPT), which trains several models in parallel and lets the training process do the tuning through population-based training. PBPT periodically evaluates models on a validation set. High-performers are duplicated and their hyperparameters perturbed to explore new configurations. Low-performers stop training and are replaced by these copies. On reasoning benchmarks (Enigmata, Nemotron) and interactive tool-use environments (Gaia2, AppWorld), PBPT produces stronger agents than compute-matched groups of independent RLVR learners.…

items.title: Mind the Trap As LLMs Guess the Data Model: Grain-Aware Guards Against Fan-out in Text-to-SQL and Its Benchmarks
items.summary: Text-to-SQL systems built on large language models (LLMs) often aggregate over one-to-many and many-to-many joins, a classic trap: when the joined rows repeat an entity, a SUM or COUNT counts it more than once, yet the query runs and returns a plausible number. We characterize these fan-out errors by one condition on the relation an aggregate reads, which depends on two facts a schema does not show: each measure's grain, and how many rows a join on each key repeats. An audit that tests the condition on the data finds distorted gold answers for 4.2% of the dev questions of BIRD, a widely used benchmark, and BIRD's later, independent revision changed 44% of the answers the audit flags as definite fan-out, against 16% of unflagged ones. We release BIRD-FanOut, 486 BIRD questions with reviewed gold, and GrainTraps, synthetic questions that set this trap and related ones.…

items.title: Mirrored Min-of-K Training
items.summary: Min-of-K (MoK) training is widely used to train models that produce diverse outputs from random noise. For each target, it draws K outputs from the model and backpropagates only through the one closest to the target. However, MoK generally does not make the generated distribution match the data distribution. In this paper, we analyze the MoK bias across all values of K and show that tuning K shifts between failure modes, from mode dropping at small K to distribution flattening at large K. We further prove that every nontrivial loss based only on target-candidate distances fails to recover some data distribution, since these distances do not reveal how the candidates are placed relative to each other.…

items.title: DoC: Learning to Defer or Commit for Timely, Accurate, and Stable Conversational Diagnosis Prediction
items.summary: Conversational diagnosis prediction requires accurate, early, and stable predictions from ongoing clinical dialogue, yet dialogue-level labels do not specify when to commit. We propose a two-phase framework for learning deferral and diagnosis decisions. First, iterative commitment-boundary estimation constructs Defer/diagnosis supervision without annotated commitment times. Second, Defer-aware supervised fine-tuning initializes a policy, refined through reinforcement learning with trajectory-level rewards for timeliness, first-commit accuracy, and post-commit stability. On EMSDialog and MediTOD, DoC commits early, achieving the highest first-commit accuracy among post-trained methods (76.7%/51.2%) and the lowest post-commit error overall (16.4%/48.3%).

items.title: Elicitation format changes zero-shot classification accuracy in a medical vision-language model: a two-center evaluation on colorectal histopathology
items.summary: Background. Verbalized confidence from a hosted medical vision-language model is usually treated as packaging around an unchanged prediction. Methods. We held a nine-class colorectal histopathology prompt fixed except for the requested response format and evaluated MedGemma-27b-it on 10,004 validation and 7,180 external-center PathMNIST patches, with preregistered endpoints, randomized ties, and random floors recomputed for each patch set. Results. Requesting probabilities over all nine classes instead of a ranked top-3 reduced accuracy by 14.8 points on validation, -0.1475 [-0.1594, -0.1353], and 13.4 at the external center, -0.1341 [-0.1484, -0.1196], against chance accuracy of 0.1111.…

items.title: Diagnosing Verbalized Confidence in a Medical Vision-Language Model for Selective Prediction on Colorectal Histopathology Patches
items.summary: Flagging uncertain histopathology patches for specialist review needs a confidence that is higher when the model is right. We test whether an open medical vision-language model emits one. MedGemma-27b-it and its base Gemma-3-27b-it were run zero-shot under one prompt on 10,004 PathMNIST validation patches and 7,180 patches of a patient-disjoint external cohort. Both are too inaccurate to deploy (40.6% and 35.5%); the object of study is the confidence. MedGemma's verbalized confidence puts 96% of patches at one value; its confidence-correctness AUROC is 0.499 and 0.528, and routing by it moves selective-accuracy AUC by -0.004 and +0.037. Gemma-3 spreads its confidence over nine values, reaches AUROC 0.70, and gains +0.114 and +0.115. MedGemma's label-token probabilities do not rescue it: their validation advantage reverses where the top-20 alternatives include every class.…

items.title: CLASP: Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling for Zero-Shot OOD Detection using Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) enable zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in medical imaging, yet existing approaches often rely on final-layer confidence or entropy-based layer selection, potentially missing complementary information. We show that low in-distribution (ID) confidence entropy does not reliably predict OOD discrimination. We introduce CLASP (Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling), an ID-only framework that jointly models layer--prompt responses and visual features. CLASP ranks visual encoder layers using Gaussian conditional mutual information and selects a compact subset through anchored spectral selection, without fixing the number of layers. It then combines the selected layer--prompt profiles with PCA-compressed visual embeddings and fits a single shrinkage-regularized Gaussian.…

items.title: World Models for Ocean Engineering: A Critical Review of Maritime Autonomy, Adaptive Latent Prediction, Digital Twins, and Biodiversity Monitoring
items.summary: Marine robots face partial observability, non-stationary dynamics, and sparse communication, motivating WMs that learn compact predictive states for planning. This review develops a functional taxonomy of WMs for ocean engineering, focusing on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) and AdaJEPA's test-time adaptation within model predictive control, mapping them to navigation, adaptive sampling, digital twins, and biodiversity monitoring, and separating demonstrated evidence from prospective applications. The synthesis identifies key Gaps: benchmarks, uncertainty calibration, safe adaptation and proposes a research agenda for physics-informed, deployment-adaptive marine WMs validated through simulation and field missions.

items.title: aleemssg/Qwen3-1.7B-Tool-Agent
Learning Land-Surface Hydrology World Model from Satellite Observations
items.summary: A world model should tell us not only what will happen, but what would happen under a different action. Learned Earth models now forecast remarkably well, yet forecast skill says little about what their state means or how it responds to a changed driver. We build LandWM, a world model of land-surface water in which rain is the action, learned from seven years of SMAP and CYGNSS observations: physical observation operators tie its latent state to soil water, and a mass-conserving balance governs how that state responds to rain. Over the U.S. Southern Great Plains, the model, never shown a soil-moisture value, tracks 28 in-situ probes as well as the operational SMAP Level-4 product, even from CYGNSS alone, and a storm added to the forcing of a station's cell wets its soil as natural storms wet the probes.…

items.title: Micro Operational Robustness of LLMs on Code Generation
items.summary: It is now common practice in software development for large language models (LLMs) to be used to generate program code. It is desirable to evaluate the robustness of LLMs for this usage. This paper is concerned in particular with how sensitive LLMs are to variations in descriptions of the coding tasks. However, existing techniques for evaluating this robustness are unsuitable for code generation because the input data space of natural language (NL) descriptions is discrete and sparse. To address this problem, we propose a robustness evaluation method called scenario domain analysis, which aims to find the expected minimal change in the NL descriptions of coding tasks that would cause the LLMs to produce incorrect outputs.…

items.title: Nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in {-1,0,1}
items.summary: We determine all nilpotent tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$. The problem reduces to describing the set $\cN_n$ of pairs $(d,b)\in\{-1,0,1\}^n\times\{-1,1\}^{n-1}$ for which the tridiagonal matrices with diagonal $d$ and with products $b_k$ of opposite off-diagonal entries have characteristic polynomial $λ^n$. We show that $\cN_n$ is obtained from $\cN_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ by one of two explicit ``folding'' operations, according to the parity of $n$. As a consequence, $\cN_n$ is non-empty precisely when $n=1$ or $3\cdot2^j-1\le n\le2^{j+2}-1$ for some $j\ge0$, in which case it has $2^{\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor}$ elements. This yields a formula for the number of nilpotent $n\times n$ tridiagonal matrices with entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$, which begins $1,9,73,585,4809,39113$. The case $d=0$ is a conjecture of Corless, established in an earlier paper.…

items.title: When Rubrics Do Not Decide: Silent Value Completion in LLM Evaluation
items.summary: Multi-criterion LLM judges often evaluate responses without specifying how conflicting criteria resolve, leaving the winner undetermined even under exact criterion scores. Issuing a strict verdict without declaring the required trade-off premise constitutes silent value completion. We introduce TradeoffBench to isolate this failure by separating rule execution from response scoring. On authoritative criterion vectors, six open-weight non-reasoning judges pass all dominance and equality controls yet pick unsupported winners on 9%-81% of 1,345 conflicts. All 577 order-stable choices follow an explicitly banned majority rule. Reasoning-enabled configurations drop anonymous-vector violations to 2 in 9,720 judgments under an explicit rule, yet cannot bridge omitted trade-offs or divergent component scoring.…

items.title: DIPS-OjOS I: Project Design and Science Validation
items.summary: Automated pipelines and machine-learning algorithms are efficient at detecting standard planetary transits, but can miss subtle, non-periodic morphological anomalies. We present the pilot phase of DIPS-OjOS (Detecting Irregular Photometric Signals - OjímetrO Survey), a professional-amateur collaboration designed to develop and validate a scalable workflow for identifying irregular photometric signals in exoplanet transit light curves through trained visual inspection. The project targets starspot-crossing events, stellar flares, circumplanetary structures, exomoon-like signatures, and transit-duration or timing anomalies overlooked by automated searches.…

items.title: STRIDE: Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-Guided Skill Disclosure and Evolution for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Skill-augmented reinforcement learning enables LLM agents to reuse task-solving knowledge across episodes, but existing systems typically expose agents to a flat skill pool and update skills only from coarse, episode-level outcomes. This conflates two distinct uses of experience: a stable strategy that should frame the whole episode, and tactical know-how that should be retrieved only when the agent reaches a local execution gap. We propose STRIDE (Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-guided skIll Disclosure and Evolution), a framework that brings progressive skill disclosure into agentic reinforcement learning. STRIDE keeps the selected strategy visible as episode context, exposes a compact tactic menu, and loads full tactic content only after an explicit retrieval action.…

items.title: Controlled One-Click Benchmarking and Post-Fusion Recalibration for Support-Conditioned Medical Segmentation
items.summary: Sparse-prompt medical segmentation is hard to compare when prompts, supports, thresholds, and splits differ. This paper uses a controlled one-click protocol: each test image receives one positive foreground click, training-only support, validation-only checkpoint selection, and no test-time threshold tuning. We propose {Support-Aware Recalibration (SAR)}, a late post-fusion recalibration block for MultiverSeg that combines large-kernel spatial gating with squeeze-and-excitation channel recalibration after support--query fusion. BUSI, NerveUS-BP-present, and Kvasir-SEG are evaluated with matched 697 foreground-present sample budgets, shared splits/clicks, and threshold-free Dice-AUC/IoU-AUC.…

items.title: FormaFin: Verifiable Financial Analysis with Solver-Guided Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Formally verifying financial analyses generated by large language models (LLMs) remains challenging as financial rules are largely expressed in natural language and rarely have corresponding formal specifications. Training language models to formalize these rules is hindered by the scarcity of labeled data and reliable training signals, while confidential financial data favor small models that run locally. We introduce FormaFin, a framework that trains small open language models to translate financial rules into reusable SMT formulas. FormaFin integrates teacher distillation with reinforcement learning using an SMT solver to compute rewards from numerical thresholds stated in financial rules. We evaluate FormaFin on corporate loan monitoring, in which lenders check borrowers' financial figures against loan agreements.…

items.title: Beyond Invoice Volumes: Temporal Network Structure, Maturity Concentration, and Systemic Liquidity Exposure in SME Trade-Credit Networks
items.summary: Trade-credit invoices encode directed obligations whose temporal synchronization and counterparty concentration are obscured by annual volume totals. We audit 749,952 atomic B2B invoices from 2012-2023 (EUR 99.705B; 75,343 firms) from the pseudonymized Mendeley Data corpus (Esteva de la Rosa, 2026), separating 1,240 terminal 2024 bridge records (EUR 630.12M; 9 bridge-only firms) and 13 extreme-duration contracts (>3,650 days; EUR 297.75k). Using directed weighted graphs, HHI, Shannon entropy, CR1 shares, spectral centralities, and multi-cadence temporal operators, we formulate and benchmark a Maturity-Aware Network Exposure (MANE) indicator. Invoice values are heavily skewed: the top 1% hold 81.41% of value (Gini = 0.9742).…

items.title: NAT: Scaling Causal Neural Action Tokenizers Across Embodiments
items.summary: Action tokenizers let robot policies treat control as autoregressive next-token prediction. As these policies are trained on larger and more diverse datasets, they will need a universal tokenizer that can encode actions from many embodiments and data sources, including ones it has not seen. We study action tokenization at scale, training on 49k hours of action data from real-world robots, handheld grippers, simulation, and humans. We introduce Neural Action Tokenizer (NAT), a causal tokenizer whose decoder lets actions be executed as their tokens are generated. Across four simulation benchmarks, NAT outperforms FAST and prior neural action tokenizers when tokenizing unseen robot embodiments, and in vision-language-action models it outperforms FAST+ across four benchmarks and on a real robot when acting through its tokens.…

items.title: LIBERO-MOR: A Multimodal Robustness Benchmark Across the Vision-Language-Action Pipeline
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong performance on robot manipulation benchmarks. Translating this progress into reliable deployment calls for systematic evaluation of how policies respond to variations throughout the robot interaction loop. We introduce LIBERO-MOR, a multimodal robustness benchmark across the vision-language-action pipeline. Built on standard LIBERO, it covers five deployment-facing domains: vision, language, proprioception, action execution, and environment. The benchmark comprises 22 deployment-inspired perturbations, each evaluated at three severity levels across 40 tasks under a paired clean-perturbed protocol, enabling controlled and reproducible comparisons. We evaluate seven representative VLA models spanning diverse action-generation mechanisms.…

items.title: Random Projection Neural Networks for Phase-Field Models: Model Reformulation, Scaling, and Network Architecture
items.summary: Phase-field models, particularly the Allen-Cahn(AC) and Cahn-Hilliard(CH) equations, are widely used to describe interfacial dynamics, but resolving their sharp transition layers and stiff dynamics presents substantial numerical challenges. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free approach, yet optimizing large numbers of network parameters can be computationally demanding and may still yield limited accuracy. We develop a random projection neural network (RPNN) framework that combines first-order PDE reformulations with independent random-feature representations of the unknowns. By fixing randomly initialized hidden-layer parameters and optimizing only the output coefficients, RPNNs reduce training to least-squares problems amenable to Newton-type solvers.…

items.title: PhyMind: Physics-Informed Masked Autoencoding for EEG Foundation Models
items.summary: EEG foundation models are pre-trained almost exclusively with masked reconstruction through a free-form decoder, sometimes with hand-crafted spectral targets added, as in MANAS-2. We study what happens when that decoder is replaced by a generative forward model of EEG. PhyMind keeps a standard masked transformer encoder, but its decoder must explain the masked signal through 68 cortical regions, each driven by damped stochastic oscillators and an aperiodic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, projected to the recording's own montage by a fixed boundary-element lead field evaluated per derivation. Training combines masked reconstruction with a Whittle spectral likelihood, an oscillator-dynamics residual, a minimum-norm source prior and a penalised neural residual.…

items.title: Bias Cascade: Understanding the Gap Between Knowledge Alignment and Effect Replication in LLM-based Social Simulation
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate participants in social experiments. Existing research has primarily focused on aligning social knowledge and isolated responses, while overlooking whether simulations can reproduce the collective effects of social interventions. This distinction is critical due to a failure mechanism we call a $bias$ $cascade$: similar individual states can lead to different actions, while agreement on isolated actions can still produce divergent outcomes through dynamic interactions. As a result, models may produce accurate social judgments yet fail to reproduce the outcomes of classic human studies.…

items.title: Twisted Block Particle Filters: A Local Particle-System Change of Measure for High-Dimensional State-Space Models
items.summary: Block particle filters mitigate weight degeneracy in high-dimensional state-space models, but their normalizer estimates can remain highly variable. We introduce a twisted block particle filter (TBPF) that incorporates predictive guidance through an exact change of measure at blockwise resampling. The method guide-tilts one uniformly selected offspring per block, leaves the state-transition kernel unchanged, and computes the resampling correction using finite empirical guide averages. We prove that this correction exactly preserves the finite-particle block particle filter normalizer expectation, separating the effect of guided sampling from the approximation introduced by spatial blocking. Our analysis provides exact conditional local moments and a one-step conditional central limit result.…

items.title: EA-Bench: Measuring information and action efficiency under imperfect instructions
items.summary: Personal agents help users complete everyday work across digital applications. Many standard benchmarks assume that users provide sufficient information to solve a task. However, agents often encounter incomplete, distracting, or inconsistent information in practice. To systematically study agent inefficiency under such imperfect information, we introduce Efficient Action (EA)-Bench, which evaluates both tool calls and user interactions in work-related tasks. To our knowledge, it is the first benchmark to jointly evaluate tool-call efficiency and user-interaction efficiency under controlled missing, redundant, and conflicting information. We construct 63 base-task instances adapted from existing work-related benchmarks.…

items.title: Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models benefit from strong semantic representations that support object recognition and instruction understanding. However, precise manipulation also depends on resolving object locations and workspace relations, and on selecting actions with an estimate of how the scene will evolve. Existing geometry-aware methods make the current scene more explicit, while predictive methods model future observations or representations. Yet future information is often neither grounded in a control-relevant spatial state nor directly used to guide action generation. We introduce Spatially Grounded Latent Lookahead (SG-LL), which uses the grounded present as the reference for predicting an actionable near-future representation. A frozen spatial teacher first distills geometric priors into policy-connected spatial tokens.…

items.title: Pixel Auto-Encoder: Reconstructing Language Model Activations Through Pixel Art
items.summary: Interpreting the high-dimensional internal representations of large language models (LLMs) remains a challenging problem. Recent approaches have explored translating these representations into human-understandable forms, particularly natural language. In this work, we explore the use of images as an alternative target modality for interpreting LLM activations. As a first step toward this goal, we introduce Pixel Auto-Encoder, which converts intermediate LLM activations into $32 \times 32$, 32-color pixel art and reconstructs them for subsequent computation within the model. By encouraging the intermediate representations to resemble predefined concept images, we investigate whether LLM activations can be expressed visually while preserving the model's language capabilities.…

items.title: Improving semantic equivalence in research-level math formalization
items.summary: Formalizing mathematics in Lean is never a word-for-word translation of a paper: a Lean formalization changes definitions, strengthens hypotheses, splits arguments, and adds lemmas the paper never mentions. It stands to reason that a model that is good at autoformalization must be a good predictor of how a natural language source must differ from its faithful Lean formalization. With that in mind, we collect 4{,}076 audited examples of such changes from 832 Lean projects that formalize research-level mathematics, and use them to ask a practical question: how well can a model \emph{write} Lean inside a real research-level project that may contain tens of thousands of lines of code, and does training on discrepancies between natural language sources and their faithful Lean formalizations help? Our training set consists of 3{,}431 tasks from 141 repositories, and the test set consists of…

items.title: Beyond Raw IQ: Compact Semantic Representations for Task Oriented Automatic Modulation Classification
items.summary: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is an important component of modern wireless communication systems, but conventional signal representations can be expensive to store, process, and communicate, particularly under noisy channel conditions. This work investigates whether learned semantic representations can provide a compact alternative to high-dimensional in-phase and quadrature (IQ) representations while retaining robustness to noise. Starting from a 2048-dimensional IQ representation, we evaluate learned semantic representations with dimensions of 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. Across the evaluated configurations, a 16-dimensional representation provides the strongest overall trade-off between classification performance, robustness, and representation size. The resulting representation achieves a 128x compression ratio and a 99.22% reduction in dimensionality.…

items.title: Learning free energy across a differentiable temperature range by deep generative modeling
items.summary: Free energy governs the directionality, stability, and temperature sensitivity of physical, chemical, and biological transformations. Conventional free energy calculations, such as thermodynamic integration and free energy perturbation, often have to be performed at individual temperatures and are limited by the high cost of sampling an extensive set of thermodynamic states. Here, we introduce learned temperature-differentiable free energy perturbation (TD-FEP), a deep generative framework that learns a temperature-conditioned, invertible mapping between reference and target systems through data-free, energy-based optimization. TD-FEP thereby unifies one-shot state generation and free energy calculation across a continuous temperature range. We validated TD-FEP across a broad range of applications, including isolated molecules, periodic materials, and chemical reactions.

items.title: RadAG: Reward-Adversarial Attention Guidance for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment of Diffusion Models
items.summary: Diffusion and flow-based models have achieved remarkable success in generation, yet their samples often remain suboptimal in fidelity and text alignment. Two lines of inference-time methods address this: extrapolation guidance, such as classifier-free guidance (CFG) and its variants, and reward guidance, which aligns samples with reward models of human preference. Extrapolation guidance needs only forward passes, but it builds its reference by heuristic rules unrelated to the reward and therefore cannot steer sampling toward a given reward. Gradient-based reward guidance steers sampling directly toward a higher reward, but backpropagates through the entire generator at every step. This trade-off raises the question of whether extrapolation guidance can steer sampling toward a higher reward without a full backward pass.…

items.title: Synthetic EHR Generators Should Be Audited Like LLMs
items.summary: Synthetic electronic health record (EHR) generation is increasingly adopting large autoregressive models, yet privacy evaluation has not kept pace, relying heavily on similarity-based heuristics and aggregate metrics that can obscure patient-specific memorisation. We argue that these models should additionally undergo LLM-style memorisation audits at the level of individual patient records. We support this position by comparing membership-inference evaluations across four prominent autoregressive EHR generators, highlighting inconsistent evaluation practices in patient representations and attack procedures. We evaluate trajectory reconstruction from partial context and introduce randomly assigned patient-level canaries to distinguish memorised associations from clinical generalisation.…

items.title: DeRail: Escaping Trajectory Priors via Counterfactual Action Steering for Mid-Execution Instruction Switching
items.summary: Robots operating in the real world must often adapt when user instructions change mid-execution, yet current instruction-conditioned robot policies, including Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and World-Action Models (WAMs), are largely evaluated under fixed-instruction episodes. We study mid-execution instruction switching and identify trajectory hijacking as a key failure mode, where the policy fails to redirect sufficiently toward the switched target, with its post-switch behavior remaining fully or partially drawn toward trajectories associated with non-target tasks.…

items.title: HighwayVerse: A Chain-of-Inspection Benchmark for Highway Infrastructure Anomaly Understanding
items.summary: Practical highway infrastructure inspection entails progressive diagnostic reasoning from visual perception to maintenance decisions, yet existing benchmarks remain confined to isolated tasks, leaving Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) insufficiently evaluated across sequential inspection stages. Meanwhile, current datasets focus primarily on highway pavement defects, falling short of real-world inspection across diverse infrastructure components such as highway pavements, guardrails, glare screens, and drainage systems. To address these gaps, we formulate the Highway Infrastructure Inspection Progression Chain (HIIP-Chain), spanning Anomaly Detection, Anomaly Recognition, Condition Analysis, and Maintenance Resolution, and introduce HighwayVerse.…

items.title: DiscernBench: Evaluating Cooperative Discernment of LLM Agents in Institutional Settings
items.summary: The deployment of large language models in operational settings demands evaluation of judgment under institutional constraint. We introduce DiscernBench, a benchmark for evaluating cooperative discernment: the ability of an agent to determine whether to comply with, refuse, or escalate a request in an institutional setting. DiscernBench comprises scenarios derived from real-world incident reports across domains such as aviation, law enforcement, and emergency management. We evaluate eight LLMs across three decision-making configurations and analyze both final decisions and the intermediate judgments produced during multi-agent deliberation. Under disagreement, Final Responders exhibit model- and role-dependent aggregation patterns in which a lone specialist recommendation can disproportionately influence the collective decision, a phenomenon we term Minority-Signal Override.…

items.title: Transient coupling of Marangoni spreading and interfacial waves
items.summary: How does an initially non-uniform distribution of surfactant generate waves on a de- formable interface, and how do those waves then govern the redistribution of the surfactant? We answer this question for the linear Cauchy-Poisson problem of an axisymmetric interface between two viscous fluids, released from rest with independently prescribed distributions of surfactant and of interface displacement, by Hankel and Laplace transforms. In Stokes flow the pressure and the viscous normal stress of the Marangoni flow cancel in the nor- mal traction on the interface, for any viscosity ratio, so that the surfactant relaxes without displacing the interface: the coupling between surfactant redistribution and interface de- formation is inertial.…

items.title: Contrastive Gradient Guidance for Test-Time Multi-Preference Alignment of Diffusion Models
items.summary: Aligning pre-trained diffusion models with multiple context-dependent preferences requires adapting generation at test time rather than relying on offline fine-tuning, which requires hyperparameter tuning and a new training run for each preference trade-off. Existing approaches compress diverse preferences into a single scalar reward objective for fine-tuning or test-time guidance rather than directly reusing existing generative experts released for different purposes and obtained through different fine-tuning methods. In this work, we propose Contrastive Gradient Guidance (CGG), a test-time compositional generative framework that reformulates multi-preference alignment as a composition of distributions.…

items.title: VTLA-RL: Learning Visuotactile Policies for Load-Adaptive Grasping
items.summary: Vision-language-action foundation models learn general manipulation priors, but object mass and local slip are difficult to infer from vision alone. Changing loads require contact-driven grasp adjustments that demonstrations collected under fixed conditions may not adequately cover. We present VTLA-RL to study visuotactile grasping policies and their reinforcement learning (RL) post-training under varying loads. Our main approach shares a visual encoder between tactile-image histories and RGB inputs to jointly generate and execute motion and bilateral force targets in a unified action space. Mixed real and simulated demonstrations first establish motion and contact priors.…

items.title: richa3137/climate-stance-xlmr
Sharp Purity Based Entropy Bounds and Machine Learning Assisted Entropy Estimation
items.summary: Purity quantifies quantum-state mixedness, motivating the study of its role in controlling entropy variations. A sharp purity-based continuity bound is established for the von Neumann entropy of qubit states. The bound is attainable for every admissible purity difference and strictly improves the existing purity bound. In higher dimensions, an explicit sharp bound is derived within the family of pure states mixed with the maximally mixed state. Further continuity estimates are obtained for conditional entropy, quantum mutual information, quantum conditional mutual information, and squashed entanglement within specified bipartite and tripartite families. An application to machine learning assisted qubit entropy estimation illustrates how the sharp bound converts purity estimation errors into rigorous entropy error bounds.

items.title: Multimodal LLMs Know the Game but Assume the Real World
items.summary: Multimodal large language models can state the rules of a video game, but do they apply them when they only see the game? We introduce RuleCraft, 1,240 image questions over 155 Minecraft rules with outcomes verified in the game engine, each asked in text, on the image with the game named, and on the bare image. Six widely used models know the rules and recognize the game, yet answer the bare image by real-world physics: naming the game raises their accuracy on rules where the game departs from reality by 8.2-19.8 points on a main set and by 33.8-52.7 on a hard stress-test set. Their errors pick the real-world outcome, the gap is largest where the game leaves a scene unchanged, and reasoning traces state the game's rule, then answer by reality. On the main set, naming the game mostly swaps the real-world default for the game's.…
