items.summary: token-classification / gliner

items.title: Improving the Optimisation Landscape for Particle Mixtures
items.summary: Several methods in statistics and machine learning represent a predictive distribution as an equally weighted mixture of models, or particles, trained via the mixture predictive likelihood. However, we prove that the mixture predictive likelihood is poorly suited to gradient-based optimisation, because it does not identify how the mixture is decomposed across particles, so that a poorly matched particle can be starved of training signal. As a remedy, we study a convex combination between the individual risk, i.e. the average log loss of the individual particles, and the mixture risk. At the particle level, this regularised risk imposes a reverse-KL barrier on the responsibilities of the particles, so that no particle can be starved of training signal.…

items.title: Large Reported CHB-MIT Adaptation Gains Disappear with Pretrained Encoders and Matched Probes
items.summary: Dani and Liebe (2026) (DL) report that adapting the final encoder block of BIOT and CBraMod with self-supervised learning (SSL) improves CHB-MIT seizure-detection ROC-AUC by 36.2 and 29.5 points over linear probing. We investigate these results with their released code and an independent pipeline. The release loads pretrained weights for adaptation only when an otherwise unset configuration key is supplied, and its CBraMod probe reads the reconstruction head with dropout active. With pretrained initialisation and a probe on the encoder output in evaluation mode, the fixed-recipe adaptation gain on DL's split is -0.6 points for BIOT (95% interval [-3.8, +2.6]) and +0.01 for CBraMod ([-0.02, +0.04]) across five seeds.…

items.title: Uncovering Multimorbidity Patterns Through a Novel Randomized Clustering Algorithm
items.summary: Patients with several chronic conditions rarely share the same combination: in four years of the nationally representative Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS), we find 32,789 distinct combinations of two to seven conditions, and over 90% of those involving four or more occur in a single patient. Methods that search for common combinations discard most of this heterogeneity. We present the Randomized Length Sequential Clustering Algorithm (RLSCA), which links diseases by lift, a pairwise association measure counted only above a user-set support threshold. A mixed-integer program repeatedly selects and removes the group of conditions with the greatest internal lift, up to a random size; 100 iterations yield a database of clusters scored by size, rediscovery frequency, and body systems spanned.…

items.title: Partially canonical axes in large language model representations
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) develop rich internal representations of language, but whether their individual coordinate axes carry meaning, or whether meaning is encoded only in directions in representation space, is still an open question. A common assumption is that individual axes in LLMs are arbitrary. We here challenge this view: across 12 LLMs from six model families, the native axes are reliably more aligned with other models' representations, with human brain responses to language, and with interpretable linguistic features than randomly rotated axes that preserve the same geometry. The native axes nonetheless fall well short of the best achievable alignment, so LLM coordinates are not fully arbitrary but also not fully canonical: they are partially canonical.…

items.title: ThreatDefence/agentic-attack-detections
items.summary: Detection rules and IOCs for AI agent attack frameworks: ARTEX, Cairn, PentAGI, HexStrike, CyberStrikeAI, Strix, Hermes Agent, Agent Zero, RedAmon, Xalgorix, Pentest Swarm AI. KQL hunts for Microsoft Sentinel and Defender XDR, Sigma, Suricata, Zeek, YARA, Splunk, Elastic, STIX 2.1.

items.title: Degradation of Language Models under Controlled Load: Synchronization, Rule Execution and Misfires on the Background
items.summary: As the load grows, a language model makes more and more errors, but different processes stand behind this decline in quality. The model may lose the correspondence with the source text, it may keep its place in the text but execute a rule wrongly, or it may change a word that no rule concerns. In this work the degradation of a model under controlled load is separated into these three components: synchronization, rule execution and misfires. The load is set by rules that replace one word with another in a meaningless text, and each kind of load (the text length, the position of a word in the answer, the replacement density, the number of rules and the place of a rule in the list) is set separately.…
items.tldr: A method separates a language model's quality decline under controlled load into synchronization, rule execution, and misfires, then derives load-dependent laws that characterize each model.

items.title: FUSE: FUsing EEG-MEG in a Shared Embedding via self-supervised learning for BCI
items.summary: Combining complementary neurophysiological modalities offers a promising strategy for improving motor imagery (MI) brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but learning shared representations across modalities remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose a two-phase deep learning framework for multimodal EEG-MEG decoding that explicitly decouples representation learning from downstream classification. In the first phase, a convolutional encoder-decoder learns a shared latent representation by predicting the power spectral density (PSD) of EEG and MEG signals directly from time-domain activity, rather than using the conventional objective of reconstructing the input signal. In the second phase, the encoder is frozen and its learned representations are reused, without further adaptation, to perform the classification of the downstream MI-BCI task.…

items.title: Neural Circuit Mechanisms of Representation Transformation in Sequential Economic Choice
items.summary: Choices under sequential offers require the brain to encode a current offer, maintain its value, and compare it with a later offer before selecting an action. Prominent models explain choice through attractor dynamics that maintain stable, identity-preserving representations of offers and choices. However, recent recordings from monkey orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) during sequential-offer economic choices revealed strong order-based choice signals and weak identity-based signals. To identify the circuit principles underlying these representations, we trained recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to perform an order-based choice task and reproduce the observed psychometric behavior.…

items.title: MLE EEG Toolbox: A Personal AI Laboratory Assistant for Literature-Informed and Reproducible M/EEG Research
items.summary: Electrophysiological research increasingly relies on complex analytical workflows, yet integrating methodological evidence, computational execution and reproducibility remains challenging. Here we introduce MLE EEG Toolbox, a framework for building a personal AI laboratory assistant for electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) research. The toolbox integrates locally deployed AI, natural-language-guided analysis, literature retrieval and methodological comparison, and reproducible computational workflows. A constrained language model translates research instructions into validated, researcher-approved operations, while literature-informed guidance supports parameter selection and protocol reconstruction. Computational provenance enables transparent inspection and replay of analytical workflows.…

items.title: Lightness illusions and saliency maps for reflectance estimation are similar across a wide range of deep neural network architectures
items.summary: People perform many visual tasks that depend on having representations that remain correlated with surface reflectance despite large variations in illumination and context. This ability is known as `lightness constancy'. Developing image-computable models of lightness constancy has been challenging, but we recently showed that deep neural networks trained for reflectance estimation achieve good performance on some lightness tasks, and furthermore are susceptible to many of the same lightness illusions as human observers. Here we extend this work by testing whether these findings are specific to the network architecture we used in our previous work, or whether they generalize broadly across architectures and training procedures.…

items.title: BrainRoute integrates machine learning prediction with community-driven verification of blood-brain barrier permeability
items.summary: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a highly selective barrier that restricts the entry of many therapeutic agents into the brain. The lack of efficient methods for BBB permeability research and data management remains a significant challenge for central nervous system drug-development pipelines. Although BBB permeability data are available from multiple open sources, few platforms integrate these datasets with molecular exploration, predictive tools, and a structured process for community-supported data verification. Here, we present BrainRoute, an open platform for BBB molecular data collection, exploration, prediction, and community-supported verification.…

items.title: Harmonizing resting-state functional MRI data to increase sample size and to classify tinnitus brain connectivity
items.summary: Tinnitus, or ringing in the ears, is a hearing disorder that affects approximately 15% of human adults globally. The neuroscientific understanding of this subjective disorder is limited at present, partly due to a lack of sufficient neuroimaging data to compensate for the heterogeneity in the disorder; neural data acquisition is often impeded by low patient counts and doubled costs against scanning ample controls. However, with the increase in data sharing practices, data scarcity can be overcome with harmonization methods if scans from independent sites and studies are pooled successfully. To achieve data harmonization for limited data from a tinnitus neuroimaging study, we merged a modest fMRI dataset acquired in our lab (n=35) with age- and gender-matched samples from another large dataset, the Lifespan Human Connectome Project Aging (n=377).…

items.title: A Shared Neural Network for Highly Liked and Disliked Music
items.summary: While the neural correlates of music-induced peak moments of pleasure (e.g., chills) have been well studied, data on other types of aesthetic responses, such as judgments of beauty, goodness, or liking, are sparse. Among these, liking is of particular interest given its complex nature and its ubiquity in everyday, and musical, experiences. In this fMRI study, 26 participants listened to musical excerpts while continuously rating how much they liked the music. In addition, subjects provided an overall liking judgment at the end of each musical piece. Participants' individualized musical preferences manifested remarkably early and were sustained over time, with the value of the continuous rating at the end of each piece showing the strongest correlation with the overall ratings.…

items.title: NeuroSim: a clinically informed multi-disorder EEG simulator with personalized pattern injection and AI-driven neurological modeling
items.summary: Deep learning for electroencephalography (EEG) based neurodiagnostics is constrained by the limited availability of labeled clinical recordings. Datasets covering Alzheimers disease (AD), Parkinsons disease (PD), schizophrenia (SCZ), epilepsy (EPI), and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) are scarce, demographically narrow, and heterogeneous across acquisition sites, while privacy requirements restrict data sharing. Existing EEG simulators typically address a single disorder or trade biological interpretability for statistical fidelity. This study presents NeuroSim, a simulation framework that generates synthetic multichannel EEG with user-controlled injection of disease-specific patterns across five disorders and multiple severity levels.…

items.title: Improving Target-Adverse Event Association Prediction via Inverse Node Frequency Transformation to Mitigate Knowledge Graph Topological Bias
items.summary: Motivation: Identifying significant associations between therapeutic protein targets and adverse events (AEs) is a critical component of drug safety assessment. To accelerate the process, machine learning methods have been developed to predict these associations as edges in network data integrating molecular interactions and other key biomedical knowledge. However, these networks often suffer from topological imbalances where a minority of "hub" nodes determine the predictive signal. This "topological" or "degree bias" can lead to poor performance on novel or understudied targets where safety inference is most needed. Results: We introduce Inverse Node Frequency (INF), a generally applicable node degree-based approach for mitigating topological bias.…

items.title: Modelling Phenotypic Assay Noise for Multivariable Biomarker Discovery using Deep Neural Networks
items.summary: Accurately predicting cancer drug response remains a major challenge in precision oncology. Although some therapies are guided by clinically-approved biomarkers, these markers often yield limited predictive value and are unavailable for many drugs. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning approaches trained on large-scale cancer cell line pharmacogenomic screens offer a promising route to more comprehensive response prediction, yet they generally assume that phenotypic readouts are measured without error. This assumption is problematic because viability-based drug response assays are inherently noisy, potentially causing models to learn experimental artefacts rather than biologically meaningful determinants of sensitivity.…

items.title: PhageLysClass: Evidence-aware classification of phage lytic proteins using protein language models
items.summary: Phage lytic proteins are promising antibacterial and biotechnological candidates, yet uncertain annotations, modular architectures, and class imbalance complicate sequence-based classification. We developed PhageLysClass, an evidence-aware framework for recognizing lytic proteins and distinguishing Endolysins, Depolymerases, and virion-associated lytic enzymes. From 442,329 unique phage sequences, including 11,867 evidence-supported positives, we defined distinct candidate non-target, unlabeled, and challenge populations. Seven supervised and two positive-unlabeled tasks were evaluated across factorial redundancy and train-test homology conditions, yielding 2,240 and 768 experiments, respectively. Redundancy reduction influenced generalization more strongly than homology separation, with non-additive interactions between them.…

items.title: Curated annotations locate biological concepts in protein language models from layers to neurons
items.summary: Interpretability methods describe what a network has learned, yet their claims are rarely tested against model-independent ground truth. We argue that proteins are an ideal modality for interpretability since curators annotate functional sites residue by residue. Across three ESMC protein language models (300M-6B parameters), we show that conclusions depend on where models are read, how concepts are decoded, which units are examined, and how they are scored. Concepts become linearly readable along depth long before erasure impairs masked-token prediction, and 20-fold scaling shifts concept depth more than peak score. Most of a nonlinear probe's lead over a linear one reflects fitting and readout shape rather than nonlinear encoding. Over whole proteins, saturated metrics render feed-forward neurons indistinguishable from random rotations.…

items.title: MSGFLEX: An optimized end-to-end pipeline for proteomics and metaproteomics analysis built on MS-GF+ with a dedicated rescoring model XPECTRA
items.summary: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics workflows often face competing demands between identification sensitivity, false discovery rate (FDR) control, and computational scalability, particularly for metaproteomic datasets that require searching large and complex sequence databases. Here, we present MSGFLEX, an integrated end-to-end workflow that combines database searching, machine-learning based rescoring, and peptide-to-protein quantitative inference. MSGFLEX integrates three components: SPARX handles raw file conversion, and MS-GF+ database searching; XPECTRA is a cross-validated XGBoost ensemble that rescores peptide-spectrum matches by combining ensemble predictions with MS-GF+ search evidence through noisy-OR fusion model. QUANTIX provides protein quantification through multiple protein rollup strategies.…

items.title: Mapping whole-tissue spatial multi-omics at single-cell resolution with STEP
items.summary: Spatial omics technologies have revolutionized our ability to map transcriptomic, proteomic, or metabolomic profiles within tissue contexts. However, existing spatial multi-omics approaches emphasize clustering or domain identification from measured profiles, while a general framework for whole-slice mapping in measured and unmeasured areas at single-cell resolution across additional omics layers remains lacking. Here we introduce STEP, a computational framework that integrates probabilistic inference with deep learning for flexible integration of histology, spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT), single-cell, and/or multi-omics data. We validated STEP's advantages across diverse applications. Furthermore, STEP enables tri-modal integration of Xenium, CITE-seq, and imaging mass cytometry to map transcriptome-wide gene expression and protein profiles from a small gene panel.…

items.title: Analysing Spatial and Temporal Concept Drift in Forecasting Malnutrition Admissions in Kenya
items.summary: Forecasting malnutrition admissions could support anticipatory planning in health systems, but existing machine learning and statistical approaches have struggled to produce forecasts of practical value. We investigate whether this disappointing performance is partly attributable to spatial and temporal concept drift, whereby relationships between predictors and admissions differ by location and over time, respectively. We also examine whether adaptations to the modelling approach can mitigate these effects. We used malnutrition admissions from 44 subcounties across 14 counties in Kenya between 2015 and 2020, alongside potential predictors including normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and rainfall.…

items.title: Effects of an exercise prescription system (ACTIVE) on physical function in community-dwelling older adults: protocol for a single-centre, assessor-blinded, parallel-group randomised controlled trial
items.summary: ABSTRACT Introduction China is experiencing rapid population ageing and has the largest elderly population in the world. Physical exercise is one of the core strategies for promoting healthy ageing, and digital, intelligent exercise interventions hold promise as important tools for healthy ageing; however, clinical evidence remains limited. Methods and analysis This study is a single centre, assessor blinded, parallel group randomised controlled trial (RCT) designed to evaluate the effects of a knowledge rule based artificial intelligence exercise decision making programme (ACTIVE) on improving physical function in older adults, compared with a standardised, nonpersonalised exercise programme.…

items.title: A report-supervised EEG-language foundation model enables broad, interactive clinical interpretation
items.summary: Medical AI for complex signals such as electroencephalography (EEG) relies on costly expert annotations and predefined diagnostic labels that fail to capture the richness and nuance of clinical interpretation. Whether models trained on routine clinical reports can overcome these limitations while matching expert-supervised performance remains unclear. We introduce EEG Copilot, a biosignal-language foundation model trained on routine EEG-report pairs without dedicated task-specific expert annotations. Across two external datasets (6,078 EEGs), EEG Copilot performed on par with a state-of-the-art expert-supervised model across 11 shared findings (mean AUROC 0.80-0.81), corroborated by direct neurologist review of 200 EEGs.…

items.title: LCatlas: A Point-Of-Care Tool for Predicting Immunotherapy Outcomes in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
items.summary: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality, with a minority of patients experiencing durable responses to first-line immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Currently, there are no easily accessible tools to predict clinical benefit to first-line immunotherapy. To address this gap, we developed LCatlas (https://www.lcatlas.org), a point-of-care web application designed to predict immunotherapy outcomes and inform evidence-based treatment decisions. Using data from 79 NSCLC patients receiving first-line immunotherapy, we extracted demographic, clinical, and molecular features from electronic medical records and compared three independent approaches, statistical model (logistic regression), machine learning (XGboost), and AI model (TabTransformer) to identify the most effective predictor.…

items.title: Automated Screening for Generalized Anxiety Disorder Using Voice Analysis and Machine Learning
items.summary: This study evaluated machine learning models for screening elevated generalized anxiety symptoms from remotely collected neutral read speech in 1,788 adults from Botswana, Ghana, Nigeria, and Tanzania. Elevated symptoms were defined by Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7-item (GAD-7) questionnaire scores [≥] 5. Nine classifiers were assessed across nine scenarios defined by speech-task configuration (short sentence, long passage, or both tasks) and sex stratification under participant-separated, repeated nested cross-validation (CV). Acoustic-only models used the extended Geneva Minimalistic Acoustic Parameter Set, and context-augmented models added age, self-reported health, and sex where applicable.…

items.title: Clinician gaze as a supervisory signal for electrocardiogram deep learning: a matched-control proof-of-concept study
items.summary: Aims To assess what evidence is required to attribute an apparent effect of clinician-gaze supervision on an electrocardiogram (ECG) deep-learning model to gaze itself, separating target engagement, case specificity, and diagnostic preservation. Methods and results Ten ECG stimuli interpreted by 63 readers yielded 12-lead gaze targets for nine consultants and 20 clinicians. A pretrained 23-output ECG network was fine-tuned with gaze-only loss on eight ECGs per cross-validation fold. Held-out gaze cosine improved modestly (consultants 0.858 to 0.872; all clinicians 0.884 to 0.898), but untrained training-fold mean gaze agreed better (0.929 and 0.951). Lead-occlusion concordance was weak (mean Spearman {rho} 0.236).…

items.title: Building an Auditable Reference Standard for Clinical Information Extraction from Transesophageal Echocardiography Reports
items.summary: Objectives To develop an auditable, two-institution reference standard for intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) reports and evaluate whether reviewer disagreement identifies limitations in the underlying clinical information model. Materials and Methods We selected 300 reports (150 per institution) from 925 at the University of Pennsylvania and University of Washington using random sampling and enrichment for challenging documentation. Four trained abstractors applied a shared 39-variable V1 codebook. Independent paired comparisons included 297 reports; three historical reports contributed only to the final reference standard. Categorical agreement used exact agreement and unweighted Cohen's {kappa}; numeric left-ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) used exact agreement and mean absolute differences.…

items.title: A Blockchain-Enabled Federated Ensemble Framework for Privacy-Preserving Mortality Prediction Across Heterogeneous Healthcare Systems
items.summary: Objective: To test whether a smart contract that admits hospital-trained models to a shared mortality model only after peer hospitals verify their performance can exclude poisoned or substituted models, and at what cost. Design: Retrospective simulation study of a federated learning protocol. Methodology: In the Blockchain-Enabled Federated Ensemble (BFE), hospitals committed SHA-256 digests of locally trained XGBoost and random-forest models to a Solidity contract; peers posted digest-bound validation AUROCs, and the contract admitted models with a median peer AUROC of at least 0.70. Admitted models were pooled by weighted logit averaging (BFE-PW) or stacking (BFE-Stack) with federated recalibration. Code and drafts were produced with an AI coding assistant under the authors' supervision.…

items.title: The ITE-Transformer: A pre-trained foundation model for predicting individualized treatment effects from electronic health records
items.summary: Transformer-based foundation models have shown strong potential for modeling longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), yet existing models focus primarily on risk prediction rather than treatment effect estimation, which limits evidence generation. Here, we introduce the ITE-Transformer, a transformer-based framework that combines self-supervised representation learning from longitudinal patient trajectories with doubly robust causal machine learning for predicting individualized treatment effects (ITEs). As a result, our ITE-Transformer allows to study counterfactual questions of how an individual patient's outcome may differ under alternative treatment strategies.…

items.title: SIREN: Predicting RNA-Small Molecule Interaction using Language Models without Requiring Structure
items.summary: RNA-targeted drug discovery is constrained by the scarcity of resolved RNA tertiary structures and the conformational flexibility of RNA, which limit the applicability of structure-based virtual screening. Here, SIREN (Small molecule Interaction with RNA via sEquence-based predictioN) is presented, a sequence-based framework that ranks small molecules for a given RNA target directly from its primary sequence without requiring tertiary structure. SIREN integrates a pretrained RNA language model with molecular language model embeddings and physicochemical descriptors through an interaction network that outputs a target-specific compound-ranking score.…

items.title: Sequence-Derived Geometric Priors Enable Controllable Generation of Intrinsically Disordered Protein Ensembles
items.summary: Predicting heterogeneous conformational ensembles from sequence remains a central challenge for intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs). Sequence-to-ensemble models often entangle geometric inference with coordinate generation, obscuring error sources and limiting control over ensemble properties. Here we introduce MANTA, a C-level framework that separates these stages. An encoder derives geometric priors from protein language-model representations, and a graph-Laplacian decoder converts these priors into conformational ensembles. On a homology-held-out test set, replacing predicted priors with reference-derived priors under the same decoder reduces the median absolute relative radius-of-gyration error from 8.78% to 1.89%, identifying geometric-prior estimation as the dominant bottleneck in MANTA. Across an external benchmark of 27 IDPs, MANTA generates broad, locally valid ensembles.…

items.title: Sensory-processing traits generate dietary phenotypes that predict microbiome structure: an agent-based modelling framework
items.summary: Differences in gut microbiome composition are frequently reported across neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions, including autism and depression, and are often interpreted as reflecting underlying neurobiological variation. However, dietary behaviour is both a major determinant of microbiome composition and a downstream consequence of sensory and cognitive processes. To investigate whether microbiome differences can emerge through behavioural pathways alone, I developed a minimal agent-based model linking sensory-processing traits, dietary behaviour, and microbiome structure. Agents were characterised by latent sensory drive, predictability preference, and context sensitivity, which influenced food selection through reinforcement learning and stochastic environmental interactions.…

items.title: Deep learning design and in vivo validation of Müller glia-specific cis-regulatory elements
items.summary: Effective recombinant adeno-associated virus gene therapies require promoters that are compact and cell-type-specific. Ideally, promoters should also exhibit functional conservation when tested in model organisms to ensure that preclinical findings translate reliably to human patients. Here, we introduce a deep learning framework for designing cis-regulatory elements (CREs) meeting these criteria, applied to retinal Muller glia (MG). Using single-cell chromatin accessibility data from human and mouse retinas, we trained species-specific models to predict cell-type accessibility, and designed compact CREs using two complementary strategies. In silico validation predicted that the designed CREs exhibit high MG-specific accessibility (on-target) in both species with minimal off-target accessibility across hundreds of human cell types and tissues.…

items.title: Automated echocardiography image quality assessment and its association with AI performance
items.summary: Background Echocardiographic image quality influences clinical interpretation, yet its definition remains subjective and its impact on artificial intelligence (AI) systems has not been systematically evaluated. We developed EchoQuality, a deep-learning model for automated echocardiography quality assessment, and quantified the effect of image quality on AI performance across a broad range of tasks. Methods A multidisciplinary co-creation process established a definition of echocardiographic image quality, which was used to annotate 6,474 videos for EchoQuality development and internal testing, and 1,000 videos for external testing.…

items.title: Real-world adherence to guidelines in acute severe ulcerative colitis: automated assessment using large language models
items.summary: Background and Aims: Acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) is a medical emergency which requires close guideline adherence for optimal outcomes. However, measuring real-world adherence to guidelines and identifying guideline deviations are labor-intensive. We assessed how well a large language model (LLM) based framework can measure real-world adherence to ASUC guidelines and identify reasons for deviations. Methods: The retrospective study focused on clinician adherence to the 2025 American College of Gastroenterology guidelines on ASUC. A multi-agent GPT-5 framework first reviewed inpatient health records to confirm ASUC status. Then for each guideline, it assessed whether it was applicable, recommended by consultants, ordered, or executed. This system was benchmarked against manual chart review.…

items.title: Beyond Consensus: Human Ground Truth, Expert Disagreement, and Clinical Relevance in Pathology AI
items.summary: Human consensus is often treated as ground truth in clinical artificial intelligence (AI), yet greater agreement does not necessarily ensure greater clinical relevance. We investigated how expert panel size, composition, and consensus formation influence the reproducibility and clinical relevance of reference standards across three independent pathology cohorts evaluated by international expert pathologists: 50 transbronchial lung cryobiopsy cases from patients with interstitial lung disease assessed by 27 pathologists, 95 resected lung adenocarcinomas evaluated by 11 pathologists, and 596 images of pulmonary granulomatous lesions evaluated by 12 pathologists.…

items.title: Electronic Health Record-Based Machine-Learning for Cardiac Arrhythmia Identification in Adults with High-Risk Chronic Disease: Model Development and Validation Study
items.summary: Background: Cardiac arrhythmias may remain unrecognized in adults with chronic disease. Established risk scores primarily address atrial fibrillation. Objective: To develop and internally evaluate an electronic health record (EHR)-based machine-learning model to identify patients more likely to receive a documented cardiac arrhythmia diagnosis. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated EHR data (2018-2025) from one healthcare organization among adults with type 2 diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chronic kidney disease, or coronary artery disease. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were compared. XGBoost was selected using internal validation, reduced to 30 features using Shapley additive explanations, and evaluated in a holdout set with data ending one day before the index date.…

items.title: Discovery and Cross-Omic Replication of a Candidate Plasma Proteomic Signature for Anti-TNF Response in Crohn's Disease
items.summary: Background and Aims: Despite expanding therapeutic options for Crohn's disease (CD), treatment selection remains largely empiric. Identifying biomarkers linking inflammatory endotypes to treatment outcomes could inform first-line therapy selection. We sought to identify baseline plasma proteins associated with clinical, biochemical, and endoscopic outcomes in patients with CD receiving anti-TNF therapy. Methods: In this prospective multicenter cohort, children and young adults with CD initiating infliximab or adalimumab underwent plasma proteomic profiling at baseline and months 3 and 12 using SomaScan v4.1 (7,322 analytes) with deep remission (clinical and endoscopic) as the primary outcome. Rank-based composite correlation analysis identified candidate proteins associated with prespecified treatment outcomes, followed by functional enrichment analyses.…

items.title: Automated aortoiliac calcification segmentation from arterial-phase computed tomography scans: development and validation
items.summary: Introduction: Arterial calcium is widely used as a biomarker for coronary artery disease but is underutilized in peripheral artery disease (PAD) due to challenges in automated measurement. We developed a fully automated deep-learning pipeline for aortoiliac calcium measurement from arterial-phase, contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT angiography (CTA). Methods: Two nnU-Net models perform aortoiliac arterial segmentation and identification of calcified voxels. We trained on 56 CT scans and validated on 106 scans by comparing the pipeline's calcium estimation from CTA against calcium burden on corresponding non-contrast phase CT within manually segmented arterial contours across radiodensity thresholds of 100-1,000 HU.…

items.title: Explicit Style Extraction for Personalized Long-Form Text Generation
items.summary: Personalized long-form generation asks a language model to write new text the way a specific user would. The standard recipe, retrieval-augmented generation, places a few of the user's past texts in the prompt but leaves the model to decide what to take from them. We introduce StylePrism, a taxonomy of 28 stylistic aspects in seven categories, and SP-Refine, an inference-time method that makes style extraction an explicit step: the model first fills StylePrism with the user's patterns, quoted evidence, and habits to avoid, then drafts from the user's samples and revises the draft twice against this profile, guided by its own style scores. On the three long-form tasks of LongLaMP with three LLMs, SP-Refine outperforms LongLaMP's retrieval-augmented baseline in 25 of 27 ROUGE and METEOR comparisons, by 10.2% on average and by up to 35.8%.…
items.tldr: A method that explicitly extracts a user's stylistic profile and uses it to guide drafting and revision improves personalized long-form text generation over retrieval-augmented baselines.

items.title: SAVIOR: Sample-efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for OCR Representation
items.summary: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) pipelines and vision-language models exhibit high accuracy on standard OCR and document-understanding benchmarks, yet they systematically underperform on document patterns that are operationally critical in financial workflows. These patterns include vertical or rotated text, logo-embedded vendor names, fine-print regulatory clauses, degraded scans, and complex multi-column layouts. While underrepresented in public datasets, they constitute a substantial portion of real-world failure cases. We introduce SAVIOR, a sample-efficient data curation methodology that targets such high-impact failure scenarios to adapt vision-language models for robust financial OCR. We further propose PaIRS, a structure-aware evaluation metric that measures layout fidelity by comparing pairwise spatial relationships between tokens.…
items.tldr: A sample-efficient curation method and a structure-aware layout metric enable a fine-tuned vision-language model to improve OCR on challenging financial document patterns, achieving high word recall and document question-answering F1.

items.title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
items.summary: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extends residual connections to multiple streams and stabilizes residual propagation by constraining stream-mixing residual matrices to the Birkhoff polytope, the set of doubly stochastic matrices. In this work, we investigate how to effectively mix residual streams within the Birkhoff polytope. We reveal a mixing trade-off: when under-mixed residual matrices stay close to the vertices of the Birkhoff polytope, hyper-connections will degenerate into a set of nearly independent streams; when over-mixed residual matrices are concentrated around the uniform barycenter of the polytope, streams will become less distinguishable from each other. We theoretically validate our findings by bounding the cumulative residual mixing, stream difference and gradient difference of mixing coefficients across layers.…
items.tldr: Constraining residual stream mixing within the Birkhoff polytope via geometric contraction improves stability and scalability of hyper-connections in large-scale dense and mixture-of-experts model pretraining.

items.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
items.summary: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller that keeps playing from the screen without further model calls until it hands control back. To evaluate agents in real-time games, we build AFK-Bench, 120 diverse browser games grouped by how they respond to inaction and playable in real time or with the clock paused.…
items.tldr: A harness that lets multimodal foundation models emit primitive actions, open-loop macros, or closed-loop controllers improves real-time game performance and reduces API cost.

items.title: Non-penetrating World Models
items.summary: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent.…
items.tldr: A benchmark and lightweight framework leverage hidden states from frozen diffusion transformers to detect and prevent object penetration in interactive video world models, reducing physical violations and generalizing zero-shot.

items.title: Learning Video Foresight Reasoning from Unlabeled Videos via On-Policy Self-Distillation
items.summary: Video foresight reasoning requires vision-language models to anticipate future events or next actions from currently observed videos. Existing methods fit future captions, rationales, or full visual states, but face two limitations. First, they rely on annotations or external large models for supervision, limiting scalability. We address this with an on-policy self-distillation framework that turns past-future video pairs into a natural self-supervised signal without extra annotations or LLM supervision. Second, they treat the whole future clip as equally valuable, although most of it is irrelevant context information. We address this by defining a foresight score, from which we obtain a contrastive privilege advantage that drives the model to learn the most valuable future information.…
items.tldr: Future-OPSD trains vision-language models via on-policy self-distillation and a contrastive privilege advantage derived from a foresight score, improving video foresight prediction and planning without extra annotations or LLM supervision.

items.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
items.summary: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models.…

items.title: Prune to Expand: Training Prompt Enhancers with Less to Imitate
items.summary: Prompt enhancement (PE) refines concise user prompts into detailed descriptions to improve the compositional aesthetics of generated images while preserving user intent. A common practice constructs supervised fine-tuning (SFT) pairs by deriving short, user-like prompts from dense captions, implicitly assuming that captions that improve image generation also provide effective supervision. In this paper, however, we uncover a counterintuitive finding: PE models trained on caption pairs with substantial generation gains perform comparably to those trained on pairs with only marginal gains. We argue that dense captions can impose redundant supervision by requiring PE models to reproduce image-specific details weakly related to user intent.…
items.tldr: Prune to Expand (P2E) refines dense-caption supervision by selectively removing redundant sentences under a per-example deletion bound, improving prompt enhancement alignment with human preferences and visual quality over conventional dense-caption supervised fine-tuning.

items.title: Which Dwarf Is This? Doppeldwarf-306 and Near-Identical Instance Retrieval
items.summary: Most established instance-retrieval benchmarks emphasise landmarks; small sculptures from visually similar series offer a complementary challenge. We introduce Doppeldwarf-306: 1,691 openly licensed photographs of 306 bronze dwarf statues in Wrocław, Poland, many made in themed series that share one style, with the photographer of each image recorded. With no training, nearest-neighbour search over frozen DINOv2 features names the right statue first for 93.1% of leave-one-out queries, and the best of thirteen backbones from seven pretraining paradigms reaches 94.7%. Accuracy falls slowly as candidates are added: for DINOv2, by about 0.8 points each time their number doubles. A natural design for a phone guide compares a photograph only with statues near the user.…

items.title: Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation of RL Experts: Toward Continual Post-Training
items.summary: RL post-training typically produces domain experts that must then be consolidated into one model, and as new experts keep arriving, this consolidation becomes a continual process. Weight merging and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) must re-consolidate the whole model whenever an expert is added, and can erode capabilities outside the target domains. We propose Composable Soft-Prompt Distillation (CSPD), which keeps the pre-RL model frozen, distills each RL expert independently into a soft prompt, and composes experts by concatenating their prompts without joint training. A single soft prompt suffices to distill an RL expert, recovering at least 90% of the teacher's gain in 22 of 23 math, code, and agent settings. Independently trained prompts compose well. In a multi-expert setting, the average rises with every expert added, and the full composition matches MOPD (67.83 vs.…

items.title: VideoJSON: A Minimal Harness Beats Purpose-Built Memory for Ultra-Long Video Understanding
items.summary: Answering questions over days or weeks of video requires searching for scattered clues across long timelines. Existing video agents rely on complex memory graphs and fixed retrieval pipelines, which restrict how the agent can search. We propose VideoJSON, a minimal harness for ultra-long video understanding that keeps the memory simple and lets a coding agent write its own search programs. During indexing, a vision-language model turns each minute of video into a single JSON record containing a dense caption and structured fields such as events, entities, places, and speech transcripts. At query time, the agent writes Python or Bash programs in a sandboxed container to filter, link, and read these records over multiple steps, without task-specific training or raw video access.…

items.title: Feedback Shortcut: Speculative Decoding for Latent Feedback Transformers
items.summary: Feeding each position's top-layer hidden state back into the next position's input improves Transformer performance. However, this feedback breaks speculative decoding, since verifying a drafted token requires the top-layer state from its preceding position, which forces the draft to rely on an approximate stand-in. Training the model to adapt to this stand-in can lower the exact-decoding performance ceiling, while using it at inference time further introduces approximation error. We propose Feedback Shortcut to address both bottlenecks. First, state alignment trains a lightweight projection from multi-token prediction head states to stand-ins, leaving base model training untouched. Second, pipelined correction re-evaluates each draft using its predecessor's newly computed state, a much closer proxy to true feedback.…
items.tldr: Feedback Shortcut reduces speculative decoding errors caused by feeding top-layer hidden states back into Transformer inputs by aligning projected states and correcting drafts with predecessor states, preserving exact-decoding quality while accelerating decoding.

items.title: HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds
items.summary: Agentic systems are increasingly being explored for automating experimental high-energy physics measurements, but the correctness of their results can today be reliably evaluated only via extensive expert review. To address this, we propose a method to perform detailed quantitative evaluations of agent-driven analyses through the use of blind analysis and injection tests, which are critical in a typical expert review. Agents develop a data analysis pipeline on a public dataset, while the evaluation is performed on programmatically generated sealed private datasets where signals are injected and simulation settings varied within realistic detector uncertainties. By requiring agents to provide a single workflow that is evaluated across these "sealed worlds", we are able to test the accuracy and robustness of the workflows.…

items.title: Mega-MMDF and DeepfakeBench-MM: Benchmarking Multimodal Deepfake Detection Across Diverse Forgery Pipelines
items.summary: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector.…
items.tldr: A large audio-visual deepfake benchmark and standardized evaluation suite show that diverse composite-forgery training improves detection performance but does not reliably generalize to constituent manipulations, while modality masking and temporal misalignment increase detection errors.

items.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
items.summary: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run. By applying learnable, scalar gates to each sublayer, we allow the training loss to remove the model's own components during training -- freeing a smaller heterogeneous network inside.…
items.tldr: Model Carving jointly learns a Transformer's weights and architecture by gating sublayers during training, producing smaller, faster, and stronger models than dense, pruned, or distilled alternatives.

items.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
items.summary: Autoresearch agents, which autonomously design, run, and refine experiments, are accelerating scientific progress, particularly in AI research. However, existing agents rely on harnesses that combine multiple mechanisms, making it difficult to determine how individual components contribute to performance. We systematically study harness design for long-horizon, self-evolving autoresearch agents along two dimensions: context management, which determines what an agent retains from its past attempts, and skill management, which governs how it stores and reuses lessons from those attempts. Across MLE-Bench and KernelBench with gpt-oss-120b, gpt-6-luna, and gpt-6-sol, we isolate the effects of individual harness design choices by evaluating each against a recency-truncation baseline within a shared agent framework.…
items.tldr: A systematic study of harness design for long-horizon self-evolving autoresearch agents finds that context folding and selective skill deletion improve performance, enabling MLEvolver to achieve strong results on MLE-Bench Lite and KernelBench Level 3.

items.title: Evaluating Memanto on DolphinBench for AI Agents
items.summary: Memory benchmarks built on question answering tell an agent which fact to recall. Workplace requests often leave that need implicit: to post an update in the team's channel, an agent must work out which channel from earlier interactions and use it in a tool call. We evaluate Memanto, a memory agent that ranks memories with an information-theoretic relevance score, on DolphinBench, which tests memory through 600 simulated workplace tasks, each validated as requiring memory. Running in the Hermes agent harness with GPT-6-Luna and at most 6 iterations per conversation, Memanto completes 503 tasks (83.83%). The strongest configuration reported by the benchmark's authors, Mem0 with GPT-5.6-Luna and up to 60 iterations, completes 424 (70.67%). Memanto's run also has the lowest total cost (10.86, against 61.48 for the cheapest reported run) and the shortest median task latency (15.32s).…
items.tldr: Memanto, a memory agent using information-theoretic relevance scoring, completes more simulated workplace tasks at lower cost and latency than the strongest reported Mem0 configuration.

items.title: Markdown Is Not a Firewall: four coding agents, one rules file, four boundaries
items.summary: Teams put a one-page rules file in a repository and call it a control on coding agents. A registered study found agents rarely look up a repository's contribution rules. I asked the security question: what does a rules file do at a boundary, against a gate? I tested one 278-word rules file, with hypotheses and analysis code deposited first. Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and OpenCode with DeepSeek worked through 20 small repositories with hidden tests, 12 for three of them. Three agents met four boundaries I built: a refused endpoint, a destructive shortcut, a planted instruction and a planted package. Permission prompts, each vendor's own control layer, were off by design. A gate in front of the mock service blocked and logged forbidden requests. Every verdict was read from records the agent could not change. Only my first scoring pass was blind to arm.…

items.title: Surface Cues Over Structure: Probing LLM Behavior on Brain Connectivity Graphs
items.summary: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) provides a noninvasive view of functional interactions across the brain, which can be represented as connectivity graphs for neurological disease analysis. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being paired with such representations, yet it remains unclear whether they genuinely reason over the underlying connectivity or simply respond to surface-level cues that may trigger learned priors. We probe this question through a controlled study of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) diagnosis from resting-state functional connectivity, isolating one factor at a time to determine what drives an LLM's predictions on brain connectivity graphs.…

items.title: Self-Evolving Beyond Human-Crafted Experience for EDA Scripting
items.summary: The growing complexity of electronic systems demands efficient design flows, yet EDA scripting remains a bottleneck: proprietary APIs are sparsely documented, and errors often appear as silent failures or cryptic exceptions. Hand-crafted knowledge helps but is difficult to maintain as toolchains evolve. We present ZhuLong-SE (Self-Evolution), an execution-grounded LLM agent that learns reusable knowledge from prior task traces. Building on ZhuLong, it enhances the task-level harness with API retrieval, documentation responses, isolated sandbox execution, and static checking, then adds governed cross-task self-evolution. Beyond solving individual tasks, ZhuLong-SE distills past execution traces into a three-tier memory store governed by ground-truth anchoring, disconfirmation filtering, held-out rollback, and anti-leakage retrieval.…

items.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
items.summary: LLM agents are expected to improve themselves from their own experience across episodes, with fixed weights. Self-improvement in an embodied world cannot be read from one measure. Existing benchmarks measure task progress, world-knowledge question answering (QA), and episodic memory, but a correct answer does not show that the agent ever observed the evidence for it, and progress does not show what the agent learned. We introduce AstronautBench, which measures one agent's self-improvement through three views on the same run: what it knows, whether its own evidence supports that knowledge, and how far it gets in the world. It is built on the game Outer Wilds, where each episode is a 22-minute loop after which the world resets, only the agent's knowledge carries over, and progress is gated by knowledge.…

items.title: AI-Assisted Decision Support for Formula 1 Pit-Stop Strategy: Deep Reinforcement Learning and Mathematical Programming
items.summary: Pit-stop strategy in Formula 1 is a sequential decision problem under uncertainty, in which strategists decide at each lap whether to pit and which tire compound to fit. We develop a data-driven simulator, calibrated with historical race data, that captures tire degradation, drivers' recent performance, overtaking, yellow flag events, and rivals' pit-stop decisions. We train agents with five Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms and compare them with a Quadratic Mixed-Integer Programming (QMIP) formulation that is optimal in deterministic single-driver settings. Without uncertainty or competition, all DRL methods except TRPO achieve near-optimal performance.…

items.title: chase1225/anythingllm-verona-document-chat
items.summary: Document-grounded chat for Verona - AnythingLLM workspace integration.

items.title: Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) theorem solvers differ in both proving capability and inference cost. Applying an expensive solver to every subgoal wastes computation when cheaper models are sufficient, while always starting from the cheapest solver wastes attempts on subgoals that require stronger models. We present BudgetPV, an agentic budget-aware predict-and-verify system that allocates computation across unresolved subgoals and heterogeneous LLM solvers. BudgetPV uses a cross-solver predictor to guide solver selection for each subgoal and revises the allocation as verification feedback becomes available. The allocation problem changes as proving progresses. Early decisions mainly determine which solver should handle an untried subgoal, while later decisions determine which previously attempted subgoals should receive additional computation.…

items.title: Interfacial Transition Waves and Domain Wall Self-Pinning in Bi-stable Mechanical Metamaterial
items.summary: The understanding of transition waves in mechanical metamaterials currently derives from architectures fitting one of three archetypes as distinguished by the stability and order parameter: multi-stable with scalar or vector order parameter, and bi-stable with scalar order parameter. However, a fourth archetype is conspicuously absent: bi-stable with vector order parameter. Completing the tetrad, in this article, we numerically examine the transformation dynamics unique to bi-stable mechanical metamaterials with vector order parameter. We report two types of interfacial transition waves, whose propagation is restricted to the narrow region of configurational boundaries (e.g., domain walls). We show that the wave speed may depend on its polarization.…

items.title: How Language Models Compress and Compare: Understanding Selection with Token Covariance Maps
items.summary: Many language-model tasks reduce to selecting among structured alternatives, yet we still lack a simple picture of how a decoder-only transformer organizes an entire selection prompt across depth. We introduce token covariance maps, a prompt-level geometric view that tracks how token positions co-vary in hidden-state space at each layer. This turns a structured prompt into a depth-indexed sequence of maps whose spectral and block structure can be aligned with instructions, context, and candidate answers. Across 14 decoder-only models from 4 families and 12 structured-selection benchmarks, token covariance maps reveal a robust compress-then-compare organization. Early layers represent prompts diffusely, middle layers compress them into a shared low-rank bottleneck, and late layers re-expand into context-option and option-option geometry.…

items.title: Self-Supervised Learning with Recursive Quadrature Filters for Neural Time Series
items.summary: We develop self-supervised methods for training Recursive Quadrature Filter (RQF) encoders on unlabeled time series. RQFs are biologically motivated, complex-valued temporal filters that form a special class of diagonal state-space models (SSMs). Each RQF acts as a band-pass filter whose selectivity is determined by two learnable parameters: its tuning frequency and bandwidth. We separately introduce a self-supervised learning objective based on prediction error; the encoder is trained so that its current state predicts its own future activity. In the windowed mode, the summary of the current window predicts the summary of a later window; in the dense mode, the state at the current timestep predicts future log-power.…

items.title: A Sparsity Analysis of Traffic Forecasting Architectures: How Much Missing Data is Too Much?
items.summary: Traffic forecasting models are typically evaluated under ideal conditions with complete data. This evaluation does not reflect the frequent sensor failures and communication outages common in real-world deployments. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of multivariate traffic prediction models to evaluate their performance under varying levels of sensor data loss during inference. We benchmark several architectural paradigms, including graph neural networks, attention-based Transformers, and selective state-space models, across sparsity levels ranging from zero to complete sensor loss, using two widely used multi-channel traffic benchmarks. To ensure consistent comparison across traffic variables, we use normalized metrics and define a usability threshold to identify when predictions become unreliable.…

items.title: Recovering from Averages: An Inverse Problem Perspective on Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
items.summary: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approximate the potential energy surface of atomistic systems from quantum-mechanical reference data and enable molecular simulation at near-ab-initio accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Since they are fitted to total energies and forces, it is not obvious what is estimated: the total energy or the many-body potentials from which it is assembled. Mathematically, this can be formulated as a question whether a function can be recovered from averages of its values over random clusters. We study it for a linear model of fixed correlation order in simplified statistical setting. We show that, in the population limit, the potential is identifiable in a natural weighted Sobolev space, and derive finite-sample recovery guarantees. Numerical experiments for pair, three-body, and four-body models support the theory.

items.title: Specification-Grounded Adaptive Triage and Formal Invariant Exclusion Synthesis for Autonomous Silicon Coverage Closure
items.summary: Closing the final 5%-15% of code and functional coverage remains a major schedule bottleneck in silicon tapeouts. Existing LLM-based coverage closure loops feed raw uncovered RTL lines or branches directly into iterative prompts, failing on industrial subsystems due to: (1) token and context explosion from querying thousands of correlated holes independently; (2) illegal stimulus that violates cross-signal invariants and yields dirty coverage; and (3) unsafe exclusion hallucination on structurally unreachable dead code. We present ARGUS (Autonomous Reachability & Guided Unified Stimulus), a specification-grounded, dual-regime coverage closure and formal exclusion synthesis engine. ARGUS mines microarchitectural specs and SystemVerilog Assertions into a formal Block Contract (C), then runs adaptive Macro-Clustering vs.…

items.title: Don't Discard Your Rollouts: Reusing Teacher RL Traces for Student Distillation
items.summary: RL post-training methods such as PPO and GRPO are computationally expensive, with substantial resources devoted to sampling rollouts, which contain multiple completions per prompt along with their respective rewards. Canonical distillation, however, discards these traces and uses more compute to regenerate data from the final teacher. We ask if and how we can reuse the saved teacher RL rollouts to distil student models. Reusing rollouts is non-trivial: naive SFT on the rollouts underperforms canonical distillation, and naive DPO, while performant, is unstable, collapsing on weaker students. We show that treating rollout reuse as a data selection problem using metadata already recorded during GRPO substantially reduces this gap. We use prompt pass rates to order the data, using the easiest prompts for an SFT warm start prior to using mixed-success prompts for DPO.…

items.title: Beyond Final Answers: Interpretable Tumor Immune Microenvironment Reasoning from H&E and mIF
items.summary: Readouts of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), such as CD8+ T-cell density, intra-epithelial infiltration and the Ki67 index, combine tissue architecture from H&E with cell phenotypes from multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF). Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) could automate these readouts with an explanation, but two gaps remain. Pathology MLLMs read H&E alone, while these readouts need the cell phenotypes that mIF measures. And their reasoning has no step-level truth to be checked against, so R1-style reinforcement learning rewards only the final answer and leaves the reasoning unverified.…

items.title: Prediction of lattice thermal conductivity of half-Heusler compounds by machine learning and transfer-function calibration
items.summary: High-throughput searches for half-Heusler thermoelectrics increasingly rely on lattice thermal conductivity ($κ_L$) from first-principles calculations, or from machine-learning models trained on them. These calculations describe an ideal single crystal, whereas measurements are made on polycrystalline samples, in which grain boundaries and defects scatter heat as well. The resulting gap between calculated and measured $κ_L$ has been noted for individual compounds but not, to our knowledge, quantified across a materials class, so the values used for screening carry an unknown, systematic bias. Here we quantify and correct this bias for cubic half-Heusler compounds with 18 valence electrons.…

items.title: CADENCE:Temporally Coherent Whole-Body Human Mesh Recovery that Preserves Expressive Hand Motion
items.summary: Whole-body SMPL-X estimators recover body, hand, and face meshes from single images, but applied frame by frame to video they produce jittery motion. Smoothing the output removes the jitter at a cost that body-only benchmarks do not measure: a temporal filter strong enough to steady the torso also flattens the fast finger strokes that carry meaning in sign language and gesture. We present CADENCE, a whole-body SMPL-X system for monocular video designed around this trade-off. A per-frame estimator built on a shared C-RADIOv4 encoder, with a high-resolution hand pathway that reuses the same encoder on hand crops, produces each frame's estimate.…

items.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization
items.summary: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation resolves atomic-scale motion and predicts the structural, mechanical, and dynamic properties of materials, making it cen- tral to materials design and discovery. Yet an MD study requires an expert-driven workflow: designing the simulation, writing reliable input scripts, executing them, and analyzing the results with separate tools. Here we present ChatAtom, a multi-agent large language model system that translates a natural-language request into a complete MD workflow without the user writing input scripts or analysis code. Each agent has a defined responsibility within the workflow.…

items.title: What Helps Language-Model Agents Review Violent Video? A Controlled Comparison with a Human Evidence Reference
items.summary: Systems that flag violent video for a human operator can now be built from language models without training, by combining perception models and letting a language model decide. We ask how the observations of the perception models should reach the decision, and which evidence matters. On the XD-Violence test set (799 clips) we fix one set of perception agents (video description, object detection, sound tagging, speech recognition and speech tagging) and one reasoning model, and compare three interfaces: messages between agents, a typed evidence graph explored with tools, and flat text read in one pass; and a single audio-visual model given the raw clip. Two annotators provide a human reference that records the decision, the incident segments and whether they relied on sight, sound or speech.…

items.title: A reciprocal-matrix proof of Sendov's theorem and applications to control theory
items.summary: This proof grew out of the author's research on interpreting mathematical statements from the viewpoint of control theory. Its value lies both in the understanding it brings and in the applications that arise from the argument. Let $a$ be a simple zero of a polynomial of degree $n\ge 2$ whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk. If $c_1,\ldots,c_{n-1}$ are its critical points, counted with multiplicity, then the reciprocals $1/(a-c_j)$ are the eigenvalues of an explicit matrix built from the other zeros. A failure of Sendov's bound at $a$ would therefore make the associated discrete-time system asymptotically stable. This observation leads to an alternative proof of the quadratic inequality of Tang and Zhang, including its equality case.…

items.title: Pharos: Learning to Control Rare Events at Scale
items.summary: Rare events drive transformations across physics, chemistry and biology, yet predicting their mechanisms and rates remains a fundamental challenge. Here we introduce Pharos, a framework that learns to make rare transitions accessible while predicting how frequently they occur under physical dynamics. Through stochastic optimal control, Pharos jointly learns the probability of completing a transition and how to steer simulations toward it, allowing sampling and learning to improve one another. Across biomolecular benchmarks, Pharos learns accurate transition probabilities with order-of-magnitude gains in convergence speed over previous algorithms.…

items.title: Reinforcement Learning Unlearns Corrupted SFT Reasoning
items.summary: We show that reinforcement learning (RL) in reasoning tasks can succeed even when the supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data is severely corrupted. In a mathematical reasoning dataset (GSM8K), we systematically corrupt training trajectories across 361 configurations by injecting realistic error types, varying error locations, trace-answer consistency, and corruption ratios up to 100%. While aggregated SFT-only performance steadily deteriorates under corruption (dropping from 43.61% to 13.80%), Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training consistently restores model accuracy back to gold-baseline levels (approximately 60%). Crucially, initializing RL with as few as N = 8 minimal, incorrect, three-line "form-only" traces boosts post-RL performance to 69.30%, outperforming standard gold SFT initialization (60.71%) and GRPO without SFT (35.00%).…

items.title: Self-verifiable LLM-driven science and why it needs human researchers
items.summary: Language models are now used throughout all sciences - for reading literature, extracting numbers from tables and spectra, analyzing data, drafting conclusions - and their answers arrive in the same polished confident tone whether they are right or wrong, so a result has to be re-derived by a human researcher before it can be relied on. The cost of that re-checking, not the ability to generate results, is what currently limits AI-assisted research. In the field of mathematics, this problem is solved by proof assistants like Lean 4 and Coq that let any formal statement and its proof be written down and checked - a perfect match for LLMs, which are now actively used to search for proofs with every step automatically validated, rather than relying on a human to judge the result. In this paper, we propose an extension of this approach to non-mathematical sciences.…

items.title: Depth-Linked Residual Tokens for Multimodal Retrieval and Generation
items.summary: Iterative architectures such as looped language models improve parameter efficiency and reasoning capacity of transformers, yet their sequential backbone iterations introduce substantial computational latency. Conversely, parallelizable learnable special tokens (such as the register tokens in Vision Transformer) enable efficient single-pass inference, but often suffer from the absence of sequential refinement and exhibit redundant representations across tokens. To address these challenges, we introduce Depth-Linked Residual Tokens (DepThink), an efficient framework designed for multimodal retrieval and generation. Operating within a single pre-filling forward pass, DepThink appends a sequence of K learnable residual tokens whose hidden states are coupled through a lightweight, learnable residual recurrence.…

items.title: From Observation to Explanation: Mechanistic Interpretability of LLM-Generated Code for Principled Repair
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed software development, yet our understanding of how they generate code remains critically underdeveloped. We address this gap by triangulating evidence across three layers. Longitudinally, autonomous agent-attributed code is statistically indistinguishable from human code under a semantic modification definition (HR = 1.019, p = 0.490), yet attracts disproportionately corrective modifications in production (49.1% vs 37.9% human baseline). This finding demands a causal explanation. Empirically, existing benchmarks overestimate LLM capabilities: models that achieve 84 to 89% correctness on synthetic tasks attain only 24 to 35% on real-world class-level code.…

items.title: Generative Bayesian modelling of radio antenna beams An application to the MeerKAT radio telescope
items.summary: Accurate primary beam models are essential for high-fidelity calibration and imaging in radio astronomy. Traditional approaches either lack the ability to represent realistic antenna patterns (analytical models) or become computationally prohibitive to interpolate for wide-bandwidth observations (electromagnetic simulations, direct holographic measurements). We develop a generative beam model that represents both the spatial structure and the frequency variations in the primary beam while remaining tractable for integration into calibration and imaging pipelines, achieving superior accuracy compared to existing parametric models and reducing data storage compared to data-based models. We adopt a non-parametric Bayesian framework grounded in information field theory, implemented using the NIFTy library.…

items.title: ScaleWorld: High-Resolution World Generation through Shared Prediction and Refinement
items.summary: High-resolution generation enables video world models to render fine-grained scene structures and textures, but directly generating high-resolution video incurs substantial computational and memory costs. We present ScaleWorld, a causal video model that unifies low-resolution world prediction and high-resolution refinement within a single shared backbone. By refining its own predictions, ScaleWorld produces high-resolution world videos without requiring a separate refinement model. For each video chunk, the shared backbone first completes a low-resolution prediction and then performs one-step high-resolution refinement conditioned on that prediction. To support efficient streaming generation, we maintain separate causal states with a long low-resolution history for prediction and a short high-resolution history for refinement.…

items.title: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation
items.summary: Collecting and labeling inertial measurement unit (IMU) data for human activity recognition (HAR) is expensive, and models trained on one group of subjects often fail to generalize to unseen individuals. Even with balanced data, classifiers struggle to distinguish dynamically similar activity classes and benefit from targeted augmentation. We explore whether synthetic IMU data generated in the representation space of a pretrained biosignal encoder, Bio-PM \cite{b1}, can serve as a practical augmentation source. Rather than synthesizing raw signals, we leverage Bio-PM's frozen encoder to convert 10-second IMU windows into token embedding sequences and train class-conditional decoders in this space: (1) an autoregressive transformer decoder that predicts tokens sequentially, and (2) a diffusion decoder that learns the token distribution through a denoising objective.…

items.title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
items.summary: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices. For the Hubbard model at $U/t=8$ and $1/8$ hole doping, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies in large lattices of up to 1024 sites. These results demonstrate an accurate approach to strongly correlated fermions by connecting neural networks with Gaussian tensor networks.

items.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
items.summary: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. At training time the label and the unobserved feature values are available, and together they determine the teacher in closed form: an oracle that ranks every candidate by its effect on the downstream predictor's error. OracleImitator distills this ranking into a deployable policy by soft-target imitation.…

items.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
