Given an input vector field, our model estimates a second vector field that is orthonormal to it, while also requiring the Lie bracket of the two to vanish.…

items.title: Physics-Guided Crystal Structure Elucidation from Powder X-Ray Diffraction with Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
items.summary: Determining unique atomic coordinates from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) remains challenging because peak overlap, weak scattering from light elements, limited scattering contrast between elements with similar atomic numbers, and experimental noise render the inverse problem underdetermined. Here, we present XCAPE (XRD-Constrained Accelerated Prediction Engine), a crystal structure prediction (CSP) framework that integrates experimentally derived composition, unit cell parameters, space group, and PXRD data into a symmetry-aware evolutionary search. XCAPE explores Wyckoff-site configurations using tailored mutation operations, evaluates candidates by both energetic stability and diffraction agreement, and accelerates geometry optimization using a universal machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP).…

items.title: GramStatTexNet: Efficient, Interpretable, and Neuro-Inspired Texture Analysis-by-Synthesis
items.summary: Deep networks achieve high realism in texture synthesis but often rely on opaque, over-parameterized representations that have limited direct connection to biological vision. Neuroscience-informed pyramid models are interpretable, compact, and biologically inspired, but rely on small, hand-curated statistics sets that are difficult to generalize or extend. We introduce GramStatTexNet, a hybrid analysis-by-synthesis framework that combines the multi-scale Gabor filter structure of classical models with the flexibility of Gramian-based correlations, organized into structured filter families.…

items.title: Beyond Replacement: Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) offer a flexible alternative to autoregressive models, enabling any-order infilling. While most existing decoding methods treat decoded tokens as fixed, some recent models allow previously decoded tokens to be revised only by replacing them with alternative tokens, a paradigm we refer to as replacement-only editing (ROE). Although ROE can correct individual tokens, it is inefficient for sequence shifts caused by missing or extra tokens and struggles when errors occur across many positions. To address these limitations, we propose LED (Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models), a post-training framework that extends ROE with insertion and deletion, enabling Levenshtein-style refinement of generated sequences. It uses two training designs.…

items.title: ZERITH V2.5: From Predictive Power to Policy Learnability
items.summary: When humans learn to manipulate an unfamiliar object, they may already be able to anticipate how its state will change while still being unable to control it skillfully. This gap between prediction and control motivates us to study how the priors acquired by video generation models can be used effectively by an action policy. We present ZERITH V2.5, a video-action model (VAM) in which the action policy reads intermediate features of a video generation model, and use it to study, under fixed demonstrations and a fixed total number of updates, what kind of predictive training improves subsequent action learning. We find that the way video predictive training is supervised affects subsequent action learning. In our experiments, adapting at many noise levels yields a large gain, while adapting only at the noise level used at deployment yields none.…

items.title: Same Rank, Different Needs: Rethinking LoRA Redistribution in Federated Learning
items.summary: Federated low-rank adaptation (LoRA) enables clients with different resource budgets to collaboratively fine-tune foundation models. To distribute an aggregated update within each client's rank budget, existing methods commonly retain its leading singular directions. However, directions that best reconstruct the update matrix need not best preserve its responses on a particular client's inputs: a lower-energy direction may matter more to that recipient. We formalize this mismatch and show that matrix-optimal truncation can incur arbitrarily larger response error than another readout of the same rank. Motivated by this result, we propose Receiver-Aware Subspace Adaptation (RASA), a plug-in framework for receiver-aware knowledge transfer. RASA uses compact diagonal input second moments to perform uncentered PCA of receiver-weighted update responses.…

items.title: Reliability is a user-specific property of large language models
items.summary: Public benchmarks support comparisons of large language model (LLM) capabilities, yet users can experience the same highly ranked model differently. Drawing on traditional software reliability, we argue that the reliability of an LLM service should be assessed for specified users and conditions of use. This requires more than a capability score: evaluation evidence must support a claim about failure during future operation. We distinguish testing to discover faults from testing to assess reliability and identify ten modelling considerations behind such claims. We propose a six-workstream research roadmap linking claim specification, dynamic operational profiles, graded outcomes and noisy judgements, local probabilistic robustness, interaction dependence, and statistical inference with reassessment.…

items.title: RecallFlow: Episodic Memory as the Source Distribution of Generative Robot Policies
items.summary: Diffusion and flow-matching policies have become a standard choice for visuomotor imitation learning, owing to their ability to model multimodal action distributions. In memory-dependent manipulation, the robot must act on information that is no longer visible. Existing methods feed the observation history to the policy as an additional condition, while action generation still starts from Gaussian noise. However, the policy must then pick out the relevant target from a long and redundant history, leading to spurious correlations and unreliable decisions as the memory load grows. Additionally, the initial noise carries no information about what the robot has seen, leaving generation without guidance toward the remembered target. To address these issues, we propose RecallFlow, a flow-policy framework that builds the source distribution from episodic memory.…

items.title: Toward Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Neural AC Power Flow
items.summary: Growing uncertainty in power system operations from renewables integration, extreme weather, and data center loads challenges the reliability of traditional power flow solvers at scale. Machine learning-based proxies are a potentially promising alternative, but the prohibitive cost of generating training data for large grids makes out-of-distribution generalization a key capability for deployment; currently, models trained on small grids lack that capability. In this work, we systematically evaluate how physics-informed losses, multi-grid training, and perturbation-based data augmentation improve the zero-shot transfer of three graph neural network-based power flow models from smaller systems to a larger, unseen 500-bus system.…

items.title: AdaS-ViT: Test-Time Adaptive Routing for Spiking Vision Transformers with Ultra-High Energy Efficiency
items.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise event-driven and energy-efficient vision, yet existing spiking vision transformers (S-ViTs) largely confine spiking tokens to fixed and uniform firing schemes along the temporal, spatial and channel dimensions, whereas suppressing the computational redundancy thus incurred calls for adaptive firing mechanisms that operate jointly across all three axes at test time. To this end, we propose the Adaptive Efficient Integrate-and-Fire (AdaE-IF) model, which consults the attention score of each spiking token and routes salient regions to fine-grained firing patterns while assigning energy-frugal coarse patterns to the remaining regions. Building on AdaE-IF, we further introduce Spiking Gated Self-Attention (S-GSA) and Spiking Local-Gated Unit (S-LGU), which enforce selective spike emission at token and channel granularity.…

items.title: GTA: Generative Tower of Agents for Scalable Holonic Scene Generation
items.summary: Scalable world modeling requires coordinating scene-wide goals with fine-grained objects and dynamic characters under limited time and context budgets. We introduce GTA (Generative Tower of Agents), which represents every unit at every level of an adaptive scene hierarchy as a holon, both a self-contained construction task and a composable scene unit. Parallel agents recursively plan the hierarchy top-down, generate assets, and assemble and refine them bottom-up. Uniform interfaces carry scene-wide requirements down the hierarchy, guiding local construction so that each holon fits into the larger one. GTA accelerates scalable world modeling through high-throughput parallel execution while preserving well-structured layouts and fine-grained asset details.…

items.title: When Price Charts Rhyme: Historical Visual Retrieval for Stock Return Prediction
items.summary: We study whether visually similar price histories predict similar future returns, using a vision model to retrieve each stock's most similar charts from three decades of U.S. price histories. A representation pretrained only on natural images already retrieves neighbors whose realized returns predict the cross-section of stock returns. Aligning the representation with subsequent returns more than doubles the strategy's Sharpe ratio and outperforms a convolutional neural network trained directly on chart images. The predictability is concentrated among stocks with greater limits to arbitrage. Returns and order imbalances around portfolio formation indicate that the signal identifies temporary selling pressure that partially reverts. A sparse autoencoder traces the return-aligned signal to recurring visual states that determine which historical charts are retrieved.…

items.title: Do 3D Point Representations Encode Architectural Functions? Probing Supervised and Pretrained Models on Urban Facades
items.summary: Semantic labels say what a building element is, not what it does: two identical-looking windows on one facade may be operable or fixed, a column may carry load or only decorate. We ask whether 3D point representations encode such architectural function. On 22 mobile-LiDAR buildings with 15 functional attributes per element, we hold out entire buildings and compare hand-crafted descriptors, networks trained from scratch and frozen self-supervised point transformers. Descriptors and frozen features are read by the same linear layer. No network trained from scratch, from PointNet to a 108M-parameter PTv3, clearly exceeds the descriptors (0.610 mAP on functionally ambiguous elements), whereas frozen Utonia reaches 0.732. Random-weight controls of the same architectures (0.649 and 0.652) attribute the gain to pretraining (Utonia: +0.080, 95% building interval [+0.035, +0.124]).…

items.title: Improving While Deployed: Learning Proactive End-to-End Driving from Imperfect Human Takeover Data
items.summary: Once deployed on vehicles, end-to-end driving models continuously encounter challenging scenarios, generating valuable human takeover data that capture both model outputs and human behaviors. However, human interventions are often imperfect, as drivers may intervene too late or unnecessarily. Consequently, direct imitation can reinforce late responses or discourage otherwise appropriate maneuvers. To address this challenge, we propose an offline post-training framework that transforms imperfect takeover data into proactive supervision. We first construct diverse trajectory candidates by augmenting the plans of the deployed model and shifting recorded human corrective maneuvers earlier in time. We then train a scene-conditioned trajectory scorer to rank these candidates using expert demonstrations and unpaired preference signals from takeover logs.…

items.title: ExecGap: Exploiting Command-Execution Gap for Patch Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have become a powerful paradigm for robotic manipulation and show strong promise for real-world deployment, making adversarial robustness critical for reliable robot operation. Existing adversarial attacks on VLA-controlled robots mainly optimize prediction-level discrepancies or rollout-level deviations to disrupt manipulation. However, they rarely account for the fact that VLA-predicted commands are not executed directly, but must be realized through downstream control and robot embodiment. In this paper, we propose ExecGap, an adversarial patch attack framework that exploits this command-execution gap to expose embodiment-specific execution vulnerabilities. Specifically, ExecGap biases VLA-predicted task-space commands toward low-executability directions, which are estimated from kinematic inefficiency and dynamic weak actuation.…

items.title: Rational Ensemble Logic for Cohort Discovery with Real-World Electrophysiology Data
items.summary: Biomedical knowledge representation should make the passage from observations to conclusions transparent, rigorous, understandable, explainable, and reproducible (TRUER). We introduce Rational Ensemble Logic (QEL) for specifying temporal phenotypes in real-world electrophysiology data (RWED), with a meaning independent of the implementation software. QEL combines three parameterized modal operators (exact displacement, bounded existence, and bounded universality) over rational time with Boolean connectives and first-order quantification. Its Labeled Interval Ensemble (LINE) semantics represents annotated records as finite interval ensembles. We relate the operators to morphological operations and develop endpoint-array algorithms and finite rational evidence sets for model checking.…

items.title: Localizing Text Anonymization for Trustworthy AI: Extending RAT-Bench to Malaysian Microdata and PII
items.summary: As governments and organizations adopt foundation models for public services and workplace productivity, sensitive citizen, employee, and administrative text may enter LLM workflows through inference, retrieval, fine-tuning, or local model development. We examine whether text anonymizers transfer to new deployment settings by extending RAT-Bench to Malaysia using local microdata, Malaysian PII formats, and culturally grounded transcripts in Malaysian English and Bahasa Malaysia. We evaluate NER- and LLM-based anonymizers using an LLM attacker that infers attributes from anonymized text, measuring both re-identification success and text utility. Across Malaysian English and Bahasa Malaysia, the two LLM anonymizers provide the strongest explicit privacy-utility trade-offs, reducing Easy/Hard re-identification risk to 23-29% while preserving BLEU scores of 0.77-0.94.…

items.title: KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
items.summary: The growing volume of topically similar papers makes it difficult to identify new work that can offer useful research insights or methodological guidance. We present KnowMe Paper Radar, a lightweight discovery tool that combines multiple sources of evidence into personalized reading priorities. Users specify topics, priorities, exclusions and dates; the system brings together topical relevance, recency, author research histories, collaboration paths and direction-specific institutional context. By exposing each score component and its supporting sources, KnowMe helps readers select promising papers for their current questions and discover relevant work beyond familiar authors. Automatic acquisition, version merging and graph-cache reuse keep this workflow convenient without large language model (LLM) inference during ordinary use.…

items.title: Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents
items.summary: Clinicians reviewing a diagnostic work-up will ask what was considered at each step and why the assessment changed. Agents powered by free text can reach physician-level diagnostic accuracy, but their written reasoning does not always reflect the factors that went into the decision. Here, we present Decision2Care, a decision agent that works up the acutely ill patient without producing any text. A decision model assigns a probability to each permitted EHR action, and fixed rules carry out the most probable one. We evaluated Decision2Care on the records of 546 emergency admissions across 12 diseases. Decision2Care reached a diagnostic accuracy of 86.5%, compared with 86.1% for the MIRA-v2 agent, and required a median of 2.2 s per work-up, compared with 92-100 s. Each work-up tracked which options Decision2Care was considering at each step.…

items.title: MoMoVL: Modality-Aware Adaptive Compression for On-Device Sparsely-Activated Vision-Language Models
items.summary: The rise of the agentic web has been accompanied by growing demand for on-device Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that perform diverse cross-modal web tasks with enhanced privacy and reduced latency. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are widely adopted in modern VLMs for compute-efficient scalability, yet their multi-expert architecture poses deployment challenges due to substantial memory demands. Mixed-precision quantization is an effective compression technique that reduces bit-widths while adapting to the heterogeneous hardware budgets of edge devices, particularly well-suited for MoE due to its inherent structural sparsity, which causes imbalanced importance among experts.…

items.title: Measuring the Conservatism of Latent Safety Filters for World Models
items.summary: A latent safety filter decides from the latent of a world model whether a planned action is safe. Conformal calibration sets the threshold of the filter so that it accepts an unsafe action only with a small probability. However, the filter can still be conservative and refuse many safe actions, depending on the latent. To measure the conservatism that a latent forces on the filter, we group similar latents and actions into cells. A filter that gives one decision per cell can refuse the unsafe transitions of a cell only by refusing the safe ones in it as well. We call the share of safe transitions that lie in such cells the overlap. We prove that the overlap is the minimum share of safe transitions that such a filter has to refuse in order to accept no unsafe transition in the data. Both the overlap and the conformal calibration can be applied to any latent.…

items.title: Variable Length Diffuse Everything: Arbitrary Length Generative Modeling on Arbitrary State Spaces
items.summary: Diffusion and flow-based generative models have achieved remarkable results across diverse applications, but most assume data of fixed-dimension/length. Meanwhile, real-world problems such as layout generation often involve variable-length, multimodal data, such as continuous bounding box coordinates paired with discrete types. Existing methods typically address variable length by padding data to a fixed size or by introducing specialized objectives to model lengths explicitly, adding complexity and limiting generality. We propose Variable Length Diffuse Everything (VL-DE), a simple and general framework for variable-length multimodal generation on arbitrary state spaces. Instead of padding, VL-DE handles variable length through an insertion-based mechanism grounded in a principled theoretical framework, yielding a tractable training objective.…

items.title: Structured Extraction of Diffraction Data from Covalent Organic Frameworks
items.summary: Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) is the primary structural evidence for covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and many other materials. Yet decades of measured patterns exist only as images in published figures. Automatic recovery is difficult, because PXRD figures vary widely in format, from a single curve to crowded stacks with labels, insets, and neighboring plots that challenge traditional computer vision. This work presents a pipeline in which a vision large language model (LLM) interprets the layout of each figure, locating the diffraction plot and its curves and sketching a coarse trace of each, while classical computer vision (CV) refines every trace to pixel-level accuracy. Applied to 3,954 COF articles, the pipeline produces 11,445 calibrated diffraction curves, released in the open database COF-PEAK.…

items.title: Evaluating Governed LLM-Driven ML Experimentation: Lifecycle, Provenance, and Failure Metrics
items.summary: Autonomous agents that run ML experiments are usually judged by the best score they reach. That score says nothing about how it was reached: whether the agent stayed within the files it was allowed to edit, whether failed trials were kept or silently dropped, and whether each keep or discard decision can be traced to its evidence. We propose evaluating such systems on their experimental process as well as their outcome, and we build a governed harness that makes this possible. A control plane, not the LLM that proposes changes, owns each trial's lifecycle, checks its edit scope, decides keep or discard, and appends one record per trial to an append-only ledger. Governance metrics such as the invalid-action rate, the repeated-bad rate and provenance completeness are computed from that ledger.…

items.title: Finetuning VLAs for Dexterous Manipulation: The Right Checkpoint Is All You Need
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action models have demonstrated strong manipulation capabilities. A limitation of VLA models is that most manipulation datasets focus on parallel-jaw gripper systems, making transfer to multi-finger hands challenging, particularly as teleoperation datasets are harder to collect with multi-fingered robots. In this work, we study how to best adapt VLAs to dexterous hands by pairing supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with diffusion-steering reinforcement learning (DSRL). Using $π_{0.5}$ and a LEAP hand, we evaluate five fine-tuning recipes across two simulation tasks using only a handful of demonstrations.…

items.title: Learning What to Degrade: A Recoverability-Aware Curriculum for Reliable Smart-Glasses Super-Resolution
items.summary: Degradations in smart-glasses images obscure small text and fine-grained structures needed by vision-language models (VLMs) for visual assistance. We introduce an high-resolution (HR)-referenced semantic evaluation protocol that compares VLM outputs on restored images with those on corresponding HR references. Our evaluation reveals two failure modes: generative SR can synthesize misleading details, whereas restoration-oriented SR can leave critical evidence blurred or ambiguous. These findings motivate improving faithful detail recovery in restoration-oriented SR, where a key training challenge is to provide sufficiently difficult inputs while retaining recoverable visual information. We propose ReDiC (Recoverability-Difficulty Curriculum), which combines a model-independent recoverability proxy with model-relative restoration difficulty to adapt training degradation severity.…

items.title: Communicative On-Policy Distillation: Distilling Black-Box Teacher Capabilities through Communication for Long-Horizon Tasks
items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) is a powerful paradigm for improving language-model agents on long-horizon tasks, yet its conventional formulation relies on teacher logits that text-only black- box models do not expose. To address this limitation, we introduce Communicative On-Policy Distillation (COPD), which uses natural-language communication as a medium for distilling a stronger model's capabilities into a smaller student. During task execution, the student au- tonomously decides when to consult a black-box teacher and formulates open-ended natural- language requests without predefined question templates or intervention schedules. Successful student-teacher interactions are retained as privileged references to supervise fresh adviser-free student rollouts through on-policy self-distillation, jointly with task-reward reinforcement learning.…

items.title: Image-Condition-Controlled Diffusion Network with Large-Scale CT Pretraining for CT-Free Attenuation Correction in Dynamic Cardiac PET
items.summary: Positron emission tomography (PET) provides quantitative information on myocardial perfusion. In dynamic PET, tracer kinetics are tracked through a series of reconstructed time frames. Reliable attenuation correction is essential for accurate measurements. Clinical attenuation maps ($μ$-maps) are typically derived from computed tomography (CT), which adds radiation exposure and may introduce PET-CT misregistration due to respiratory and cardiac motion. Moreover, supervised CT-free methods rely on paired non-attenuation-corrected (NAC) PET and CT data, which are scarce, whereas large-scale unpaired CT data are more readily available.…

items.title: allenai/RoboTracker-Warp
items.summary: robotics

items.title: A Free Lunch: Gradient Averaging Achieves Optimal Statistical Efficiency in Newton Sketch
items.summary: We study statistical inference for online sketched Newton methods, in which each Newton system is approximately solved by an inner randomized sketching solver. Existing work reveals a computational--statistical trade-off: the sketching solver (and its accelerated variants) reduces the per-step cost of Newton methods from $O(d^3)$ to $O(d^2)$, but the randomness introduced by sketching also inflates the limiting covariance of both the last and the averaged Newton iterates. In this work, we address this trade-off via gradient averaging. We show that simply replacing the stochastic gradient with a moving average at each step can mitigate, and in some cases eliminate, the trade-off in Newton sketch. Importantly, gradient averaging requires no additional oracle evaluations and leaves the contraction bound of the inner sketching solver unchanged.…

items.title: LightSEAD: Lightweight SE(3)-Aware Keypoint Detector through Selective Knowledge Distillation
items.summary: The pursuit of improved performance in deep learning has often been accompanied by increasing architectural complexity and computational demands. We explore an alternative direction: achieving more with less through structured supervision. We introduce LightSEAD, a lightweight SE(3)-aware keypoint detector initialised with calibrated Harris pseudo-labels and enriched through viewpoint-aware and appearance-aware supervision and selective knowledge distillation. LightSEAD comprises only six convolutional layers and 84,289 learnable parameters, achieving competitive repeatability across HPatches, KITTI 06 and 4Seasons while demonstrating its downstream applicability to relative pose estimation on MegaDepth-1500. Further optimised for mixed-precision inference, LightSEAD Coarse achieves approximately 909 FPS on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 and 139 FPS on a Jetson Orin Nano Super.

items.title: Searching the Pareto Front: Multi-Objective Retrieval for Heterogeneous Scientific Modalities
items.summary: In cosmology, surveys span different sky regions and wavelength ranges, resulting in uneven modality coverage across observational datasets. Such heterogeneity can be addressed through either multimodal foundation models (FMs), which learn shared embedding spaces, or independently learned modality embeddings combined via late fusion. We investigate whether the latter provides an adaptive alternative to FM-based scientific retrieval. We evaluate this approach on a galaxy retrieval task spanning diverse modalities--history of star formation, spectra of light emitted, and multi-wavelength observations from two telescopes--comparing an FM baseline with separately trained embeddings fused through multi-objective optimization based on Pareto optimality.…

items.title: When Do LLMs Model the Right Target? Problem Formulation in High-Stakes Risk Prediction
items.summary: Generative AI is increasingly used to assist with data science tasks, yet fundamental questions remain about its ability to correctly formulate analytical problems. We investigate how well large language models (LLMs) can formulate prediction problems when developing models for high-stakes decision making. We focus on one particular challenge to validity: decision dependency, which arises when historical decisions affect observed outcomes. We evaluate this aspect of problem formulation in LLM-generated code and explanations across child-welfare, healthcare, and employment settings, using 11 models from OpenAI and Anthropic and seven prompt conditions. We assess whether the LLM-generated code implements a procedure appropriate for estimating the intended outcome under the study's assumptions and whether the explanation acknowledges decision dependency.…

items.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
items.summary: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. Clover adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion by combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block. Historical memory readout competes with current-block tokens in a shared softmax, with learnable block-size calibration and a separate, zero-initialized right-context convolution branch. Clover leads the seven evaluated agent metrics, including 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. On internal agent workloads, it reaches a reported generation speed of 680 tokens/s using one NVIDIA GB300 GPU at BF16 precision and batch size one.…

items.title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision. Moreover, an episode terminates at its first failure, concealing subsequent failures until the earlier ones are repaired.…

items.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
items.summary: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. For each step it submits a short logged contract: a goal, a verbatim quotation of the user, and scope fields. Code validates the contract, and a small trusted model checks it against the user's words and writes the tool call itself. Provided the validation and dispatch code is correct, every executed call is written by the trusted model, the planner's influence on a call is confined to a contract logged before it, and the trusted side decides how much of a request to carry out. We compare contracts with two reviewers of planner-written commands: one sees only the user's words and the command, the information boundary of a reasoning-blind permission classifier, and one also sees the planner's goal and a checked quotation.…
items.tldr: Intent contracts, in which a planner submits logged contracts and a trusted model writes tool calls, do not reduce unauthorized actions and match blind review, but complete more benign over-reach tasks than an intent-visible reviewer.

items.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
items.summary: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments. To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. We describe these choices along three dimensions: reward coverage, the goal-reaching trajectories the verifier rewards; data coverage, the application data the agent is exposed to beyond what the task reads or writes; and feature coverage, the application features beyond what the task uses. Existing works set each dimension on engineering grounds, but they do not measure its effect on training. How complete must an environment be to train a capable agent, and along which dimensions? In MobileGym, we adjust each dimension separately, train Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, and evaluate every policy in the original full environment.…

items.title: On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models
items.summary: Hybrid attention models combine full and linear attention to achieve a better quality--efficiency trade-off. Converting pretrained Transformers into such models requires identifying which layers should retain full attention under a prescribed budget. We identify two off-policy mismatches in FlashMorph's layer selection: (i) continuous branch interpolation and teacher-forced hidden states differ from discrete hybrid computation; and (ii) frozen model weights fail to account for parameter adaptation during subsequent recovery. We introduce FlashMorph2, an on-policy layer-selection method that (I) evaluates sampled discrete hybrid architectures end to end using their own hidden states, and (II) jointly optimizes layer-selection scores and model weights under the recovery objective to reflect post-adaptation performance.…
items.tldr: FlashMorph2 performs on-policy layer selection and weight adaptation for hybrid attention Transformers, improving long-context benchmark scores while selecting layers efficiently across model scales.

items.title: WM^MLLM: Turning MLLMs into World Models
items.summary: Video world models keep the world in the context of a generator, so a revisit is synthesized again and earlier edits can drift or disappear. We present WM^MLLM, the first interactive world model built on multimodal large language models (MLLMs), for persistent, editable world generation from a single image. WM^MLLM keeps the world state outside every generator, as a panorama with a revision history, and lets the MLLMs write it: they turn each request into operations on this state, select where a local edit is written, and check every candidate before it becomes the next state. Image generators only propose views, and video only presents them. Users can walk to new places and return, edit objects through text or a box, place subjects, and change lighting, weather or season.…
items.tldr: WM^MLLM uses multimodal large language models to maintain an external panorama state with revision history, enabling persistent, editable world generation from a single image with exact revisits and local edits.

items.title: WAM-Policy: World Action Models with On-Policy Distillation for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Arm-free quadrupeds can perform loco-manipulation, walking on three legs while manipulating with a front leg, yet no existing policy for it follows language instructions. World action models (WAMs) have emerged as effective language-conditioned manipulation policies, but are pretrained for robot arms and sample slowly. WAM-Policy turns one WAM into a quadrupedal loco-manipulation policy via two stages. The first, Cross-Morphology Policy Adaptation and Acceleration, adapts the arm-centric WAM to quadrupeds and distills the transferred policy into a student with one video and two action steps by on-policy self-distillation (OPSD). This student, however, is bounded by its teacher, which only imitates demonstrations.…

items.title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
items.summary: Optical neural networks promise fast, energy-efficient computing, but every device departs from its design and must be trained with the hardware. In situ training relies on an expert-built calibrated digital model of each device or on gradient-free trial and error. Coding agents, large language models that write and run programs, have shown an emergent ability to understand and edit the weights of digital neural networks. Here we introduce optics as code, a method in which a coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone, through a harness that returns camera images of its probes and requires a hypothesis per request. We discovered that the agent forms a physical understanding of the optics and reparametrizes the network with interpretable optical elements tuned on the hardware.…
items.tldr: A coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone by reparametrizing it with interpretable optical elements, achieving better classification and image encoding than gradient-free methods and approaching backpropagation through a calibrated model at lower cost.

items.title: NarrowSpec: Draft Hidden Width Need Not Match the Target in Speculative Decoding
items.summary: Speculative decoding is widely used to speed up generation in large language models (LLMs), with a small draft model proposing tokens that one forward pass of the target model verifies. Draft models that read the target's hidden states, such as DFlash and EAGLE-3, typically inherit the target's hidden width. We show that the draft's whole residual stream can run at half or a quarter of that width while largely preserving acceptance. For DFlash, which borrows the target's vocabulary projection, the trained output adapter folds into it, giving one narrower projection with logits unchanged up to floating-point rounding. We test two drafter families, DFlash and EAGLE-3, on two targets, Qwen3-8B (NVFP4) and GPT-OSS-20B (MXFP4), in SGLang on a B200 and a DGX Spark (GB10).…

items.title: CortexDecoder: Efficient fMRI-to-Image Reconstruction from Cortical Flatmaps
items.summary: Recent brain decoding work has shown the potential of Vision Transformers (ViTs) to learn mappings from neural representations to visual features. Here we present CortexDecoder, a framework that reconstructs viewed images from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) flatmaps, which are neural responses projected onto the cortical surface and unfolded into 2D images. We show that a frozen, pretrained cortical foundation model is sufficient for competitive reconstruction. A frozen CortexMAE encoder turns flatmap patches into brain tokens, and two lightweight cross-attention bridges map these tokens to semantic CLIP embeddings and low-level image features. The final image is generated using a frozen SDXL-unCLIP model which takes a low-level image reconstruction as an initial image and a predicted CLIP embedding used to condition the image generation.…

items.title: Innate development of cognitive functions and motor programs by chemoaffinity
items.summary: Humans and animals possess a rich repertoire of innate cognitive and behavioral abilities, yet the developmental mechanisms that establish the underlying neural circuitry remain unclear. Here, we show that a simple chemoaffinity-based connectivity rule, combined with stochastic cell-autonomous expression of cell adhesion molecules, can establish neural networks for a broad range of cognitive functions. We derive expression patterns that support the development of continuous attractor networks for path integration with toroidal grid-cell topology, networks with exponentially many discrete Hebbian assemblies, and circuits generating innate motor trajectories. Expression patterns can be combined in a modular way to encode recurrent networks for increasingly complex functions.…

items.title: Stability and flexibility in the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task emerge from goal-directed inference and planning under the free-energy principle
items.summary: In goal-directed behavior, the brain has to balance stability and flexibility. Stability means keeping the current recognition of environmental context, whereas flexibility means switching to a new one. The Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (WCST) is a standard task for studying this balance. In this task, stability is keeping the category estimate after correct feedback, and flexibility is switching it after incorrect feedback. Computational models have been proposed to elucidate the mechanism behind this balance. However, most models are given a variable for each category in advance, and every model treats correct feedback as desirable from the start. These models cover neither the category learning process nor the goal-directed process that adjusts the card selection to get correct feedback.…

items.title: Counterfactual aging in individual digital twin brains uncovers a latent dimension of resilience to aging
items.summary: Cognitive reserve concerns why the same aging causes less decline in some individuals than others, a question that digital twin brains can address by aging each individual in silico. Here we present Brain-VRNN, a connectome-constrained variational recurrent neural network trained on longitudinal multitask functional MRI. Its regenerated brain signals reproduced four functional aging markers of unseen individuals (r = 0.93-0.96) and identified each person (accuracy 0.98). Without cognitive scores, its global latent learned a trait dimension stable within each person, which helped predict future cognition. Crucially, when every individual underwent the same counterfactual aging, those with a lower trait value declined more, yet recovered up to 1.6 times as much with a reduction in body mass index, a modifiable dementia risk factor.…

items.title: Modern speech recognition systems exhibit human-like word recognition but superhuman use of statistical dependencies between words
items.summary: Advances in machine learning have yielded machine systems that approach human performance on real-world perception tasks. For speech recognition, it remains unclear whether such models' behavior resembles that of humans. We addressed this question by measuring word recognition abilities in humans and models across 272 speech distortions, providing a detailed behavioral fingerprint. Three recent industry speech recognition models trained on hundreds of years of speech outperformed humans. However, in conditions where linguistic context was removed, they matched human performance well, suggesting that the models are superhuman in their ability to leverage statistical dependencies between words. Experiments manipulating model training data suggest that training data variability and realism contribute to the match to human perception.…

items.title: Flux Transformer learns intracellular metabolic fluxes from isotope labeling and measured reaction rates
items.summary: Cells convert incoming nutrients into energy and biomass via metabolic fluxes. Quantifying these fluxes involves feeding cells isotope-labeled nutrients, quantifying metabolite labeling patterns, and inverting the labeling data to retrieve the underlying flux distribution. Traditional metabolic flux analysis (MFA) is both computationally expensive and frequently requires manual refinement of the cost function to obtain plausible results. For this reason, MFA has remained inaccessible to non-experts. Here we present Flux Transformer, an AI model that uses reaction-specific attention to integrate isotope-labeling data with available reaction-rate measurements, reconstructing mass-balanced steady-state fluxes. The model is trained on simulated data with added noise and identifies the underlying fluxes from these data more effectively than traditional MFA.…

items.title: Accurate and interpretable protein complex stoichiometry prediction through agentic AI with StoiAgent
items.summary: Accurate protein complex structure modeling requires knowledge of complex stoichiometry, yet the copy numbers of individual subunits are often unknown. Consequently, predicting protein complex stoichiometry has emerged as a major challenge in recent years. Here, we present StoiAgent, a large language model (LLM)-powered AI agent that automates the retrieval and integration of sequence, structural, and literature evidence to predict stoichiometry while preserving interpretable reasoning traces (chain of thoughts) of its evidence assessment and ranking decision. An open-weight LLM model, Qwen3.6-27B, is used by StoiAgent as the LLM backbone to combine sequences, structural templates, AlphaFold3 structure predictions, and literature evidence, and perform stoichiometry candidate generation and ranking.…

items.title: GENECraft: A Function- and Prior-Constrained Discrete Dynamical System for Controllable Regulatory DNA Design
items.summary: Designing regulatory DNA requires reconciling two complementary modeling paradigms: genomic language models (gLMs) capture evolutionary syntax without guaranteeing targeted regulatory activity, whereas sequence-to-function predictors provide explicit functional supervision without enforcing native-like sequence plausibility. We introduce GENECraft, a training-free Function- and Prior-Constrained Discrete Dynamical System (FP-DDS) that couples a genomic language model (Carbon) and a functional oracle (AlphaGenome) during inference-time optimization to balance predicted regulatory activity and consistency with genomic sequence priors.…

items.title: scUNVEIL: Learning scRNA-seq Cell Embeddings Through Measurement Enrichment
items.summary: Large-scale pretraining can improve scRNA-seq representations through measurement enrichment: estimating what the same measurement would reveal at greater UMI depth under the same measurement process. We introduce scUNVEIL, a self-supervised model trained through next-UMI prediction. We show that the Bayes-optimal next-UMI predictor is the posterior mean of the transcriptome composition that arbitrarily deep sequencing would reveal. Because UMI identities are exchangeable conditional on transcriptome composition, scUNVEIL operates directly on count vectors using a residual multilayer perceptron, without attention over gene tokens. The measurement-enriched transcriptome composition is predicted from a single low-dimensional hidden state, which therefore serves naturally as the cell embedding.…

items.title: BI-SCUDO Regression - A novel algorithm to infer clinical variables from omics datasets
items.summary: Regression analysis of high-throughput omics data is often made difficult by noise, batch effects, and the loss of information resulting from the discretization of continuous variables. Existing machine learning algorithms often struggle to extract stable biological signals under these heterogeneous conditions. We introduce BI-SCUDO Regression, a rank-based regression framework designed for omics data analysis. By leveraging within-sample rankings and network-based predictions, BI-SCUDO Regression bypasses the need for complex normalization and provides robust, interpretable results. In synthetic benchmarks, BI-SCUDO Regression demonstrated strong resilience to noise, maintaining predictive and feature-selection stability under conditions in which standard models exhibited performance degradation.…

items.title: Elflow: Automated Quality Control and Self-Supervised Representation Learning for High-Dimensional Cytometry
items.summary: High-dimensional flow and mass cytometry are foundational technologies for clinical immunophenotyping and hematological diagnostics, yet computational data analysis remains bottlenecked by operator-subjective manual gating. While computational tools have emerged, they remain fragmented across isolated tasks such as quality control or discrete clustering, leaving an unmet need for integrated, modular workflows that resolve continuous biological variation without manual supervision. Here, we introduce Elflow, a modular, self-supervised framework that links automated quality control, single-cell representation learning, and patient-level modeling without manual gating at inference.…

items.title: DRAFT: graph-recurrent learning of dynamic gene regulatory networks along single-cell multi-omics trajectories
items.summary: Single-cell multi-omics data offer an opportunity to resolve how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are rewired during cell-fate transitions, but most existing methods infer static snapshots, ignore temporal dependencies or assume linear regulation. Here we present DRAFT, a deep learning framework that combines graph attention with recurrent temporal memory to infer dynamic GRNs from time-resolved single-cell multi-omics data. On simulated data, DRAFT outperforms existing methods in accuracy and temporal smoothness. In mouse cellular reprogramming and Drosophila adult spermatogenesis, it recovers interactions supported by independent ChIP-seq, perturbation and Hi-C data, together with known stage-specific regulators.…

items.title: Sc-HistoMorphomics: A General Framework for High-throughput, Multimodal Profiling of Nuclear Morphology in Tissues.
items.summary: Quantitative cellular morphology provides a rich but underutilized window into cell identity and state. We introduce sc-HistoMorphomics, a scalable framework for profiling nuclear morphology in whole-slide H&E images and correlating these measurements with spatial transcriptomics data. Our pipeline combines deep-learning based segmentation with 194 interpretable morphometric features capturing nuclear shape, eosin and hematoxylin texture, and neighbourhood architecture, enabling high-throughput, multimodal characterization of tissue organization. Applied to endometrium, breast cancer tissue, and pancreas, sc-HistoMorphomics revealed conserved high-dimensional feature structure across tissues and reproducible association between morphology and gene expression.…

items.title: BiomedCAT: Biomedical Context Analysis Tool for Supporting Mechanistic Hypothesis Generation via User-defined Contextual Subgraph Extraction
items.summary: Researchers formulate mechanistic hypotheses in slides and figures long before they write them as text, yet knowledge-graph (KG) tools expect a query in the vocabulary of the graph. We present BiomedCAT, an open-source workflow that turns biomedical slides into a subgraph of the RTX-KG2c knowledge graph shaped by the user's research profile, on a laptop and without sending the documents out. A small vision-language model describes each slide; a 4-billion-parameter agent types the terms into the classes of the Biolink model; an existence gate removes invented entities; identifiers are retrieved from Translator services or from a local table and selected, never generated, by a judge model; and a profile-weighted two-hop expansion builds the context graph.…

items.title: CIRCA learns identifiable cell- and niche-level programs and their interactions with tissue pathology from spatial transcriptomics
items.summary: Interactions among cells and their local microenvironments shape tissue organization and function, while their dysregulation can contribute to disease. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), the complex responses of glial cells and neurons to amyloid-{beta} pathology can both mitigate and exacerbate neuronal injury. Spatial transcriptomics enables investigation of these relationships in situ, but recovering interpretable transcriptional programs and their interactions from spatial transcriptomics remains challenging, in part because conventional nonlinear models are non-identifiable. Here we present CIRCA (Causal Interaction Representation for Cellular Architectures), a self-supervised causal representation learning framework that jointly learns identifiable cell- and neighborhood-level transcriptional programs and the directed interactions among them under explicit assumptions.…

items.title: SPIDER: Contextualizing Biomedical Knowledge for Evidence-Grounded Scientific Reasoning
items.summary: Aggregated relations in biomedical knowledge graphs can obscure evidence and study conditions, complicating the distinction between scientific disagreement and contextual differences. Here we introduce SPIDER, a multi-agent framework grounding biomedical relations in literature evidence and extracting study conditions for interpretation. Applied to a graph integrating 48 databases and ontologies, SPIDER analyzed 1.95 million PubMed abstracts, adding 2.31 million previously unrepresented, literature-supported entity pairs to construct SPIDER-KG. Daily updates incorporate relations and evidence from newly indexed PubMed records. Across 89,937 evidence-supported comparisons of potentially incompatible relations, SPIDER classified 79.0% as contextual differences, and 6.1% as genuine disagreement, achieving 80.3% macro-F1 averaged across both categories against expert annotations.…

items.title: Learning spatial cellular state through 3D reconstruction of the cell
items.summary: Subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics localizes individual RNA transcripts within cells with high-precision. Existing methods for identifying spatially organized cell populations rely on cellular niches defined by neighboring cells, leaving open whether such populations can be identified from individual-cell representations alone. Moreover, representations that jointly capture transcript identity and three-dimensional (3D) spatial organization have not been systematically learned or biologically evaluated. Here we present a representation learning framework that models each cell as a gene-annotated point cloud of transcripts and trains a rotation-equivariant neural network to reconstruct 3D cell shape, yielding spatially informed transcript embeddings. We further aggregate these embeddings into a cell-state representation that summarizes transcript-level spatial patterns.…

items.title: Benchmarking four large language models on generating and selecting hypotheses that match published findings in 50 studies of ageing biology
items.summary: Objective We asked how often hypotheses generated by large language models for 50 research tasks matched the withheld finding of the published study, and whether model forecasts could identify the matching hypotheses. Methods We built tasks from 50 peer-reviewed studies in ageing biology published after the models' stated training cutoffs; each task gave the background and a research question and withheld the study's finding (the reference finding). GPT-6 Astra, Grok 4.5, Claude Opus 5.5, and Gemini 4 Argon each generated five hypotheses per task by three methods: a single request, a multistep pipeline, and the Omega Point method without literature search (2997 hypotheses).…

items.title: GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes from histology to map senescence across aging and disease
items.summary: Spatial omics has generated measurements at unprecedented scale, yet computational approaches remain largely confined to individual modalities and 2D representations. Here we assemble ImageOmicsNet-300M, a corpus of 300 million single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiles, including 24.9 million H&E-predicted virtual spatial transcriptomics profiles, and 4,623 H&E sections. Of these H&E sections, we generated 1,782 from aging mouse organs and serially sectioned human skin spanning five decades, with matched spatial transcriptomics and snRNA-seq. Building on this resource, we develop GenVinci, a multimodal tissue foundation model that reconstructs 3D tissue scenes from routine 2D histology.…

items.title: Hidden but Expanding Sampling Bias Distorts Prokaryotic Genome Collections
items.summary: Public genome collections underpin our understanding of bacterial diversity and the distribution of traits such as antibiotic resistance, and increasingly serve as training data for genomic foundation models. Their growing size promises an increasingly complete view of microbial genetic variation. However, these collections combine studies with different sampling priorities, often overrepresenting subgroups of closely related strains of particular interest. The resulting bias reduces effective information, and its consequences for diversity estimates and the value of further sequencing remain insufficiently quantified. Here we show that accounting for this escalating sampling bias is essential for accurate gene frequency estimates and hints at greater genomic diversity than current data suggest.…

items.title: Fine-tuned DNA sequence language models for predicting gene expression in admixed population: A comparison with variant-based methods
items.summary: Predicting gene expression from whole genome sequencing data is essential for elucidating regulatory mechanisms and interpreting functional consequences of non-coding variants to complex diseases. While traditional approaches rely on variant-based linear models, DNA sequence-based language models have gained increasing popularity for their ability to learn regulatory features directly from whole genome sequence data. Previous studies have evaluated models such as Enformer, but newer sequence-to-function models, including Borzoi and AlphaGenome, remain less well characterized for individual-level gene expression prediction, particularly in non-European and admixed populations. Here, we evaluated and fine-tuned Borzoi and AlphaGenome using personal genomes paired with whole-blood RNA-seq data from the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos (HCHS/SOL).…

items.title: Regulatory grammar design of tissue-specific enhancers across species
items.summary: Enhancers encode tissue-specific gene expression through the combinatorial identity, number, and arrangement of transcription factor motifs, collectively known as regulatory grammar. However, existing deep-learning methods directly optimize nucleotide sequences, leaving enhancer regulatory grammar implicit. Here we introduce REgulatory Grammar Architecture via reinforcement Learning (REGAL), a framework that explicitly programs enhancer grammar under sequence-to-function oracles. REGAL generated tissue-specific enhancers across species using the same placement architecture with interchangeable oracles and motif vocabularies. Experimental validation and perturbation revealed that tissue specificity requires coordinated target-tissue activation and off-target repression, depends on both motif composition and spatial organization, and employs distinct regulatory strategies across tissues.…

items.title: Computable Genomes: A Layered Computational Framework for Non-Coding DNA and Cellular Behavior
items.summary: Genome-wide association studies have catalogued tens of thousands of trait-associated loci, most of them in non-coding DNA, yet for most loci the path from nucleotide to phenotype remains correlational. We propose a layered computational decomposition of the genome as a complement to data-driven approaches: sequence as formal language, sequence as information-bearing signal, mobile elements as runtime, compilation to interaction networks through thermodynamic and rule-based models, and execution as cellular and multicellular dynamics. Each layer is defined by its inputs, outputs and formalisms, and we set out where the frame breaks down, including the looseness of algorithmic-information estimates, the triviality of universality results and the failure of string grammars at the chromatin level.…

items.title: MARRI: Mechanism-Aware Learning of RNA-RNA Interactions with Foundation Models
items.summary: RNA-RNA interactions (RRIs) are central to post-transcriptional regulation, yet their prediction requires accounting for structural accessibility and intermolecular base pairing beyond sequence complementarity. Pretrained RNA foundation models provide representations of individual RNAs, but translating these representations into interaction predictions requires mechanistic knowledge of interaction recognition. Here, we introduce MARRI, a mechanism-aware multimodal framework that couples pretrained representations with domain knowledge by embedding learned opening penalties and hybridization gains into bidirectional cross-RNA attention. MARRI improves ROC--AUC and PR--AUC over the strongest baseline by 12.20\% and 10.25\%, respectively, and maintains strong discrimination for unseen RNA partnerships and interaction regions.…

items.title: An Interactive Trustworthy AI Pathology Copilot to Improve Biomarker-Driven Prognostic Stratification and Therapeutic Response Prediction
items.summary: Predictive assays for precision oncology increasingly rely on multi-scale biomarkers that manifest as morphological signatures in routine whole-slide images (WSIs). However, most computational pathology models treat biomarker profiling and outcome prediction (i.e., prognostic stratification and therapeutic response) as independent tasks, and lack the interactive and trustworthy capabilities required for clinical translation. Here, we present TEAM, an interactive trustworthy AI pathology copilot that improves biomarker-driven outcome prediction. Pretrained on 55,648 pan-cancer WSIs and 1,750,648 regions of interest (ROIs), comprising 360 million patches, TEAM learns risk-aware embeddings by conditioning on clinical metadata and aligning with the relative risk prior.…

items.title: Active Health Problems in Real-World Consultations on a Purpose-Built Medical AI Platform
items.summary: Importance: Consumers use conversational artificial intelligence (AI) for health at scale, but whether purpose-built medical AI is used primarily for information seeking or as an entry point into care remains unclear. Objective: To characterize the clinical concepts users present, their visit intentions, and progression to physician telehealth care in real-world consultations on a purpose-built medical AI platform. Design: Exploratory retrospective cohort study of consultations sampled in equal monthly numbers between June 1, 2025, and June 30, 2026. Setting: A free, publicly available, consumer-facing, anonymous-by-default medical AI platform. Participants: Random sample of 26,000 English-language consultations by users aged 18 years or older, each with at least 5 chat interaction rounds. Exposure: A chat consultation with the medical AI.…

items.title: Manifestation-Guided Adaptation of CT Foundation Model for Early Neurological Prognosis after ECPR
items.summary: Purpose. To develop a data-efficient, clinically guided transfer-learning framework for hyperacute neurological outcome prediction from head CT in patients undergoing extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) after cardiac arrest by leveraging free-text radiology report. Methods. This retrospective study included 683 patients with available CT examination and radiology reports from December 2015 to November 2025. The primary outcome distinguished favorable neurological outcomes (Cerebral Performance Category [CPC] 1-2) from neurological death due to brain death or cerebral herniation (CPC 5). A cross-attention adaptor jointly learned to predict neurological outcome and five report-derived manifestations of brain injury from a frozen pretrained head CT encoder. Outcome prediction used CT images alone at inference.…

items.title: 2D anomaly detection of fatal cerebral hemorrhage on postmortem CT
items.summary: Postmortem computed tomography (PMCT) is increasingly used in forensic medicine, yet image interpretation remains largely manual and time-consuming, and supervised deep learning is constrained by the scarcity of annotated forensic datasets. This study investigated whether diffusion-based generative models can detect fatal cerebral haemorrhage on PMCT through reconstruction-based anomaly detection, using solely image-level labels derived from the documented cause of death. Postmortem brain CT examinations acquired at a single forensic institute between 2011 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed, comprising 265 healthy subjects and 33 cases of fatal intracranial haemorrhage.…

items.title: Intracranial pressure waveform estimation using extracranial signals with deep learning
items.summary: Continuous intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring requires invasive instrumentation and reaches only a subset of the critically ill patients who may need it. We tested whether deep learning models trained on routinely acquired extracranial signals can estimate ICP waveforms with clinically motivated point-estimate accuracy. Five architectures were trained on arterial blood pressure (ABP), photoplethysmography (PPG), and electrocardiography (ECG) waveforms, using invasive intraparenchymal ICP as ground truth, and compared across two fusion strategies and three training objectives. Models were externally validated on the independent MIMIC-III (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III) Waveform Database. Performance was assessed by mean absolute error (MAE) and Pearson correlation (r).…
categories: intensive care and critical care medicine

items.title: PedDx: An End-to-End Deep Learning Framework for Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumor Diagnosis with Agentic AI-Enabled Independent External Evaluation
items.summary: Reliable clinical translation of diagnostic artificial intelligence (AI) requires evaluation beyond classification accuracy. We developed PedDx, a segmentation-free framework for pediatric posterior fossa tumor diagnosis using T2-weighted MRI, pretrained 3DINO representations, calibrated predictions, and confidence-based abstention. Evaluation included 492 discovery, 114 replication, 129 external validation, and 40 independently tested cases, alongside 236 out-of-distribution (OOD) cases and controlled imaging perturbations. Classification accuracy was 79.8% in replication and 81.4% in external validation, increasing to 90.5% and 88.7%, respectively, among non-abstained cases. OOD analyses revealed performance degradation and confidently incorrect predictions, while perturbation analyses identified acquisition and alignment vulnerabilities.…

items.title: Agentic AI versus pediatric emergency physicians for differential diagnosis of acutely ill and injured children
items.summary: BackgroundMisdiagnosis and delayed diagnosis of children in pediatric emergency departments lead to complications, and are particularly problematic in settings with limited pediatric expertise. Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in diagnostic reasoning for adult emergency department patients, but utility for pediatric cases is largely untested. MethodsRetrospective study of patients seen in the emergency department of a major urban pediatric academic medical center and subsequently admitted to the operating room or inpatient service. Records from 100 patients were randomly selected, stratified by age. We compared the accuracy of differential diagnoses (up to five, ranked by likelihood) generated by a previously developed agentic AI system, Dr.…

items.title: Widening racial and ethnic disparities in Helicobacter pylori infection in the United States: a Bayesian meta-analytic catalytic model of age-specific forces of infection
items.summary: Background Helicobacter pylori is the main cause of non-cardia gastric cancer. In the U.S. H. pylori seroprevalence has declined. However, whether all subgroups have benefited equally from this change is unclear. Further, prevalence alone cannot indicate when infection risk is most acute and thus when to target prevention efforts like screening. Methods We synthesized age-stratified H. pylori seroprevalence data from 36 U.S. studies (N=56,845; 1965-2014), identified via literature search through September 2022. We fitted Bayesian hierarchical catalytic epidemic models to estimate, by race/ethnicity (for each of five race/ethnicity groups) and birth cohort (pre-1960 vs. 1960+, or continuous), the maximum proportion infected, age-specific force of infection (FOI), and the age at half-maximum seroprevalence.…

items.title: A Whole-Blood Four-Gene Panel Distinguishes Pediatric Crohn's Disease from Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction
items.summary: Background and Aims: Crohn's disease and disorders of gut-brain interaction present with overlapping symptoms, and distinguishing them often requires endoscopy. We assessed whether the whole-blood transcriptome at presentation distinguishes these conditions and reflects disease activity. Methods: In a prospective two-center cohort, whole-blood RNA sequencing was performed in 425 treatment-naive participants aged 5 to 25 years (112 Crohn's disease, 313 disorders of gut-brain interaction). Differential expression was modeled for diagnosis and, within Crohn's disease, for the Pediatric Crohn's Disease Activity Index. Co-expression modules were integrated with protein-protein interaction networks, and machine learning distilled network genes into a diagnostic panel, evaluated internally and in an independent pediatric cohort.…

items.title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to infer psychological attributes, predict individual behaviour, and simulate human populations. However, despite generating plausible responses, they often misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics. Here we introduce Chiron, a foundation model to measure and predict human behaviour. We jointly fine-tune an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics. The training and evaluation data span 36 behavioural domains and 78 social science experiments, comprising 288,307 person records, 1,411,750 atomic behavioural decisions, and 99,953 psychometric assessments over 109 psychological constructs.…
items.tldr: A foundation model fine-tuned from a large language model measures and predicts human behaviour and aligns simulated population responses with human statistics, improving accuracy over frontier LLMs.

items.title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
items.summary: A central challenge in adapting large language models (LLMs) is capability preservation: an adaptation can achieve its target while degrading general capabilities. We introduce CurvDelta, a scalable framework that incorporates the preservation constraint into the parameterization of the model update. By analyzing the local geometry of the preservation constraint around the pre-adaptation model, CurvDelta constructs a low-curvature space in which parameter updates leave the preservation loss nearly invariant. We make its construction practical for LLMs through Kronecker-factored approximate curvature (K-FAC) and a factorized projection. We also introduce CurvLoRA, a low-rank variant within the same preservation geometry, designed for more efficient adaptation. Both methods apply to preservation-constrained adaptation tasks such as capability learning and selective unlearning.…
items.tldr: CurvDelta and CurvLoRA constrain LLM updates to a low-curvature preservation space, improving retention while maintaining target adaptation across reasoning, code, and unlearning tasks.

items.title: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents routinely interact with untrusted external data, exposing them to indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks that hijack agents into executing attacker-chosen tasks. To uncover these vulnerabilities at scale, automated red-teaming methods often leverage reinforcement learning (RL) to generate attacks that achieve high attack success rates (ASR). Model developers use the attacks discovered during internal red-teaming to harden agents through adversarial training before deployment, a collaborative offensive-defensive process known in cybersecurity as purple-teaming. However, we show that achieving high ASR during red-teaming does not guarantee robustness gains from subsequent adversarial training.…
items.tldr: A novel framework addresses the limitations of current reinforcement learning-based red-teaming methods by employing dictionary learning and on-policy adversarial training to improve the robustness of LLM agents against indirect prompt injection attacks.

items.title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
items.summary: Pretrained Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) provide strong representations for downstream classification tasks. Yet adapting a TSFM under changing operating conditions remains challenging. A model must improve on each newly observed condition without sacrificing conditions it has already learned, often from only a small labeled calibration set and without knowing the operating condition at inference time. We find that this difficulty has an important geometric structure. Under an operating-condition shift, the embedding space of a TSFM does not move uniformly: some local regions change substantially, while others remain nearly unchanged. Consequently, a global adaptation can unnecessarily move embeddings that were already correctly classified. To address this, we propose the novel PACT (Piecewise Adaptation via Chart Transport).…
items.tldr: PACT adapts a pretrained time-series foundation model to new operating conditions by partitioning its frozen embedding space into local charts and learning gated residual transports that preserve previously learned conditions, achieving high macro-F1 with limited labeled calibration data and no…

items.title: TabBioMed: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Biomedical Tabular Learning
items.summary: Recent advances in machine learning have accelerated biomedical prediction, but evaluation on structured biomedical data remains fragmented, especially for datasets with high dimensionality, large sample size, missingness, and class imbalance. We introduce TabBioMed, a large-scale benchmark of 94 curated public biomedical tabular datasets spanning electronic health records, drug discovery, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, single-cell omics, and systems biology. TabBioMed unifies these datasets through a standardized, dataset-aware preprocessing and evaluation framework, enabling reproducible comparison across classification, regression, and multi-target tasks. We benchmark 23 models across classical baselines, gradient-boosted trees, neural tabular architectures, and tabular foundation models.…
items.tldr: A large-scale benchmark of 94 curated biomedical tabular datasets standardizes evaluation across classification, regression, and multi-target tasks and finds that foundation models lead overall while tree-based models and tuned multilayer perceptrons remain competitive under cost constraints.

items.title: UltraTex: Aligning Physical Knowledge for High-Fidelity PBR Texture Generation
items.summary: Generating physically based rendering (PBR) texture maps for a 3D mesh from a single reference image is highly ambiguous, as the observed appearance entangles material identity, surface reflectance, and illumination. While current generative methods produce realistic albedo maps, they still struggle to infer accurate metallic and roughness attributes for relighting. We present UltraTex, a cascaded multi-view framework that moves beyond appearance matching by integrating physical knowledge into multi-view diffusion-based PBR generation. UltraTex first jointly predicts albedo and world-space shading normals to generate more detailed albedo maps, and then predicts metallic-roughness (MR) maps conditioned on the generated albedo, reference image, and material semantic priors.…
items.tldr: UltraTex employs a cascaded multi-view framework that integrates physical knowledge and vision-language model features to accurately generate physically plausible PBR texture maps.

items.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
items.summary: System One models such as Jev return decisions through fast, parallel prediction. In this paper, we introduce Jeveration, showing that the same decision paradigm can also generate high-quality images in a single forward pass. Jeveration builds on a frozen vision-language model, repurposing its visual-semantic knowledge for holistic image generation. The key challenge is to maintain global consistency. A single prompt admits many valid images, yet parallel predictions must converge on a coherent whole. We therefore condition all positions on a shared random state to coordinate parallel predictions, so that each draw yields a different but coherent image. Since the model tends to ignore this state under direct image supervision, we first learn a distribution over discrete image codes to guide single-pass generation.…
items.tldr: Jeveration repurposes a frozen vision-language model to generate coherent images and perform image-to-image and dense prediction tasks in a single forward pass with fast 512x512 generation.

items.title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). The models predict probabilities over candidate answers for general-purpose text and visual judgments, agent harnesses, data workflows, and interactive games. Piccolo-27B tops the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard with a score of 75.59, while Piccolo-9B and Piccolo-4B achieve 68.35 and 67.46, respectively. All three rank first on the Private benchmark in their respective model-size categories. Research agents analyze model behavior, construct training data, conduct experiments, and use the results to refine subsequent proposals. Semantic slices and a shared research memory connect these actions across the model family's development.…

items.title: StrideWorld: Benchmarking Scene Rigidity and Action Consistency in Interactive Video World Model
items.summary: Interactive video world models turn user commands into the exploration of a generated scene, which requires the scene to keep its 3D structure as the camera moves and each action to keep a stable effect. Existing benchmarks mostly evaluate these properties against references fitted to the video under test, either a scene reconstructed from its own frames or a camera trajectory aligned to the command path with a free scale. Such references can absorb gradual scene deformation and changes in pace and route length, so these errors can pass undetected. We therefore introduce StrideWorld, a benchmark whose references are fixed before the motion they judge. It evaluates scene rigidity against the ground-truth geometry of the start view, and action consistency against the stride of each action, the camera motion of one command.…
items.tldr: StrideWorld is a benchmark that fixes references before motion to detect scene deformation and action inconsistency in interactive video world models, showing that most models deform scenes and only depth-scaled command models preserve composed routes.

items.title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Video rough-cut is a core stage in media production workflows, organizing raw media materials into an initial video cut.
