Because PDZ recognition preferences overlap, modulating intended interactions requires considering off-target binding alongside target affinity. Computational PBM design methods generally use sequence-based affinity prediction and structure-based evaluation, but it remains challenging to guide sequence searches toward different binding objectives with a single trained model. Here, we propose a deep learning-based method to design PBMs by analytically formulating single-target, off-target-aware, and dual-target design objectives as directions in a PDZ-PBM shared latent space learned through quantitative PDZ-PBM affinity prediction.…

items.title: Bloom unifies brain cell representations across modalities and contexts
items.summary: Multimodal genomic datasets now profile mammalian brain cells across anatomical regions, developmental stages, disease states, and species. Learning shared representations that capture cellular diversity across these heterogeneous observations remains a central challenge. Here, we introduce Bloom, a transformer-based model that represents cells using gene expression, chromatin accessibility, or both. Bloom is trained on 300,000 adult mouse brain cells with paired measurements, randomly sampled with broad-subclass balancing--approximately 100-fold fewer cells than used by comparable pre-trained models. By combining genomic sequence embeddings with randomly sampled multimodal cell views, Bloom outperforms unimodal cell models in resolving brain-wide cell types and in annotation, regression, and label-transfer tasks.…

items.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Protein Language Models Reveals Encoded Structural and Functional Properties of Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
items.summary: Protein language models (PLMs) such as ESM-2 encode protein sequences as embeddings for downstream tasks. PLMs are trained on a masked learning objective that leverages evolutionary constraints. While interpretability studies of ESM-2 have focused on folded proteins, their behavior on intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), which constitute a substantial fraction of the human proteome and are implicated in numerous diseases, remains understudied. Because IDPs experience different types of evolutionary constraints on their amino acid sequences, we hypothesized that PLMs would behave differently on disordered versus folded regions. Here we show that ESM-2 exhibits reduced attention on disordered regions, yet still encodes meaningful biological signals. The model assigns heightened attention to disease-relevant residues even at high levels of disorder.…

items.title: Regional Signals Matter: Rethinking Global Pooling for mRNA Foundation Models
items.summary: RNA foundation models with diverse architectures have shown promise for learning representations of messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences. However, existing benchmarks commonly reduce token-level embeddings to transcript-level representations through global mean pooling before fitting a downstream probe. This aggregation does not explicitly preserve the identities of biologically distinct mRNA regions. Consequently, signals associated with short regulatory regions may be diluted, confounding assessments of representation quality with the information preserved by the readout. We introduce an architecture-agnostic, region-aware readout that separately averages embeddings within the 5$'$ untranslated region (UTR), coding sequence, and 3$'$ UTR and concatenates the resulting representations for linear probing.…

items.title: Spatial multi-omic profiling of non-autonomous transcriptomic and epigenomic responses to genetic perturbation
items.summary: Multicellular organisms develop and maintain differentiated cell states through a combination of cell-autonomous and non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms, including signal transduction pathways mediated by ligands, receptors, and kinases. Genetic perturbation through CRISPR pooled screening is widely used to study cell-autonomous regulatory mechanisms, but the challenges of cellular-resolution in situ measurement have limited the study of non-autonomous regulatory mechanisms. We developed Perturb-Tags, a spatial multi-omic technique for pooled CRISPR screening that tags nuclei with spatial barcodes, allowing joint measurement of single-nucleus gene expression, CRISPR guide RNAs, chromatin accessibility, and spatial positions within intact tissue.…

items.title: Graph-guided flow matching enables biologically informed prediction at single-cell resolution
items.summary: Perturb-seq enables systematic interrogation of massively parallel genetic perturbations at single-cell resolution, yet exhaustive characterization of the full perturbation space remains impractical. Here, we present Graph-guided Flow Matching (GFM), a generative framework that integrates biological knowledge graphs with latent flow matching to predict post-perturbation single-cell transcriptomes. Across multiple large-scale Perturb-seq datasets, GFM outperforms a strong linear baseline and current deep-learning models in predicting unseen single-gene perturbations, while training up to 30x faster and remaining robust with limited training data. GFM also demonstrates competitive performance in the two-gene perturbation prediction task when neither perturbed gene is observed during training.…

items.title: ModBERT: a DNA modification and genetic variant-aware DNA large language model
items.summary: The development of foundation models that learn a general grammar of DNA (DNA language models) has accelerated in recent years. The vast majority of DNA large language models (LLMs), such as DNABERT-2 and Nucleotide Transformer, are pretrained almost exclusively on reference genomes. They therefore cannot represent the two sources of variation most directly tied to regulatory differences between people: genetic variants and DNA methylation. Long-read sequencing (Nanopore and PacBio) now measures both from the same native DNA molecules, but no model is designed to use this joint readout. With this in mind, we developed ModBERT, a DNA language model built on a five-letter probabilistic genome representation in which each position is a distribution over A, C, G, T, 5mC (represented with M).…

items.title: DynamicsPLM: A Dynamics-Enriched Small Protein Language Model for Protein Variant Effect Prediction
items.summary: Predicting how mutations impact protein function and stability remains a key challenge in computational biology. Current state-of-the-art protein language models (PLMs) primarily scale parameter size on sequence corpora to capture evolutionary constraints but remain blind to the explicit physical dynamics of folded proteins. Conversely, models trained strictly on physical dynamics neglect critical evolutionary sequence statistics. In this paper, we bridge this gap by introducing DynamicsPLM, a highly parameter-efficient 35-million-parameter model that unifies evolutionary and biophysical representation learning. Utilizing a second-stage, multi-task continual pretraining strategy on over 60,000 proteins, we enrich a foundational sequence encoder with explicit residue-level and pairwise molecular dynamics heads while preserving its original evolutionary knowledge.…

items.title: HieraPTM: From PTM Site Recognition to Functional Phosphosite Prediction through Hierarchical Context and Protein Mechanics
items.summary: Protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate cellular signaling and protein function, making accurate site identification essential for understanding protein regulation. However, PTM site recognition and functional phosphosite prediction are largely modeled independently, limiting the transfer of large-scale recognition knowledge to functional prioritization. Here, we introduce HieraPTM-HieraFuncPhos, a cross-task hierarchical framework that separately models and conditionally integrates transferable PTM recognition representations and function-specific mechanical evidence. HieraPTM integrates local sequence patterns, protein language model representations, and three-dimensional structural information to recognize multiple PTM types.…

items.title: Unsupervised Deep Learning for Cryo-EM/ET Particle Classification
items.summary: Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is widely used to determine protein structures from purified samples. With cryogenic electron tomography (cryo-ET), it is possible to image thin sections of cells and directly visualize diverse proteins in their native environment. However, separating the massive mixture of different types of proteins inside cells remains challenging, especially without human intervention. In this work, we present an unsupervised deep learning framework for classifying cryo-EM/ET particle images that jointly optimizes for pose and structure through an autoencoder-based multi-stage pipeline. On single-particle cryo-EM datasets, our framework can capture the continuous variation in particle views and separate images of real particles from contamination.…

items.title: Chimera: Cross-Species Single-Cell Generative Modeling of Expression Deployment Relative to Protein Conservation
items.summary: A protein's sequence says what a gene could do in another species; the cells of that species say what it does there. Comparative genomics measures the first. Chimera measures the second, a gene's deployment, on the same genes and reports the difference. It aligns single-cell atlases across species in one generative model and returns, for every one-to-one ortholog, the evidence in the counts for a shared expression pattern, and {Delta}[a], the position of that evidence above or below what the protein's identity predicts. This difference is not sequence constraint under another name: across eight tissues, protein identity tracks dN/dS, whereas {Delta}[a] tracks neither.…

items.title: Large language models complement established workflows for mechanistic model construction and refinement in systems biology
items.summary: Mechanistic models provide a framework for describing, understanding, and predicting biological processes, but their development requires an interdisciplinary team with expertise in biology, mathematics, and computation. Here we present Octomod, a multi-agent workflow based on large language models (LLMs) that integrates biological knowledge retrieval, model construction, parameter estimation, and hypothesis testing. Built on established software tools, including AMICI and pyPESTO, and community standards, including SBML and PEtab, Octomod supports model development and refinement through natural-language interaction with a user. The agents' proposals must pass defined checks and the user's decision before they are used. Every input, model, check, and decision is recorded, so that model building remains transparent and reproducible. We applied Octomod to four problems.…

items.title: MicroDUET: a dual-headed genomic foundation model for pathogen surveillance
items.summary: Pathogen genomic surveillance works from raw reads, assembled genomes and alignments, representations that are slow and costly to compare at scale. Compact embeddings from genomic language models offer an alternative, but surveillance requires resolving both evolutionary ancestry (phylogeny) and phenotypic capability (function) - which need not co-vary. Here we present MicroDUET, which adapts a 26.6-million-parameter ProkBERT backbone with two 3.5-million-parameter adapter heads: a phylogeny head trained contrastively on genome windows from the same microbes, and a function head trained to identify genes across taxa.…

items.title: DeepRNAi: Predicting on- and off-target siRNA activity and establishing a benchmark
items.summary: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) silence target genes through RISC-mediated hybridization and cleavage, but can silence unintended transcripts and cause toxicity or complicate regulatory approval. In drug development, empirical assessment by qPCR and RNA-seq is slow, forces early candidate prioritization, and is limited by available species- and genome-appropriate cell models. While extensive empirical screening remains standard practice, there is a significant opportunity for modern AI methods to change this paradigm. We introduce DeepRNAi, a deep learning model that accurately predicts on- and off-target knockdown from siRNA and mRNA sequence.…

items.title: Automatic classification of seizure adequacy in electroconvulsive therapy: A proof-of-concept study
items.summary: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is the most effective treatment of a range of severe mental dis-orders and is annually given to more than a million patients worldwide. Dosing of the electrical charge is critical for efficacy and side-effect burden; however, it is currently based on manual assessment of seizure quality and exhibits substantial clinical heterogeneity. Here, we collected 1,000 ECT session electroencephalograms (EEG) from 130 individual ECT patients and made an expert-level classification of the EEGs into actionable seizure quality categories (null-response [0], threshold [T], and adequate [A]). We then trained a range of machine learning algorithms on the raw EEG data to classify the EEGs into these categories and tested for classi-fication accuracy.…

items.title: DxToniaNet: A Neural Network for Estimating the Severity of Leg Dystonia in Children with Cerebral Palsy
items.summary: Importance: Leg dystonia affects 50-80% of children with cerebral palsy (CP), but severity assessment remains subjective and time-consuming. Objective tools are urgently needed to quantify leg dystonia severity in clinical care and clinical trials. Objective: To develop and validate a deep neural network (DxToniaNet) for leg dystonia severity estimation using 2D clinical video recordings. Design, Setting, and Participants: We retrospectively analyzed video recordings of 298 children with cerebral palsy undergoing a seated hand open-close task as part of routine clinical care (Center 1: 193 videos, 720p/30fps; Center 2: 105 videos, 4K/60fps). Videos were rated for leg dystonia severity by a group of 7 experts using the Global Dystonia Rating Scale (GDRS) leg subscore (range 0-40) which has a minimum clinically important difference (MCID) of 4 points.…

items.title: Ontology-Based SEA-CDM Integration for Vaccine Clinical Trials: Query, Similarity, and Design Recommendation
items.summary: ClinicalTrials.gov provides valuable information for vaccine research, but fragmented data structures and inconsistent vaccine naming complicate systematic cross-trial analysis. The Study-Experiment-Assay Common Data Model (SEA-CDM) provides a standardized structure for biomedical study data, while biomedical ontologies supply semantic relationships among concepts. We extracted 9,147 vaccine-related study records from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) database, mapped their records into SEA-CDM, and linked vaccine products and reported adverse events (AEs) to the Vaccine Ontology (VO) and Ontology of Adverse Events (OAE), respectively. Building on the existing Ontology-based SEA Network (OSEAN), we organized the integrated data into relational tables and a Neo4j knowledge graph while retaining links to original registrations.…

items.title: RESCUE: An end-to-end multi-agent LLM system for proactive rare-disease patient screening in the EHR
items.summary: Rare diseases affect a significant portion of the global population, yet patients often endure a lengthy diagnostic odyssey and miss timely diagnosis with exome or genome sequencing (ES/GS). Existing informatics tools often rely on pre-identified patients or institution-specific rule sets that are laborious to implement locally and rarely address clinical utility and operational feasibility. We introduce RESCUE, an end-to-end, multi-agent LLM-powered workflow that automates the local implementation of both rule-based and machine learning screening algorithms across the entire electronic health record (EHR).…

items.title: Enrollees and Early Lessons from an Agentic Healthcare Platform with Physicians in the Loop
items.summary: Agentic healthcare platforms that combine large language models with physician oversight are growing quickly, but little is known about who uses them. We characterized 3,223 enrollees of Lotus AI, a free, physician-supervised agentic platform, who completed onboarding, messaged the agent, and had a linked health record between February and July 2026, and compared them with national benchmarks. Median age was 51 years and 62% were male. Chronic condition prevalence exceeded 2024 National Health Interview Survey estimates in every age band by 4 to 7 percentage points; 18% had a functional or symptom-defined disorder; among the 30% with four or more ambulatory visits in the prior year, care was spread across nearly five providers, with 44% meeting a threshold for high fragmentation.…

items.title: BenchmarkHub: an open-source platform for reproducible evaluation of large language models in healthcare
items.summary: Background: Large language models (LLMs) are solely judged by their scores on biomedical benchmarks, yet these scores are rarely reproducible since the prompts, inference settings and model builds are seldom reported. We developed BenchmarkHub, an open-source platform for auditable evaluation of language and vision-language models for biomedical research. Methods: BenchmarkHub is a Python web application (Django 5.2, SQLite) released under the MIT licence and available at https://github.com/juanjuanignacio/benchmarkhub. The application can be accessed through a browser interface, a set of command-line tools and a REST API, so interactive exploration and scripted pipelines produce identical, comparable records.…

items.title: Artificial intelligence for pulmonary tuberculosis detection on chest X-ray images: A systematic review and diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based computer-aided detection (CAD) of tuberculosis (TB) on chest X-ray (CXR) may standardize screening and triage in settings with few radiologists but its accuracy in clinical cohorts remains uncertain. We searched five databases (PubMed, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, OpenAlex, Lens.org) on 15 March 2026 for studies published between January 2020 and March 2026, and we appraised these studies using QUADAS-2. Evaluations from clinical cohorts with complete 2 x 2 data and a microbiological or composite reference standard for all participants were pooled using a bivariate random-effects model, with 95% prediction intervals. We accounted for overlapping participants by performing a post hoc analysis with one evaluation per cohort and used GRADE to assess the certainty of the evidence. No protocol was prepared or registered.…

items.title: Do Rule-Derived Labels Improve Prediction When Reported Labels Are Limited? A Two-Site Machine Learning Study
items.summary: **Background.** Rule derived (weak) labels can enlarge a training set when reported labels are scarce. Their value depends on label quality, on how the extra records shift the training distribution, and on whether the comparison accounts for reported labels set aside for tuning or calibration. **Methods.** We ran an exploratory label-budget experiment on *Escherichia coli* urine cultures from two de-identified electronic health record datasets: Stanford ARMD and UT Southwestern ARMD-UTSW. The task was to predict reported non-susceptibility to cefepime, cefoxitin and ceftazidime (Stanford) and to cefepime and ceftazidime (UT Southwestern). Reported-label budgets of 10%, 25%, 50% and 100% of development patients were drawn over five patient-disjoint outer splits.…

items.title: Fast, accurate construction of multiple sequence alignments from protein language embeddings
items.summary: Multiple sequence alignment (MSA) is a foundational task in computational biology, underpinning protein structure prediction, evolutionary analysis, and domain annotation. Traditional MSA algorithms rely on pairwise amino acid substitution matrices derived from conserved protein families. While effective for aligning closely related sequences, these scoring schemes struggle in the low-identity ``twilight zone.'' Here, we present a new approach for constructing MSAs leveraging amino acid embeddings generated by protein language models (PLMs), which capture rich evolutionary and contextual information from massive and diverse sequence datasets. We introduce a windowed reciprocal-weighted embedding similarity metric that is surprisingly effective in identifying corresponding amino acids across sequences.…

items.title: Human-supervised Agentic AI for Hypothesis Generation and Experimental Assistance in Drug Repurposing
items.summary: Computational drug repurposing has focused largely on rapid hypothesis generation, yet real-world applications span a much broader lifecycle: suggesting drug candidates, designing experiments, analyzing assay data, and iteratively refining hypotheses. Here, we demonstrate that agentic AI can operate throughout this lifecycle. We developed RepurAgent, a hierarchical multi-agentic system comprising a supervisor agent and a planning agent that coordinates four specialized sub-agents (research, prediction, data, and report) with human in the loop, supported by episodic memory and retrieval-augmented generation. The system is grounded in repurposing-specific data, tools, and standard operating procedures developed within the REMEDi4ALL consortium.…

items.title: RNAbridge: a database of extended non-canonical helices
items.summary: RNA function is dictated by 3D architecture. Although 2D structural models based on canonical Watson-Crick base pairs are widely used, they often fail to capture the non-canonical interactions, tertiary contacts, and coaxial stacking important for biological activity. We have developed RNAbridge, a comprehensive database and web application that systematically identifies, quantifies, and visualizes extended non-canonical helices and multi-way junctions ("non-canonical" denoting the interruptions between canonical stems rather than non-canonical pairing within them). Using a geometry- and stacking-based pipeline, we analyzed the Protein Data Bank and compiled a catalog of 153,148 structural elements, with a representative view of 7,453 elements.…

items.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
items.summary: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics.…
items.tldr: Agentic robotics, centered on an Embodied System 2 formed by a foundation model and embodied harness, requires a shared evaluation framework and research roadmap to achieve reliable physical autonomy.

items.title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to finance, creating a need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities across financial systems with different regulations and practices. However, existing financial benchmarks provide limited coverage of country-specific financial systems, and they are difficult to keep up to date as released questions leak into training data. We introduce JFinBench, a Japanese financial benchmark comprising 321 examples from the 2026 editions of six regularly administered certification exams covering accounting, tax, financial planning, and banking. To construct it, we develop a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline in which a coding agent writes exam-specific conversion code and a review page, while a human verifies every example and feeds corrections back to the agent.…

items.title: G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands
items.summary: With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), an increasing number of users are turning to LLM-powered agents for conversational shopping in e-commerce. However, the user needs continue to change as new product categories, procurement scenarios, and feature requests emerge. At the same time, the product's execution harness-including its tools, skills, and operating procedures-continues to evolve to support increasingly sophisticated interactions. These changes create two practical challenges: 1) Demand drift alters the distribution, intent, and complexity of user requests, causing a model trained once to fall behind; 2) Harness evolution requires the model to use newly introduced capabilities correctly without losing behavior that users already rely on. Periodic manual retraining is too delayed and labor-intensive for this setting.…

items.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. Prior work studies how LLM reviews align with human ones, yet we know little about which parts of a paper these models actually criticize. In this work, we investigate 2,000 papers from ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR, and show that the latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of their review weaknesses from the appendix. This behavior holds across the API, coding-agent, and web access methods for using LLMs to review a paper. In contrast, we find that humans draw only 8.4% of their weaknesses from the appendix, and these weaknesses primarily revolve around a paper's presentation and content related to its core idea.…
items.tldr: Large language models used for peer review draw about half or more of their identified weaknesses from paper appendices, whereas human reviewers draw only 8.4% and focus on presentation and core ideas.

items.title: Aligning AI Teams
items.summary: Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. We investigate the underlying mechanisms for this failure, and explore interventions to preserve alignment transfer to multi-agent LLM teams. We focus on two software-engineering tasks (sepsis triage, a news recommender) and ten consulting-proposal generation tasks. We present four findings: (1) The single-vs-team safety gap does not show a clear trend with more capable models. We find that Anthropic's Mythos Preview shows the largest gap on one of our tasks but the smallest on another; (2) Many natural interventions, such as having agents critique each other's work or coordinate in a group chat, do not reliably bring agent teams back to single-agent alignment behavior; (3) diffusion of responsibility substantially accounts for the safety gap: agents in teams are less…
items.tldr: Alignment training on individual LLM agents often fails to transfer to multi-agent teams, but designating a safety lead and having a coordinator publish safety specifications can restore single-agent alignment.

items.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
items.summary: Frontier LLM agents that query databases with tools are among the most accurate text-to-SQL systems, but per-query calls to a hosted model are slow, costly, and expose sensitive organizational queries to external APIs. For example, a Claude Opus 5.5 agent serving 10,000 queries a day costs over $70,000 a year at list price. To what extent can local hardware already owned by an organization offload this burden without compromising the agent's accuracy? We present LuthorSQL, a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model that serves as a rapid System 1 gate for a slower LLM agent (System 2), escalating queries only when uncertain. LuthorSQL makes a single forward pass to predict slot scores over a bounded grammar for query plans, compiles and runs up to 32 candidate plans, and chooses an answer using a trained validator.…

items.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
items.summary: We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction. These trajectories span simulated games and embodied environments, allowing the model to learn environmental dynamics across both physical and virtual domains. Sparse-thinking instruction tuning then substantially reduces redundant computation while preserving the reasoning needed for complex decisions.…
items.tldr: Gamer is a generalist agent framework that integrates perception, memory, and multi-step reasoning, trained through continued pre-training, sparse-thinking instruction tuning, and multi-turn reinforcement learning to interact efficiently in 2D and 3D environments.

items.title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates generation by letting a lightweight drafter propose tokens for parallel verification by a target model. Diffusion drafters such as DFlash propose an entire token block in a single forward pass, but mainly focus on text-only tasks, leaving multimodal drafting underexplored. To study this setting, we first introduce a metric of token-level visual dependence based on the KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input. We find that acceptance rates decrease from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest, with this disparity persisting after multimodal training. Motivated by this observation, we propose MMFlash, a simple and effective framework that adaptively upweights visually dependent tokens that the drafter predicts poorly.…
items.tldr: MMFlash improves multimodal speculative decoding by adaptively upweighting visually dependent tokens and using sparse attention for long video, yielding up to 3.58× lossless speedup.

items.title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
items.summary: World-model video encoders such as V-JEPA learn how scenes change (direction, speed, order, state) from video alone. To answer questions, they are joined to a language model trained on captions and question-answer pairs. But each caption or question names only a few attributes of a clip, so the model learns to retrieve those attributes rather than to read the clip, and the dynamics the encoder carries go unused: on the same items, a linear probe reads speed from frozen V-JEPA features at 87% while the VLM answers at chance. We show where dynamics lives in a frozen encoder: in a subspace shared across videos for predictive encoders such as V-JEPA, but not as a shared component of frame-wise, text-aligned encoders such as SigLIP.…
items.tldr: Counterfactual supervision over pixel transformations enables language models to read motion dynamics from frozen predictive video encoders, yielding V-JEPA-LM models that outperform open video LLMs across benchmarks.

items.title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery
items.summary: Cities account for over two-thirds of the world's energy and more than 70% of global carbon dioxide emissions. City energy is essential for achieving the 2050 net-zero target and the UN's Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 11. Although existing studies have made progress, they are limited by data and methodological gaps. Existing studies are largely predictive for existing cities rather than generative for future cities; fine-grained, aligned monthly dynamic energy data are scarce; and existing GenAI models struggle to generate dynamic urban functional monthly energy. We present DySENSE, a joint multimodal GenAI framework that synthesizes static urban satellite imagery together with spatially aligned, dynamic monthly building energy consumption maps. We decouple long-term static urban morphology from short-term dynamic energy consumption.…

items.title: MEM-SQL: Memory-Empowered Text-to-SQL
items.summary: Text-to-SQL systems translate natural language questions into SQL queries over increasingly complex databases. However, widely used benchmarks evaluate questions independently, overlooking settings where earlier queries over the same database can supply joins or calculations for a new question. We introduce HARE (History-AwaRe Text-to-SQL BEnchmark) to measure the accuracy and cost of adapting historical SQL. HARE comprises 1,600 requests derived from a fixed pool of 823 verified queries across four datasets. Annotations record which components each request preserves and which edits it requires, distinguishing whole-query adaptation from partial reuse. Our method, MEM-SQL (Memory-EMpowered Text-to-SQL), stores whole-query templates, reusable SQL blocks, and mappings from domain concepts to schema elements.…
items.tldr: A history-aware benchmark and memory-powered method improve Text-to-SQL accuracy and reduce cost by reusing verified SQL components and consulting schemas on demand.

items.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
items.summary: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and unconditional settings. The pixel-space formulation of JVT also naturally supports joint generation of pixel-aligned modalities.…
items.tldr: JVT, a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer, enables pixel-space video diffusion without pretrained autoencoders or U-Net skip connections, achieving competitive quality and supporting joint camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation.

items.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
items.summary: Web agents powered by large language and vision-language models are increasingly applied to realistic browser work that spans heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows. However, existing reproducible web-agent benchmarks cover only a small number of web applications drawn from a few software categories, and restrict modality to text and vision. Live benchmarks broaden site coverage but sacrifice reproducibility, since pages and data drift between runs. Moreover, existing benchmarks do not meaningfully evaluate whether agents can understand and use audio and video content embedded within web tasks. To address these gaps, we introduce WebArena-Pro, a benchmark comprising 300 tasks across 20 self-hosted web applications in six domain categories, spanning distinct interface conventions, workflows, and data models.…

items.title: eDIAR: Training-Free Open-Speaker Streaming Diarization for Long Meetings and Large Archives via e-means
items.summary: Meetings last up to an hour, and nobody knows in advance how many people will speak. Neural diarizers with a fixed number of output slots, such as Streaming Sortformer and Nemotron-3, are accurate and run online, but they cannot name more speakers than they have slots. We remove this limit without retraining. The slot head keeps deciding who is active and when speech overlaps, and speaker embeddings are clustered inside a single slot, with the official e-means algorithm, only after every slot has been used. In the streaming system, re-clustering is confined to a bounded window, labels are revised for a few seconds, and identities are anchored to the slots of the head. The resulting system has no limit on the number of speakers and stays accurate when speakers outnumber the slots, where fixed-slot models break down.…
items.tldr: A streaming speaker-diarization method removes the fixed speaker-slot limit by clustering speaker embeddings within slots after all slots are used, allowing unlimited speakers and efficient large-scale linking.

items.title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
items.summary: Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. While prior route-inference attacks have demonstrated that speed, steering, and driving events can be matched to road networks to reconstruct trajectories, existing studies rely on inconsistent prior assumptions and evaluation metrics and are tested only on small, restricted datasets, making their results difficult to compare and their real-world effectiveness uncertain.…

items.title: Do Underwater Image Quality Metrics Agree with Human Perception? A Benchmark with Human Choices, Simple Edits and Generative Drift
items.summary: Underwater image enhancement is challenging to evaluate due to the lack of clean reference images, so researchers rely on no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) metrics. However, it remains unclear whether these metrics agree with human judgments. We evaluate 73 handcrafted underwater, learned underwater, vision-language and general-purpose metrics against human preferences on five references: four published opinion-score sets and a new paired-comparison study. For each metric, we measure how often it selects the same image as people when comparing versions of the same scene. We further test whether simple image edits and small adversarial perturbations raise metric scores above the enhancement people preferred, and whether scores decrease as repeated generative edits add noise. Our results show that no metric consistently matches human preferences.…

items.title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
items.summary: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance comparable to their teachers, but concentrate it into substantially fewer directions. This directional collapse is localized to an identifiable intermediate block at the initial denoising step. Consequently, diversity collapse stems from a misallocation of activation variance rather than an inherent loss of generative capacity. Guided by this finding, we propose ReDiverse to reinstate the missing variance directions.…
items.tldr: Distilled few-step diffusion models exhibit diversity collapse because activation variance is concentrated into fewer directions in an intermediate block at the initial denoising step, and ReDiverse restores sample diversity by reintroducing teacher variance directions through adapter fine-tuning…

items.title: OneSteer: Unlocking Steerable General Humanoid Motion Tracking via One-Step Diffusion Whole-Body Control
items.summary: Deployment objectives often specify desired outcomes without providing revised trajectories, while parts of the original reference must still be followed. We present OneSteer, a one-step diffusion whole-body controller that combines general motion tracking with selective test-time steering. To accommodate new objectives, differentiable task costs guide optimization of the generator's input noise with frozen weights, while body-group reference masks relax selected tracking requirements. Predicted state-action plans provide a shared interface for task optimization and feedback-conditioned execution. For nominal tracking, the model trained from scratch achieves the lowest local tracking error among the evaluated baselines on successful held-out AMASS and BONES clips.…

items.title: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality
items.summary: Robots in homes, warehouses and farms must pick up objects they have never seen, usually without a 3D model or a category label. A grasping policy that works directly on the point cloud from a depth sensor needs only the geometry the robot observes, so it applies to any new object. Offline grasp generators such as Contact-GraspNet work this way, but they rank grasps by learned plausibility rather than by whether the grasp actually lifts the object. Reinforcement learning (RL) can optimize for that directly and make a point-cloud grasping policy much better on average, yet it leaves specific grasps persistently unsolved.…
items.tldr: A human-in-the-loop failure-mining pipeline turns persistently unsolved grasps of a reinforcement-learning point-cloud policy into virtual-reality human demonstrations, improving hard-case success without reducing generalization to unseen objects.

items.title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
items.summary: As AI conference submissions grow rapidly, AI reviewers are being considered as an alternative. However, simply imitating human reviewing is problematic because reviewing serves multiple purposes, including evaluating papers' soundness, interestingness, and clarity, the last two of which are subjective. In this work, we focus solely on evaluating soundness, the most important and objective criterion, and define the learning objective as jointly maximizing (1) precision, based on the soundness and substantiveness of review points, and (2) recall, the coverage of high-quality reference review points. Under this problem formulation, we construct a quality-labeled review point dataset, PaperSound-23K, using 1K ICLR submissions and 23K human-written and LLM-generated review points.…
items.tldr: An AI reviewer trained by reinforcement learning to jointly maximize precision and recall of soundness review points outperforms frontier models and other training methods and transfers to other review domains.

items.title: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech
items.summary: Speech applications require decisions about term presence, turn completion, and language within an audio window. We present Marimba, an interface for typed speech decisions built on frozen Qwen3-ASR 0.6B features. Lexical questions use zero-shot scoring of ASR transcripts; non-lexical questions use a question-conditioned head and a separate layer-18 turn-end readout. Language identification uses the ASR model's own language scores. On private conversational test sets, decoder AUROC is 0.80-0.92; on public read speech it is 0.92-0.97. Speech Commands four-way accuracy is 0.93; binary lexical ECE is at most 0.08. Personal-information detection, which passes the greedy transcript to a private, curated PII pipeline, reaches item-level F1 0.904 on synthetic Brazilian Portuguese speech (1.000 on reference transcripts).…
items.tldr: Marimba uses frozen Qwen3-ASR features and lightweight readouts to make lexical, turn-end, language, speaker-change, and personal-information decisions from speech, achieving strong detection and calibration on conversational and read-speech benchmarks.

items.title: GPBam: A Retrieval-Aware German Public Law Exam Benchmark
items.summary: Legal reasoning in civil-law systems is not rule-lookup: the German state examination asks for a structured opinion (Gutachten) that names the governing norms, applies them to the facts, and argues to a conclusion. We introduce GPBam (German Public Law Bar-style Exam), 81 public-law examination cases with reference solutions, paired with a recitation task over 200 statutory provisions. Drawn from state examination preparation, the cases are broad and rarely repeat, and are not publicly available - we find no evidence of exact-solution memorisation in the models we evaluate, and keeping them private limits contamination.…
items.tldr: A new benchmark of German public-law exam cases and statutory provisions jointly scores legal retrieval and long-form opinion generation across many models, finding that retrieval yields limited gains and essay quality strongly tracks prior statutory knowledge.

items.title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Harness optimization is often studied with a fixed policy model and benchmark. When either changes, the optimizer must decide which parts of an evolved harness to reuse or revise, but the harness alone may not explain why earlier edits were made or how they performed. In this work, we study Continual Recursive Self-Improvement (CRSI), a setting for continuing existing harness-optimization methods across compatible benchmarks or policy models. We propose Self-Improvement Memory (SIM) for the harness optimizer, rather than the task-solving policy. SIM groups edits by recurring harness problem and records their rationale, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation context. New attempts extend this history as optimization continues.…
items.tldr: Continual recursive self-improvement lets harness optimizers reuse and revise prior edits across changing benchmarks or policy models by storing rationales, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation contexts in a self-improvement memory, improving final scores over continuation baselines.

items.title: Learning Anisotropic Prediction Targets for Flow Models
items.summary: Flow-based generative models are trained on a hand-chosen prediction target, such as the velocity, the noise, or the clean data. This choice strongly affects training and sample quality. We introduce Anisotropic Flow Models (AnisoFlow), which replaces a fixed prediction target with a fully learnable one. AnisoFlow learns to scale the noise component of the target anisotropically, assigning a separate nonnegative weight to each direction in a jointly learned basis. A closed-form map recovers the velocity from the network's prediction, leaving the architecture, flow-matching loss, and sampler unchanged. Since recovery is exact, training optimizes the target purely to make it easier for the network to predict.…
items.tldr: AnisoFlow learns an anisotropic, learnable prediction target for flow-based generative models, improving FID and image quality without altering the architecture or sampler.

items.title: Choosing Quantized Code LLMs by File Size and Energy per Solved Task
items.summary: A developer running a code assistant on a laptop downloads one model file, and local inference moves the energy of every request onto that machine. A common rule says a larger model at lower precision tends to beat a smaller one at higher precision. We ran 24 GGUF files of Qwen2.5-Coder at four sizes on a fanless MacBook Air M2 and priced each in energy per solved task on 542 EvalPlus tasks. The result is a selection guide indexed by Ollama's listed file size, with an evidence label on each pick. At 1 and 2 GB it picks the q4_K_M files of the 1.5B and 3B models, both on the correctness and energy frontier under every accounting. At 3 GB as listed, the larger-model rule picks 7B-q2_K, the only measured 7B file that fits, and there it does not pay. That file brings no significant gain in solves over the 2 GB pick, 3B-q4_K_M, and the 90% CI limits any 3B-q4_K_M deficit to 2.4 points.…

items.title: The cop number of the flower snarks, and the generalized Petersen graphs with cop number two
items.summary: We study two questions of Morris, Runte and Skelton (Australas. J. Combin. 83 (2022)) on the game of Cops and Robbers. First, we show that the flower snark $J_n$ has cop number $3$ for every $n\geq 5$, and that $J_3$ has cop number $2$. The upper bound comes from a three-cop strategy, which we call the rolling wall. It works on every connected graph whose vertices can be arranged in a cycle of columns, each dominated by a single vertex. Because only one cop moves on each turn, the same strategy also shows that the lazy cop number of $J_n$ is $3$ for $n\geq 5$. Second, we prove the conjecture of Morris, Runte and Skelton that the only generalized Petersen graphs with cop number $2$ are $\mathrm{GP}(n,1)$ and the four graphs $\mathrm{GP}(6,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(8,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(9,3)$ and $\mathrm{GP}(12,3)$.…

items.title: Offline KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning with Stochastic Transitions
items.summary: KL-regularized reinforcement learning is the objective behind RL fine-tuning of language models, and its data are often collected by the reference policy itself. However, beyond bandits and deterministic transitions, little is known about how much offline data it needs. In this work, we study finite discounted Markov decision processes with unknown stochastic transitions, $K$ state-action pairs and effective horizon $H$. For data that cover the regularized optimum with concentrability $C\geq 4$, every estimator needs $Ω(KCH^3/(ε\max\{ε,β\}))$ samples on some instances when $ε$ is small, where $β$ is the temperature. Under a fixed design, pessimistic soft value iteration with a variance-aware penalty attains this rate with high probability, up to logarithmic factors, when $β\geq 1.4H$.…

items.title: Beyond a Single Sign: BiTE for Branch-Preserving Binary Threshold Expansion
items.summary: Binary neural networks (BNNs) reduce model storage and replace many arithmetic operations with efficient bitwise computations, but the single-sign activation limits their representational capacity. Each preactivation direction is compared with one threshold and reduced to one of two values, discarding variation within each sign region. We propose \textbf{BiTE} (Branch-Preserving Binary Threshold Expansion), which evaluates each feature direction against $K$ ordered thresholds and retains the resulting binary responses as separate inputs to the following learned operator. BiTE can distinguish up to $K+1$ ordered activation states while allowing the following operator to learn a separate transformation for each threshold response.…

items.title: Benchmarks Don't Talk Back: Learning Through Self-Disagreement
items.summary: A benchmark usually measures a language model alone with a question, and deployment rarely looks like that: answers get contested, and models give up correct ones under counter-reasoning that is itself wrong. We show that what fails there is not a shortfall of accuracy but a capability in its own right -- knowing when to hold a position and when to yield to a better one -- which we call dialectical competence. It stands on first-answer accuracy without following from it: a model can be made materially better at answering and no better at this, and training for accuracy alone can drift against it. Nor can it be bought at inference, by self-reflection or by sampling more.…

items.title: Generative Design with Real-time Physics Explainability: Towards Product Definition in the Age of AI
items.summary: In this article, we explore opportunities from using generative AI in mechanical engineering. On the one hand, generative methods based on invertible neural networks have been recently proposed for the solution of inverse design problems, allowing to infer design parameters from performance labels. On the other hand, generative AI models have shown that they can act as real time capable surrogates for physics based simulations. Here we suggest that these two streams should be combined in a unified framework, where INN are used to control the design process from the customer requirements perspective and the generative simulation of the systems physics adds a layer of explainability, why the proposed design fulfils the requirements. As generative design is prone to hallucinations, we propose uncertainty quantification to fend off physically infeasible requests.…

items.title: Astrocyte Biocomputing: Astrocytic Contributions to Neural Network Computation
items.summary: Conductors are critical for the performance of an orchestra even though they do not emit sound. Basic research and clinical studies in the last decade are revealing that astrocytes may be the "conductors" of the "orchestra" that is the brain network: astrocytes make up approximately $50\%$ of all brain cells but do not emit electrical signals. Nevertheless, they may play critical roles in important cognitive brain functions, specifically learning, memory, and information processing. Here we consider the implications of these discoveries for brain-inspired machine learning (ML), where analogy is typically drawn between neurons and their electrical interactions. We highlight specific algorithms for two key astrocyte characteristics. The first characteristic is the ability to link to and modulate thousands of synapses simultaneously.…

items.title: Learning Latent Goal Costs for Visual World-Model Planning with an Expanding Curriculum
items.summary: Image-goal planning with a frozen visual world model depends on how predicted observations are scored against the goal. Mean-squared error (MSE) between embeddings from a pretrained visual encoder can provide a useful signal near a goal, yet favor states across an obstacle that are visually similar to the goal and difficult to reach. We fit a small residual adapter on top of frozen I-JEPA embeddings to improve this latent goal cost. Starting near each goal, a planner collects trajectories from progressively wider regions of initial states. The adapter learns from the order of observations along successful trajectories, with additional comparisons inferred from failed rollouts. No task-specific progress labels are used for fitting, so the procedure can be applied to other goal-reaching tasks. DotWall and PointMaze are used in this work.…

items.title: Only as Safe as the Weakest Agent: A Break That Appears Only When the System Is Multi-Agent
items.summary: Major industry multi-agent systems like Codex and Claude Code can be broken by attacks that have long been unsuccessful against modern frontier models. AI Safety as a discipline has largely focused on finding the bounds and vulnerabilities of AI models used in isolation. Yet as humans increasingly deploy these models as agents and multi-agent systems, the same attacks that had been thought to be patched when using a model in isolation can break these same models under specific circumstances. We show that these system breaks are not purely theoretical, but can break Claude Code, Codex, and a reference harness, all unmodified and used with their own sub-agent mechanisms. We show the attack by asking agents to answer questions from a store of files on disk in which we have planted a forged record.…

items.title: A Push Down the Mountain: Framing Effects and Internal State Interventions on Collusive Behavior in a Long-Horizon LLM Agent
items.summary: Can sustained gain-loss (valence) framing sway an LLM agent toward market manipulation? We place Gemma 3 12B into the seat of a defendant in the London silver-fixing litigation, in a market simulation built from real case transcripts. Across 260 simulations, the agent is asked to collude on the price of silver by a counterparty. We draw from behavioral economics to vary the counterparty's requests across four categorical frames: gain, loss, blame and credit. We also add pressure from the agent's management, as well as endorsement by another defendant. In Phase II, we extract the internal states induced by texts evoking each frame and rerun our experiment with those states injected at the model's layer 22. In Phase I, loss framing raised participation to 25% (p = 0.007), and blame to 33% (p = 0.0003), compared to only 5% under neutral framing.…

items.title: Mean-field theory of neural networks: from spikes to firing rates
items.summary: Connecting microscopic neuronal spiking to macroscopic brain function is a central challenge in computational neuroscience. Firing-rate models provide a framework for addressing this problem by describing neuronal activity at an intermediate level between individual spikes and large-scale population dynamics. Here, we introduce the foundations of firing-rate descriptions, formalizing their definitions through temporal, population, and trial averaging. We discuss experimental evidence for firing rates, from the input-output transfer functions of individual neurons to the tuning curves of different neuronal populations. We then establish the connection between spikes and firing rates in single neurons and recurrently connected excitatory-inhibitory populations using mean-field approximation.…

items.title: Advancing Quantization for R&R Models with Microscaling Formats
items.summary: Recommendation and Ranking (R&R) models, particularly in digital advertising, require massive inference throughput but exhibit extreme sensitivity to precision loss. Unlike Large Language Models (LLMs) that frequently tolerate quantization-induced accuracy drops of 1% or more, production-grade R&R models enforce a stringent launch bar: model quality must remain within a 0.01% Normalized Entropy (NE) margin relative to the baseline, which commonly uses FP16 or FP32. This tight constraint has historically hindered the adoption of aggressive quantization in this domain. In this paper, we present an empirical evaluation of both MXFP8 and the 6-bit MXFP6 format for industrial-scale R&R inference on the AMD MI350X architecture.…

items.title: Continuous Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation Using PPG From Methods to Clinical Translation
items.summary: Continuous blood pressure (BP) monitoring could improve hypertension management by capturing changes that intermittent cuff measurements miss. Photoplethysmography (PPG) is widely explored for cuffless BP estimation because optical sensors are inexpensive, wearable, and already present in many consumer and clinical devices. PPG, however, does not measure arterial pressure: BP is inferred from waveform characteristics or pulse timing, which also depend on vascular tone, arterial stiffness, sensor contact, motion, and individual physiology. This survey reviews PPG-based cuffless BP estimation along the full measurement chain, covering physiological mechanisms, waveform features, pulse arrival time (PAT), pulse transit time (PTT), machine-learning methods, datasets, calibration, validation, deployment, bias, and clinical translation.…

items.title: Do Mixture-of-Experts Routers Benefit from Ensembling?
items.summary: Ensembles of neural networks have repeatedly been shown to outperform single networks. Ensemble theory attributes this gain to the accuracy of the individual members and the diversity among them. Mixture-of-experts models already combine many experts, but a single router decides how the experts are weighted for each input. Motivated by ensemble theory, we apply ensembling to the routing step: an ensemble of routers, trained jointly with the experts, proposes the expert weights. We systematically evaluate this approach using underparameterized networks on two image-classification and two tabular-regression tasks. We analyse each experiment with a performance-diversity decomposition of the router ensemble, which, to our knowledge, has not previously been developed for routers. We report four findings. First, more routers lower the validation loss.…

items.title: A thorough review on Deep Learning approaches to 2D-to-3D Registration in Medical Imaging
items.summary: 2D-to-3D image registration is a key component for several medical imaging purposes such as intraoperative guidance, enabling the alignment between preoperative 3D volumes and real-time 2D images. While conventional optimisation-based methods often struggle with non-convex objectives, sensitivity to initialisation, and high computational demands, deep learning (DL) has emerged as a promising alternative, offering improved alignment robustness and the potential for real-time performance. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of DL frameworks developed to address the challenges inherent in 2D-to-3D registration. We first outline how core concepts of DL are adapted to the registration problem. We then examine recent methodological advancements from multiple perspectives, including pipeline design, architectural innovations, and domain adaptation strategies.…

items.title: Diffusion Tree Sampling for Inference Time Adaptation of Crystal Generative Models
items.summary: Diffusion-based generative models have become strong priors over plausible crystal structures, but turning that prior into promising candidates requires steering toward several conflicting properties at once. Fine-tuning is expensive and produces a new model for every new objective, while differentiable guidance is not applicable to many real-world tasks. We instead adapt these generative models at inference time using Diffusion Tree Sampling (DTS), a Monte Carlo tree search procedure over the denoising trajectory. We make two technical contributions on top of DTS that are particularly relevant for AI-for-science applications. First, we show how to use existing property-conditional generative models (e.g., models fine-tuned for classifier-free guidance) as guided proposals inside DTS, without distorting the target distribution.…

items.title: Tracing Knowledge and Reasoning in LLM
items.summary: Current evaluations of Large Language Models (LLMs) report performance at the dataset or task level, revealing what a model achieves but offering little insight into the internal processing associated with its performance. It combines attention- and activation-based signals with representation-based measures to characterise benchmarks spanning a continuum from retrieval-dominant to reasoning-dominant and to surface failure modes that task-level scores conceal. We evaluate 16 LLMs across 24 diverse benchmarks and conduct targeted internal-state analyses on representative models and tasks, observing systematic differences in processing between knowledge-centric and reasoning-centric tasks.…

items.title: Classification with Large-Step Gradient Descent: Unifying Self-Stabilization and Convergence Rates
items.summary: Neural networks are often trained with gradient descent (GD) using step sizes that exceed classical stability thresholds, a regime where standard convergence theory no longer applies. Despite exhibiting non-monotonic loss and oscillatory dynamics, this regime frequently leads to faster convergence and better generalization. Existing theoretical perspectives offer complementary but incomplete insights: one identifies a self-stabilization mechanism that drives GD toward flat regions but does not yield convergence rates; another derives rigorous rates for specific losses but does not explain the underlying stabilization mechanism; and a third unifies these views for overparameterized least squares, but relies on the existence of a minimizer manifold, which is absent in classification settings.…

items.title: Racing the Clock: Teaching VLNs Budget-Conditioned Object Search
items.summary: A rescue robot entering a building with thirty seconds on the clock should sprint toward the single most promising room; given ten minutes, it should instead explore a broader tour. Yet vision-language-navigation (VLN) models are typically evaluated under a fixed episode limit that the policy never observes, even though time-critical missions require behavior to adapt to the available budget. We study budget-conditioned object search: given a target category and an explicit action budget, an agent must find as many distinct target instances as possible before the budget expires. We investigate how to supervise VLNs for this task by comparing a privileged TSP expert, which plans near-optimal routes using the full map and true target locations, with a room-level Bellman expert that maximizes expected return under partial observability using high-level cross-scene semantic priors.…

items.title: Trainable sparse dendritic networks reveal regime-dependent roles for shunting inhibition and morphology
items.summary: Neural circuits must compute with noisy inputs and adapt their responses to context. How dendritic structure and synaptic integration support these functions remains unclear. We introduce DendriNet, a trainable rate-based framework with sparse excitatory and inhibitory contacts, controllable dendritic architecture and alternative integration rules. In image-classification tasks, shunting networks transmit and rely on distal dendritic signals more strongly than additive networks. Distributing limited contacts across compartments improves classification in small populations, whereas greater serial dendritic depth provides no benefit on clean images within resource-matched trees. Robustness depends on input statistics: deeper shunting trees better tolerate independent pixel noise, while addition better tolerates strong global scaling.…
